about: x86 instructions (x86-64 and i386) as LLVM prints them, each with a description written for this project. Forms, encodings and extensions come from the X86 target of LLVM (tools/x86-index.mjs); the links lead to the HTML edition of Intel's manual.

aaa.description: Corrects AL after adding two unpacked BCD digits: if the low nibble exceeds 9 or AF is set, adds 6 to AL and 1 to AH and sets AF and CF; the high nibble of AL is then cleared. Not valid in 64-bit mode.
aaa.operation: if ((al & 0xF) > 9 || AF) { ax += 0x106; AF = CF = 1 } else AF = CF = 0; al &= 0xF

aad.description: Turns two unpacked BCD digits in AH:AL into a binary value in AL before a division: AL = AH × imm8 + AL, AH = 0. The base is normally 10; other bases come from the immediate. Not valid in 64-bit mode.

aadd.description: Atomically adds a register to a 32- or 64-bit memory location without returning the old value. The operation may be carried out near memory instead of in the core's cache and is weakly ordered, which suits shared counters and statistics.

aam.description: Splits AL into two unpacked BCD digits after multiplying them: AH = AL / imm8 and AL = AL mod imm8 (base 10 by default). An immediate of zero raises a divide error. Not valid in 64-bit mode.
aam.operation: ah = al / imm8; al = al % imm8

aand.description: Atomically ANDs a register into a 32- or 64-bit memory location without returning the old value. Part of RAO-INT: the operation may run near memory and is weakly ordered, so it suits clearing shared flag bits.

aas.description: Corrects AL after subtracting unpacked BCD digits: if the low nibble exceeds 9 or AF is set, subtracts 6 from AL and 1 from AH and sets AF and CF; the high nibble of AL is then cleared. Not valid in 64-bit mode.
aas.operation: if ((al & 0xF) > 9 || AF) { al -= 6; ah -= 1; AF = CF = 1 } else AF = CF = 0; al &= 0xF

adc.description: Adds the source and the carry flag to the destination and sets all arithmetic flags. A chain of add followed by adc implements additions wider than a register, such as 128-bit integers. APX adds a three-operand form with a separate destination.

adcx.description: Adds the source and CF to the destination register and updates only CF, leaving the other flags alone. Paired with adox it lets two independent carry chains run interleaved, as in big-number multiplication. APX adds a form with a separate destination.
adcx.operation: dst = dst + src + CF; CF = carry out

add.description: Adds the source to the destination and sets OF, SF, ZF, AF, CF and PF from the result. Works on 8-, 16-, 32- and 64-bit operands; a 32-bit register destination clears the upper half of the 64-bit register. APX adds three-operand and flag-free {nf} forms.

addpd.description: Adds the two double-precision values of the source to the matching values of the destination xmm register. The VEX form vaddpd writes a separate destination; EVEX adds masking, broadcast and rounding control.

addps.description: Adds the four single-precision values of the source to the matching values of the destination xmm register. Compilers emit it for vectorised float loops; vaddps is the VEX/EVEX form with a separate destination.

addr16.description: The 67h prefix printed on its own line: in 32-bit code it makes the following instruction form 16-bit addresses. LLVM prints it separately when it cannot fold it into the next instruction's operands.

addr32.description: The 67h prefix printed on its own line: in 64-bit code it makes the following instruction compute 32-bit addresses. Linkers also use it as padding, for example addr32 call after relaxing a TLS or GOT call.

addsd.description: Adds the low double of the source to the low double of the destination; the upper 64 bits of the destination stay unchanged. This is how compilers add double variables with SSE2.

addss.description: Adds the low float of the source to the low float of the destination; bits 127:32 of the destination stay unchanged. This is how compilers add float variables with SSE.

addsubpd.description: Subtracts in the low lane and adds in the high lane: dst[0] − src[0] and dst[1] + src[1]. Useful for complex-number multiplication.
addsubpd.operation: dst[0] = dst[0] - src[0]; dst[1] = dst[1] + src[1]

addsubps.description: Subtracts in the even lanes (0 and 2) and adds in the odd lanes (1 and 3) of four floats. Useful for complex-number multiplication.
addsubps.operation: dst[i] = i even ? dst[i] - src[i] : dst[i] + src[i], i = 0..3

adox.description: Adds the source and OF to the destination register, using OF as the carry in and out and leaving every other flag unchanged. Runs alongside adcx to keep two carry chains in flight, as in multi-precision multiplication.
adox.operation: dst = dst + src + OF; OF = carry out

aesdec.description: Performs one round of the AES inverse cipher on the 128-bit state in the destination: inverse ShiftRows, inverse SubBytes and inverse MixColumns, then XOR with the round key from the source. Round keys are prepared with aesimc.

aesdec128kl.summary: AES-128 decrypt with Key Locker handle
aesdec128kl.description: Decrypts the 128-bit block in the xmm register with all AES-128 rounds, using the key wrapped in the 384-bit handle at the memory operand. An invalid or disallowed handle sets ZF and leaves the block unchanged; success clears ZF.
aesdec128kl.operation: if (handle ok) { dst = AES128Decrypt(dst, unwrap([m])); ZF = 0 } else ZF = 1

aesdec256kl.summary: AES-256 decrypt with Key Locker handle
aesdec256kl.description: Decrypts the 128-bit block in the xmm register with all AES-256 rounds, using the key wrapped in the 512-bit handle at the memory operand. An invalid or disallowed handle sets ZF and leaves the block unchanged; success clears ZF.
aesdec256kl.operation: if (handle ok) { dst = AES256Decrypt(dst, unwrap([m])); ZF = 0 } else ZF = 1

aesdeclast.description: Performs the final round of the AES inverse cipher: inverse ShiftRows and inverse SubBytes, then XOR with the round key from the source. Unlike aesdec it skips InvMixColumns.

aesdecwide128kl.summary: AES-128 decrypt eight blocks with Key Locker
aesdecwide128kl.description: Decrypts the eight 128-bit blocks in xmm0–xmm7 in place with AES-128, using the key wrapped in the 384-bit handle at the memory operand. An invalid handle sets ZF and leaves the registers unchanged.
aesdecwide128kl.operation: if (handle ok) for i in 0..7: xmm[i] = AES128Decrypt(xmm[i], unwrap([m]))

aesdecwide256kl.summary: AES-256 decrypt eight blocks with Key Locker
aesdecwide256kl.description: Decrypts the eight 128-bit blocks in xmm0–xmm7 in place with AES-256, using the key wrapped in the 512-bit handle at the memory operand. An invalid handle sets ZF and leaves the registers unchanged.
aesdecwide256kl.operation: if (handle ok) for i in 0..7: xmm[i] = AES256Decrypt(xmm[i], unwrap([m]))

aesenc.description: Performs one middle round of AES encryption on the 128-bit state in the destination: ShiftRows, SubBytes and MixColumns, then XOR with the round key from the source. The last round uses aesenclast.

aesenc128kl.summary: AES-128 encrypt with Key Locker handle
aesenc128kl.description: Encrypts the 128-bit block in the xmm register with all AES-128 rounds, using the key wrapped in the 384-bit handle at the memory operand. An invalid or disallowed handle sets ZF and leaves the block unchanged; success clears ZF.
aesenc128kl.operation: if (handle ok) { dst = AES128Encrypt(dst, unwrap([m])); ZF = 0 } else ZF = 1

aesenc256kl.summary: AES-256 encrypt with Key Locker handle
aesenc256kl.description: Encrypts the 128-bit block in the xmm register with all AES-256 rounds, using the key wrapped in the 512-bit handle at the memory operand. An invalid or disallowed handle sets ZF and leaves the block unchanged; success clears ZF.
aesenc256kl.operation: if (handle ok) { dst = AES256Encrypt(dst, unwrap([m])); ZF = 0 } else ZF = 1

aesenclast.description: Performs the final round of AES encryption: ShiftRows and SubBytes, then XOR with the round key from the source. Unlike aesenc it skips MixColumns.

aesencwide128kl.summary: AES-128 encrypt eight blocks with Key Locker
aesencwide128kl.description: Encrypts the eight 128-bit blocks in xmm0–xmm7 in place with AES-128, using the key wrapped in the 384-bit handle at the memory operand. An invalid handle sets ZF and leaves the registers unchanged.
aesencwide128kl.operation: if (handle ok) for i in 0..7: xmm[i] = AES128Encrypt(xmm[i], unwrap([m]))

aesencwide256kl.summary: AES-256 encrypt eight blocks with Key Locker
aesencwide256kl.description: Encrypts the eight 128-bit blocks in xmm0–xmm7 in place with AES-256, using the key wrapped in the 512-bit handle at the memory operand. An invalid handle sets ZF and leaves the registers unchanged.
aesencwide256kl.operation: if (handle ok) for i in 0..7: xmm[i] = AES256Encrypt(xmm[i], unwrap([m]))

aesimc.description: Applies InvMixColumns to the 128-bit round key in the source and writes the result to the destination. Converts encryption round keys into the form aesdec needs for the equivalent inverse cipher.

aeskeygenassist.description: Helps expand AES keys: takes doublewords 1 and 3 of the source and writes each one after SubWord, and again after SubWord, RotWord and XOR with the round constant imm8. Shuffles and XORs then turn this into the next round key.
aeskeygenassist.operation: dst = {SubWord(s[1]), RotWord(SubWord(s[1])) ^ imm8, SubWord(s[3]), RotWord(SubWord(s[3])) ^ imm8}

and.description: ANDs the source into the destination, clears OF and CF and sets SF, ZF and PF from the result. Used to mask bits and align pointers, as in and rsp, -16. APX adds three-operand and flag-free {nf} forms.

andn.description: Writes the AND of the inverted first source with the second source into a separate destination. Sets SF and ZF and clears OF and CF. Saves a separate not when clearing bits selected by a mask.

andnpd.description: Inverts the destination and ANDs it with the source across all 128 bits. Compilers combine it with andpd and orpd to select between two vectors by a comparison mask.

andnps.description: Inverts the destination and ANDs it with the source across all 128 bits. Combined with andps and orps it selects between two vectors by a comparison mask.

andpd.description: Bitwise AND of the 128-bit destination and source. With a mask that clears the sign bits it computes fabs; with a comparison mask it keeps only the selected lanes.

andps.description: Bitwise AND of the 128-bit destination and source. Compilers often pick it for any 128-bit AND because its encoding is a byte shorter than andpd or pand; with a sign-clearing mask it computes fabsf.

aor.description: Atomically ORs a register into a 32- or 64-bit memory location without returning the old value. Part of RAO-INT: the operation may run near memory and is weakly ordered, so it suits setting shared flag bits.

arpl.description: If the RPL field (bits 1:0) of the destination selector is lower than that of the source selector, raises it to match and sets ZF; otherwise clears ZF. Used by protected-mode systems; in 64-bit mode opcode 63 is movsxd instead.
arpl.operation: if (dst.rpl < src.rpl) { dst.rpl = src.rpl; ZF = 1 } else ZF = 0

axor.description: Atomically XORs a register into a 32- or 64-bit memory location without returning the old value. Part of RAO-INT: the operation may run near memory and is weakly ordered, so it suits toggling shared bits.

bextr.description: Extracts a field from the source: the start bit comes from bits 7:0 of the control and the length from bits 15:8, and the field is zero-extended into the destination. BMI takes the control from a register; the AMD TBM form takes a 32-bit immediate.

blcfill.description: Clears the trailing one bits of the source, that is every bit below its lowest clear bit, and writes the result to the destination. An AMD TBM instruction that sets the flags from the result.

blci.description: Writes a value with every bit set except the position of the lowest clear bit of the source. An AMD TBM instruction that sets the flags from the result.

blcic.description: Writes a value with only one bit set: the position of the lowest clear bit of the source. An AMD TBM instruction that sets the flags from the result.

blcmsk.summary: Mask up to lowest clear bit
blcmsk.description: Writes a mask with the lowest clear bit of the source and every bit below it set, and the rest cleared. An AMD TBM instruction that sets the flags from the result.

blcs.description: Copies the source to the destination with its lowest clear bit set. An AMD TBM instruction that sets the flags from the result.

blendpd.description: Picks each of the two doubles from the source or keeps the destination's value according to bits 1:0 of imm8: a set bit takes the source lane.

blendps.description: Picks each of the four floats from the source or keeps the destination's value according to bits 3:0 of imm8: a set bit takes the source lane.

blendvpd.description: Takes each double from the source when the sign bit of the matching lane of xmm0 is set and keeps the destination otherwise. xmm0 is an implicit third operand; vblendvpd names its mask register explicitly.

blendvps.description: Takes each float from the source when the sign bit of the matching lane of xmm0 is set and keeps the destination otherwise. xmm0 is an implicit third operand; vblendvps names its mask register explicitly.

blsfill.description: Copies the source with every bit below its lowest set bit also set. A zero source gives all ones. An AMD TBM instruction that sets the flags from the result.

blsi.description: Writes a value holding only the lowest set bit of the source, or zero if the source is zero. A BMI1 instruction; CF is set when the source is not zero, and APX adds a flag-free {nf} form.

blsic.description: Writes a value with every bit set except the position of the lowest set bit of the source. An AMD TBM instruction that sets the flags from the result.

blsmsk.summary: Mask up to lowest set bit
blsmsk.description: Writes a mask with the lowest set bit of the source and every bit below it set. A zero source gives all ones and sets CF. A BMI1 instruction; APX adds a flag-free {nf} form.

blsr.description: Copies the source with its lowest set bit cleared. Loops that visit each set bit of a mask use it; CF is set when the source is zero. A BMI1 instruction; APX adds a flag-free {nf} form.

bound.description: Compares a signed index register with a pair of lower and upper bounds stored in memory and raises a #BR exception if it lies outside them. Exists only outside 64-bit mode, where its opcode 62 became the EVEX prefix.

bsf.description: Writes the index of the lowest set bit of the source and clears ZF. If the source is zero, ZF is set and the destination is officially undefined (left unchanged in practice); tzcnt is the fully defined alternative.
bsf.operation: if (src) { dst = index of lowest set bit; ZF = 0 } else ZF = 1

bsr.description: Writes the index of the highest set bit of the source, which is floor(log2(src)), and clears ZF. If the source is zero, ZF is set and the destination is officially undefined (left unchanged in practice); lzcnt counts from the other end.
bsr.operation: if (src) { dst = index of highest set bit; ZF = 0 } else ZF = 1

bswap.description: Reverses the byte order of a 32- or 64-bit register, converting between little- and big-endian values. The 16-bit form gives an undefined result; rol r16, 8 does that job instead.

bt.description: Copies the selected bit of the destination into CF. With a register offset and a memory operand, the offset is signed and can reach bits outside the addressed word, treating memory as a long bit string.

btc.description: Copies the selected bit of the destination into CF and then inverts that bit. With a register offset, a memory operand is treated as a bit string; with lock the memory form is atomic.

btr.description: Copies the selected bit of the destination into CF and then clears that bit. With a register offset, a memory operand is treated as a bit string; with lock the memory form is atomic.

bts.description: Copies the selected bit of the destination into CF and then sets that bit. With a register offset, a memory operand is treated as a bit string; lock bts is a common atomic test-and-set.

bzhi.description: Copies the source to the destination and clears every bit at or above the index held in bits 7:0 of the third operand. If the index is not less than the operand size, nothing is cleared and CF is set.
bzhi.operation: n = idx[7:0]; dst = n < size ? src & ((1 << n) - 1) : src

call.description: Pushes the address of the next instruction and jumps to the target, given relative to rip (rel32) or indirectly through a register or memory. ret later returns to the pushed address; in 64-bit mode the return address is 8 bytes.

cbw.description: Fills AH with copies of the sign bit of AL, so AX holds the same signed value as AL. Uses the 66h prefix in 32- and 64-bit code; cwde and cdqe are the wider forms.

ccmpcc.description: An APX instruction: if the condition holds on the current flags, compares the operands like cmp and sets the flags; otherwise sets OF, SF, ZF and CF from the default flag value {dfv=}. Chains of ccmp evaluate && and || of comparisons without branches.

cdq.description: Fills EDX with copies of the sign bit of EAX, forming a 64-bit signed value in EDX:EAX. Compilers emit it before idiv for signed 32-bit division.

cdqe.description: Sign-extends the 32-bit value in EAX to all 64 bits of RAX. A short accumulator-only equivalent of movsxd rax, eax.

cfcmovcc.description: An APX conditional move whose memory operand is not touched when the condition is false, so it cannot fault there. The store form writes memory only if the condition holds. Lets compilers turn guarded loads and stores into branch-free code.
cfcmovcc.operation: if (cond) dst = src  // no memory access when false

clac.description: Clears the AC flag, which re-enables supervisor-mode access prevention (SMAP) so kernel code can no longer touch user pages. Kernels pair it with stac around user-memory accesses; privileged.

clc.description: Sets CF to zero without touching the other flags. Used before an adc chain or to return a success status in CF, as some BIOS and firmware interfaces do.

cld.description: Clears DF so string instructions (movs, stos, cmps, scas, lods) step rsi and rdi upward. The ABIs require DF to be clear at calls and returns, so code that sets it with std restores it.

cldemote.description: Hints that the cache line holding the address should move from the core's private caches to a more distant shared level, so other cores reach it faster. Acts as a no-op where unsupported.
cldemote.operation: hint: move line([m]) to shared cache

clflush.description: Writes back the cache line holding the address if it is modified and invalidates it in every cache of the coherence domain. Ordered against stores and other clflush; used for persistent memory and device buffers.

clflushopt.description: Writes back and invalidates the cache line like clflush, but is not ordered against other clflushopt or clwb, so many lines can be flushed faster. An sfence afterwards waits for the flushes to complete.

clgi.description: An AMD SVM instruction that clears the global interrupt flag, holding off interrupts and other events, typically around vmrun in a hypervisor. Privileged.

cli.description: Clears IF so the processor ignores maskable external interrupts until sti. Requires CPL ≤ IOPL; kernels use it around short critical sections.

clrssbsy.description: Clears the busy bit in the supervisor shadow-stack token at the memory operand, marking that shadow stack free after switching away from it. A CET instruction for operating systems; privileged.

clts.description: Clears the TS bit in CR0, so x87, MMX and SSE instructions stop raising device-not-available faults. Used for lazy FPU context switching; privileged.

clui.description: Clears UIF, blocking delivery of user interrupts (UINTR) to the current thread until stui sets it again.

clwb.description: Writes back the cache line holding the address if it is modified, but may keep a clean copy in the cache, unlike clflush. Used with persistent memory to make stores durable; a fence orders it.

clzero.description: An AMD instruction that zeroes the whole 64-byte cache line containing the address in rax (eax in 32-bit code) without reading it first. Used to clear pages quickly.

cmc.description: Inverts CF and leaves the other flags unchanged. Occasionally used in hand-written arithmetic and status returns.

cmovcc.description: Copies the source to the destination if the condition (e, ne, l, ge, b, ae and so on) holds on the flags. A 32-bit destination is zero-extended even when false, and a memory source is read either way. The APX form writes cond ? src2 : src1 to a new register.

cmp.description: Subtracts the source from the destination, discards the result and sets the flags as sub would. A following jcc, setcc or cmovcc tests the relation: l and g for signed values, b and a for unsigned ones.

cmpccxadd.summary: Atomic compare and add if condition
cmpccxadd.description: Atomically reads memory, compares it with the second operand and, if the condition holds, stores memory plus the third operand. The old memory value goes to the second operand and the flags come from the comparison. Always locked.
cmpccxadd.operation: t = [m]; flags = cmp(t, src1); if (cond) [m] = t + src2; src1 = t

cmppd.description: Compares each pair of doubles with the imm8 predicate (eq, lt, le, unord, neq, nlt, nle, ord) and writes all ones for true, zero for false. LLVM folds the predicate into the name, as in cmpltpd; the mask feeds andpd or movmskpd.

cmpps.description: Compares each pair of floats with the imm8 predicate (eq, lt, le, unord, neq, nlt, nle, ord) and writes all ones for true, zero for false. LLVM folds the predicate into the name, as in cmpleps; the mask feeds andps or movmskps.

cmpsb.description: Compares the byte at [rsi] with the byte at [rdi], setting the flags as for [rsi] − [rdi], then moves both pointers by 1 up or down depending on DF. With repe or repne it scans until a difference, a match or rcx reaching zero.
cmpsb.operation: flags = [rsi] - [rdi]; rsi += d; rdi += d  (d = DF ? -1 : 1)

cmpsd.summary: Compare scalar double or string dwords
cmpsd.description: Two instructions share the name. The SSE2 form compares the low doubles with the imm8 predicate and writes an all-ones or zero mask to the low 64 bits (LLVM prints cmpltsd and so on); the string form A7 compares dwords at [rsi] and [rdi] and steps both by 4.
cmpsd.operation: dst[0] = pred(dst[0], src[0]) ? ~0 : 0  |  flags = [rsi] - [rdi]; rsi += 4d; rdi += 4d

cmpsq.description: Compares the quadword at [rsi] with the one at [rdi], setting the flags as for [rsi] − [rdi], then moves both pointers by 8 up or down depending on DF. Usually combined with repe or repne.

cmpss.description: Compares the low floats with the imm8 predicate (eq, lt, le, unord, neq, nlt, nle, ord) and writes an all-ones or zero mask to the low 32 bits, keeping the rest of the destination. LLVM folds the predicate into the name, as in cmpltss.

cmpsw.description: Compares the word at [rsi] with the one at [rdi], setting the flags as for [rsi] − [rdi], then moves both pointers by 2 up or down depending on DF. Usually combined with repe or repne.

cmpxchg.description: Compares the accumulator (al, ax, eax or rax) with the destination; if equal, stores the source there and sets ZF, otherwise loads the destination into the accumulator and clears ZF. With lock it is the basic atomic compare-and-swap.
cmpxchg.operation: if (acc == dst) { dst = src; ZF = 1 } else { acc = dst; ZF = 0 }

cmpxchg16b.description: Compares RDX:RAX with the 16-byte memory operand; if equal, stores RCX:RBX there and sets ZF, otherwise loads memory into RDX:RAX and clears ZF. The operand must be 16-byte aligned; with lock it is a 128-bit atomic compare-and-swap.
cmpxchg16b.operation: if (rdx:rax == [m]) { [m] = rcx:rbx; ZF = 1 } else { rdx:rax = [m]; ZF = 0 }

cmpxchg8b.description: Compares EDX:EAX with the 8-byte memory operand; if equal, stores ECX:EBX there and sets ZF, otherwise loads memory into EDX:EAX and clears ZF. With lock it gives 32-bit code a 64-bit atomic compare-and-swap.
cmpxchg8b.operation: if (edx:eax == [m]) { [m] = ecx:ebx; ZF = 1 } else { edx:eax = [m]; ZF = 0 }

comisd.description: Compares the low doubles and sets ZF, PF and CF as an unsigned compare would (all three for unordered), clearing OF, SF and AF. Signals invalid for any NaN, unlike ucomisd, which does so only for signalling NaNs.

comiss.description: Compares the low floats and sets ZF, PF and CF as an unsigned compare would (all three for unordered), clearing OF, SF and AF. Signals invalid for any NaN, unlike ucomiss, which does so only for signalling NaNs.

cpuid.description: Returns processor information chosen by EAX (leaf) and ECX (subleaf) in EAX, EBX, ECX and EDX: vendor, model, feature bits, caches and topology. Also serialises execution. Programs use it to choose code paths for the available extensions.
cpuid.operation: eax, ebx, ecx, edx = cpu_info(eax, ecx)

cqo.description: Fills RDX with copies of the sign bit of RAX, forming a 128-bit signed value in RDX:RAX. Compilers emit it before idiv for signed 64-bit division.

crc32.description: Updates the CRC in the destination with 8, 16, 32 or 64 bits of the source, using the Castagnoli polynomial (CRC-32C, as in iSCSI and ext4), not the zlib CRC-32. The 64-bit form keeps the CRC in the low 32 bits of a 64-bit register.

cs.description: The 2Eh prefix printed on its own line. It selects the CS segment for a memory operand; in 64-bit code that has no effect, so it appears as padding (cs nop) or, before a jcc, as an old not-taken branch hint.

ctestcc.description: An APX instruction: if the condition holds on the current flags, ANDs the operands like test and sets the flags; otherwise sets OF, SF, ZF and CF from the default flag value {dfv=}. Lets compilers combine conditions without branches.

cvtdq2pd.description: Converts the two signed 32-bit integers in the low 64 bits of the source to two doubles. The conversion is exact, since every int32 fits in a double.

cvtdq2ps.description: Converts four signed 32-bit integers to four floats, rounding per MXCSR when a value needs more than 24 bits of precision.

cvtpd2dq.description: Converts two doubles to signed 32-bit integers using the MXCSR rounding mode (nearest-even by default) and places them in the low 64 bits, zeroing the upper 64. Out-of-range values and NaN give 0x80000000.

cvtpd2pi.summary: Convert packed double to MMX int32
cvtpd2pi.description: Converts two doubles to signed 32-bit integers in an MMX register, rounding per MXCSR. Out-of-range values give 0x80000000. Switches the x87 unit into MMX state.

cvtpd2ps.description: Converts two doubles to two floats, rounding per MXCSR, in the low 64 bits of the destination; the upper 64 bits are zeroed.

cvtpi2pd.summary: Convert MMX int32 to packed double
cvtpi2pd.description: Converts two signed 32-bit integers from an MMX register or memory to two doubles, exactly. A register source switches the x87 unit into MMX state.

cvtpi2ps.summary: Convert MMX int32 to packed float
cvtpi2ps.description: Converts two signed 32-bit integers from an MMX register or memory to two floats in the low 64 bits of the destination, rounding per MXCSR; the upper two floats stay unchanged.

cvtps2dq.description: Converts four floats to signed 32-bit integers using the MXCSR rounding mode (nearest-even by default). Out-of-range values and NaN give 0x80000000.

cvtps2pd.description: Converts the two floats in the low 64 bits of the source to two doubles. The conversion is exact.

cvtps2pi.summary: Convert packed float to MMX int32
cvtps2pi.description: Converts the two low floats of the source to signed 32-bit integers in an MMX register, rounding per MXCSR. Out-of-range values give 0x80000000. Switches the x87 unit into MMX state.

cvtsd2si.description: Converts the low double to a signed 32- or 64-bit integer in a general register, rounding per MXCSR, like lrint(). Out-of-range values and NaN give the integer indefinite value (only the sign bit set). C casts use cvttsd2si.

cvtsd2ss.description: Converts the low double of the source to a float in the low 32 bits of the destination, rounding per MXCSR; bits 127:32 of the destination stay unchanged.

cvtsi2sd.description: Converts a signed 32- or 64-bit integer from a general register or memory to a double in the low lane; 64-bit values may round. The upper 64 bits stay unchanged, a false dependency compilers break by zeroing the register first.

cvtsi2ss.description: Converts a signed 32- or 64-bit integer from a general register or memory to a float in the low lane, rounding per MXCSR. Bits 127:32 stay unchanged, a false dependency compilers break by zeroing the register first.

cvtss2sd.description: Converts the low float of the source to a double in the low 64 bits of the destination, exactly; the upper 64 bits stay unchanged.

cvtss2si.description: Converts the low float to a signed 32- or 64-bit integer in a general register, rounding per MXCSR, like lrintf(). Out-of-range values and NaN give the integer indefinite value (only the sign bit set).

cvttpd2dq.summary: Convert packed double to int32, truncating
cvttpd2dq.description: Converts two doubles to signed 32-bit integers, rounding toward zero as a C cast does, into the low 64 bits; the upper 64 bits are zeroed. Out-of-range values and NaN give 0x80000000.

cvttpd2pi.summary: Convert packed double to MMX int32, truncating
cvttpd2pi.description: Converts two doubles to signed 32-bit integers in an MMX register, rounding toward zero. Out-of-range values give 0x80000000. Switches the x87 unit into MMX state.

cvttps2dq.summary: Convert packed float to int32, truncating
cvttps2dq.description: Converts four floats to signed 32-bit integers, rounding toward zero as a C cast does. Out-of-range values and NaN give 0x80000000. Compilers emit it for vectorised float-to-int casts.

cvttps2pi.summary: Convert packed float to MMX int32, truncating
cvttps2pi.description: Converts the two low floats of the source to signed 32-bit integers in an MMX register, rounding toward zero. Out-of-range values give 0x80000000. Switches the x87 unit into MMX state.

cvttsd2si.summary: Convert scalar double to integer, truncating
cvttsd2si.description: Converts the low double to a signed 32- or 64-bit integer in a general register, rounding toward zero as a C cast does. Out-of-range values and NaN give the integer indefinite value (only the sign bit set).

cvttss2si.summary: Convert scalar float to integer, truncating
cvttss2si.description: Converts the low float to a signed 32- or 64-bit integer in a general register, rounding toward zero as a C cast does. Out-of-range values and NaN give the integer indefinite value (only the sign bit set).

cwd.description: Fills DX with copies of the sign bit of AX, forming a 32-bit signed value in DX:AX. Used before idiv for signed 16-bit division.

cwde.description: Sign-extends the 16-bit value in AX to all 32 bits of EAX; in 64-bit mode the upper half of RAX is cleared as for any 32-bit write.

daa.description: Adjusts AL after adding two packed BCD bytes so that it again holds two valid decimal digits, setting CF and AF for the decimal carries. Not valid in 64-bit mode.
daa.operation: if ((al & 0xF) > 9 || AF) al += 6; if (old_al > 0x99 || old_CF) { al += 0x60; CF = 1 }

das.description: Adjusts AL after subtracting two packed BCD bytes so that it again holds two valid decimal digits, setting CF and AF for the decimal borrows. Not valid in 64-bit mode.
das.operation: if ((al & 0xF) > 9 || AF) al -= 6; if (old_al > 0x99 || old_CF) { al -= 0x60; CF = 1 }

data16.description: The 66h prefix printed on its own line, usually because it means nothing to the next instruction. Toolchains repeat it as padding to reach a needed length, as in data16 cs nopw and the TLS sequence data16 lea / data16 data16 rex64 call.

dec.description: Subtracts 1 from the destination and sets OF, SF, ZF, AF and PF, leaving CF unchanged. The one-byte 48+r form exists only outside 64-bit mode, where those bytes are REX prefixes. APX adds new-destination and {nf} forms.

div.description: Divides RDX:RAX (or EDX:EAX, DX:AX, AX) by the unsigned source, putting the quotient in RAX and the remainder in RDX (AL and AH for bytes). Zero divisors and quotients that do not fit raise #DE; flags are undefined. Compilers zero edx first.
div.operation: rax = rdx:rax / src; rdx = rdx:rax % src

divpd.description: Divides each of the two doubles of the destination by the matching double of the source, rounding per MXCSR. vdivpd is the VEX/EVEX form with a separate destination.

divps.description: Divides each of the four floats of the destination by the matching float of the source, rounding per MXCSR. vdivps is the VEX/EVEX form with a separate destination.

divsd.description: Divides the low double of the destination by the low double of the source; the upper 64 bits of the destination stay unchanged. This is how compilers divide double variables with SSE2.

divss.description: Divides the low float of the destination by the low float of the source; bits 127:32 of the destination stay unchanged. This is how compilers divide float variables with SSE.

dppd.description: Multiplies the doubles lane by lane, adds the products whose bits are set in imm8[5:4], and writes the sum to the lanes selected by imm8[1:0], zeroing the others.
dppd.operation: s = Σ imm8[4+i] ? dst[i] * src[i] : 0; dst[j] = imm8[j] ? s : 0

dpps.description: Multiplies the four floats lane by lane, adds the products whose bits are set in imm8[7:4], and writes the sum to the lanes selected by imm8[3:0], zeroing the others. vdpps on ymm works on each 128-bit half separately.
dpps.operation: s = Σ imm8[4+i] ? dst[i] * src[i] : 0; dst[j] = imm8[j] ? s : 0

ds.description: The 3Eh prefix printed on its own line. DS is already the default segment for most operands, so in 64-bit code it acts as padding or, before a jcc, as an old taken-branch hint. Before an indirect call or jmp LLVM prints it as notrack.

emms.description: Marks all x87 registers empty after MMX code, so later x87 floating-point code finds a clean register stack. Needed wherever MMX and x87 code share a program.

encls.description: Runs the Intel SGX supervisor leaf selected by EAX, such as creating an enclave or adding and measuring its pages, with operands in RBX, RCX and RDX. Privileged; used by the operating system's SGX driver.

enclu.description: Runs the Intel SGX user leaf selected by EAX, such as EENTER and EEXIT to enter and leave an enclave, or EREPORT and EGETKEY for attestation and sealing keys. Used by enclave runtimes in user mode.

enclv.description: Runs the Intel SGX virtualization leaf selected by EAX, which lets a hypervisor manage enclave pages of its guests, for example when overcommitting the enclave page cache. Privileged.

encodekey128.summary: Wrap AES-128 key into Key Locker handle
encodekey128.description: Wraps the AES-128 key in xmm0 with the processor's internal wrapping key and writes a 384-bit handle to xmm0–xmm2, with the restrictions taken from the source register. The destination gets handle information; xmm4–xmm6 and the flags are cleared.
encodekey128.operation: xmm0..2 = wrap(xmm0, src); dst = info; xmm4..6 = 0

encodekey256.summary: Wrap AES-256 key into Key Locker handle
encodekey256.description: Wraps the AES-256 key in xmm0:xmm1 with the processor's internal wrapping key and writes a 512-bit handle to xmm0–xmm3, with the restrictions taken from the source register. The destination gets handle information; xmm4–xmm6 and the flags are cleared.
encodekey256.operation: xmm0..3 = wrap(xmm1:xmm0, src); dst = info; xmm4..6 = 0

endbr32.description: Marks a valid target of an indirect call or jump in 32-bit code under Intel CET indirect branch tracking. Runs as a no-op on processors without CET or with tracking off.

endbr64.description: Marks a valid target of an indirect call or jump in 64-bit code under Intel CET indirect branch tracking. Compilers put it at function entries with -fcf-protection; it runs as a no-op elsewhere.

enqcmd.description: Sends a 64-byte command read from memory to the device work-queue address in the destination register as one non-posted write, tagged with the process's PASID. ZF is clear if the device accepted it and set if it asks to retry.

enqcmds.description: The kernel-mode form of enqcmd: sends a 64-byte command to a device work queue, taking the PASID and privilege from the command itself. ZF reports whether the device accepted it. Privileged.

enter.description: Builds a stack frame: pushes rbp, points rbp at the saved value and reserves imm16 bytes for locals; a nonzero imm8 also copies outer frame pointers for nested procedures. Slow, so compilers rarely use it; leave undoes it.
enter.operation: push rbp; rbp = rsp; rsp -= imm16

erets.description: Part of Intel FRED: returns from an event handler to supervisor level using the return frame on the stack, restoring rip, rflags, rsp and the stack level. Privileged.
erets.operation: rip, rflags, rsp = pop FRED frame  // stay in ring 0

eretu.summary: Return from event to user mode
eretu.description: Part of Intel FRED: returns from an event handler to user mode using the return frame on the stack, restoring rip, rflags, rsp, cs and ss. Replaces iret for this path on FRED systems; privileged.
eretu.operation: rip, cs, rflags, rsp, ss = pop FRED frame  // to ring 3

es.description: The 26h prefix printed on its own line. It selects the ES segment for a memory operand in 16- and 32-bit code; in 64-bit code it has no effect and only pads the instruction.

extractps.description: Copies the 32-bit float lane selected by imm8[1:0] from the xmm source, as raw bits, into a general register or memory. A 64-bit register destination is zero-extended.

extrq.description: AMD SSE4A: extracts a field from the low 64 bits of the destination, with the length and starting bit given by two immediates or by bits 5:0 and 13:8 of a second xmm register. The field is zero-extended; the upper quadword is undefined.

f2xm1.description: Replaces ST(0) with 2^ST(0) − 1; the input must lie between −1 and +1. Together with fscale and fyl2x it implements general powers and exponentials.

fabs.description: Clears the sign bit of ST(0), replacing it with its absolute value. Works for infinities and NaNs too, without raising exceptions.

fadd.description: Adds a float or double from memory to ST(0), or adds two stack registers with the result in ST(0) or ST(i). The sum is rounded to the precision set in the x87 control word.

faddp.description: Adds ST(0) to ST(i), stores the sum in ST(i) and pops the stack, so the result moves one position closer to the top. faddp st(1), st is the usual form.

fbld.description: Converts an 80-bit packed decimal integer (18 digits and a sign) from memory to extended precision and pushes it onto the x87 stack.

fbstp.description: Rounds ST(0) to an integer according to the control word, stores it as an 80-bit packed decimal value and pops the stack. Values that do not fit 18 digits store the indefinite pattern.

fchs.description: Inverts the sign bit of ST(0), turning x into −x. Works for zeros, infinities and NaNs as well.

fcmovb.description: Copies ST(i) into ST(0) if CF is set. The flags usually come from fcomi or ucomisd, where below means less than.

fcmovbe.summary: x87 move if below or equal
fcmovbe.description: Copies ST(i) into ST(0) if CF or ZF is set. After fcomi this means less than or equal, and also unordered.

fcmove.description: Copies ST(i) into ST(0) if ZF is set. After fcomi this means equal or unordered.

fcmovnb.description: Copies ST(i) into ST(0) if CF is clear. After fcomi this means greater than or equal.

fcmovnbe.summary: x87 move if not below or equal
fcmovnbe.description: Copies ST(i) into ST(0) if both CF and ZF are clear. After fcomi this means strictly greater than.

fcmovne.description: Copies ST(i) into ST(0) if ZF is clear. After fcomi this means the values are ordered and differ.

fcmovnu.description: Copies ST(i) into ST(0) if PF is clear. After fcomi this means neither operand was a NaN.

fcmovu.description: Copies ST(i) into ST(0) if PF is set. After fcomi this means at least one operand was a NaN.

fcom.description: Compares ST(0) with ST(i) or a float or double in memory and records the result in condition codes C3, C2 and C0 of the status word (all three for unordered). Code reads them with fnstsw ax and sahf; fcomi sets EFLAGS directly.

fcomi.description: Compares ST(0) with ST(i) and sets ZF, PF and CF directly, as an unsigned compare would; unordered sets all three. Raises invalid for any NaN operand; fucomi does so only for signalling NaNs.

fcomp.description: Compares ST(0) with ST(i) or a float or double in memory, sets C3, C2 and C0 in the status word as fcom does, and then pops the stack.
fcomp.operation: C3, C2, C0 = compare(st0, src); pop

fcompi.summary: x87 compare, set EFLAGS and pop
fcompi.description: Compares ST(0) with ST(i), sets ZF, PF and CF as fcomi does, and then pops the stack. Also known as fcomip.
fcompi.operation: ZF, PF, CF = compare(st0, st(i)); pop

fcompp.description: Compares ST(0) with ST(1), sets C3, C2 and C0 in the status word and pops both registers off the stack.
fcompp.operation: C3, C2, C0 = compare(st0, st1); pop; pop

fcos.description: Replaces ST(0) with its cosine, the angle in radians. Inputs beyond ±2^63 leave ST(0) unchanged and set C2; accuracy drops for large arguments because the reduction uses a finite approximation of pi.

fdecstp.description: Decrements the TOP field of the x87 status word, rotating the register stack without moving data or changing any tags.

fdiv.description: Divides ST(0) by a float or double from memory, or one stack register by another; fdiv st(i), st stores ST(i) / ST(0) in ST(i). fdivr divides in the reverse order.

fdivp.description: Divides ST(i) by ST(0), stores the quotient in ST(i) and pops the stack. fdivrp is the form with the operands reversed.

fdivr.description: Divides a source by ST(0) instead of the other way round: with a memory operand ST(0) = m32/m64 / ST(0); in the 'fdivr st(i), st' form ST(i) = ST(0) / ST(i). The reversed form saves an fxch when the operands sit in the wrong order.
fdivr.operation: st0 = src / st0; or st(i) = st0 / st(i)

fdivrp.description: Computes ST(0) / ST(i), stores the quotient in ST(i) and pops the stack, so the result ends up one slot higher. A typical last step of an x87 expression a / b.

femms.description: AMD 3DNow! variant of emms: marks every x87 register empty after MMX or 3DNow! code so the x87 unit can be used again. The MMX register contents are not guaranteed afterwards.

ffree.description: Marks ST(i) empty in the tag word without moving the stack top or changing the value bits. Rare in compiled code; it discards a register without popping.

ffreep.description: Marks ST(i) empty and then pops the register stack. Long undocumented by Intel but supported everywhere; some compilers emit it to drop a value from the x87 stack.

fiadd.description: Converts a signed 16- or 32-bit integer from memory to extended precision and adds it to ST(0).

ficom.description: Compares ST(0) with a signed 16- or 32-bit integer from memory and sets C0, C2 and C3 in the x87 status word. An unordered result (NaN) raises invalid-operation.

ficomp.description: Like ficom: compares ST(0) with a signed 16- or 32-bit integer from memory, sets C0, C2 and C3 in the status word, then pops the stack.

fidiv.description: Divides ST(0) by a signed 16- or 32-bit integer loaded from memory and keeps the quotient in ST(0).

fidivr.description: Divides a signed 16- or 32-bit integer from memory by ST(0) and keeps the quotient in ST(0).

fild.description: Converts a signed 16-, 32- or 64-bit integer from memory to extended precision, always exactly, and pushes it onto the x87 stack. 32-bit code uses it to turn int64 into double.

fimul.description: Multiplies ST(0) by a signed 16- or 32-bit integer loaded from memory and keeps the product in ST(0).

fincstp.description: Adds one to the TOP field of the status word, rotating the register stack. Unlike a pop, the old ST(0) is not marked empty.

fist.description: Converts ST(0) to a signed 16- or 32-bit integer with the current rounding mode (round to nearest by default, not truncation) and stores it. Out-of-range values store the integer indefinite value.

fistp.description: Like fist, but pops the stack afterwards and also has a 64-bit form. Before SSE3, a C cast to int had to wrap it in fldcw pairs to switch to truncation.

fisttp.description: Converts ST(0) to a signed 16-, 32- or 64-bit integer rounding toward zero regardless of the control word, stores it and pops. Added in SSE3 so C casts no longer need fldcw.

fisub.description: Subtracts a signed 16- or 32-bit integer from memory from ST(0) and keeps the difference in ST(0).

fisubr.description: Subtracts ST(0) from a signed 16- or 32-bit integer in memory and keeps the difference in ST(0).

fld.description: Pushes a 32-, 64- or 80-bit floating-point value from memory onto the x87 stack, widening it to extended precision; 'fld st(i)' duplicates a register.

fld1.description: Pushes +1.0 onto the x87 stack without reading memory.

fldcw.description: Loads the 16-bit x87 control word from memory: rounding mode, precision control and exception masks. Older compilers wrapped fistp in two fldcw to get truncating casts.

fldenv.description: Restores the x87 control, status and tag words and the last instruction and operand pointers from a 14- or 28-byte area written by fnstenv. The data registers are not loaded.

fldl2e.description: Pushes log2(e) ≈ 1.4427 onto the x87 stack; together with f2xm1 and fscale it computes e^x.

fldl2t.description: Pushes log2(10) ≈ 3.3219 onto the x87 stack, used for powers of ten with f2xm1 and fscale.

fldlg2.description: Pushes log10(2) ≈ 0.30103 onto the x87 stack; followed by fyl2x it gives a decimal logarithm.

fldln2.description: Pushes ln(2) ≈ 0.69315 onto the x87 stack; followed by fyl2x it gives a natural logarithm.

fldpi.description: Pushes pi onto the x87 stack with the full 64-bit significand precision of the extended format.

fldz.description: Pushes +0.0 onto the x87 stack, the quickest way to get a zero without touching memory.

fmul.description: Multiplies ST(0) by a 32- or 64-bit floating-point value from memory, or one x87 register by another, and keeps the product in the destination.

fmulp.description: Multiplies ST(i) by ST(0), stores the product in ST(i) and pops the stack.

fnclex.description: Clears the exception flags, the exception summary and the busy bit in the x87 status word without first checking for pending unmasked exceptions (the 'n' means no wait).

fninit.description: Resets the x87 unit: control word 0x37F (all exceptions masked, round to nearest, 64-bit precision), status cleared, every register tagged empty. Does not wait for pending exceptions.

fnop.description: Does nothing except advance the instruction pointer, though it does update the x87 last-instruction pointer.

fnsave.description: Stores the x87 environment and all eight data registers to a 94- or 108-byte area, then reinitializes the unit as fninit does. Superseded by fxsave and xsave.

fnstcw.description: Stores the 16-bit x87 control word to memory without checking pending exceptions; usually paired with fldcw to change the rounding mode and restore it later.

fnstenv.description: Writes the x87 control, status and tag words and the last instruction and operand pointers to memory, then masks all x87 exceptions. Used by exception handlers.

fnstsw.description: Copies the 16-bit x87 status word to AX or memory. Old code followed fcom with 'fnstsw ax; sahf' to move C0, C2, C3 into CF, PF, ZF for a conditional jump.

fpatan.description: Computes the arctangent of ST(1)/ST(0) in the correct quadrant, like atan2(y, x), stores it in ST(1) and pops.

fprem.description: Computes the remainder of ST(0) / ST(1) with the quotient rounded toward zero, like C fmod. It may reduce only partly: C2 = 1 means run it again, so code loops on it.

fprem1.description: Like fprem, but rounds the quotient to nearest, giving the IEEE 754 remainder (C remainder()). C2 = 1 means the reduction is incomplete and must be repeated.

fptan.description: Replaces ST(0) with its tangent, then pushes 1.0, leaving tan(x) in ST(1); the 1.0 is for 8087 compatibility. Arguments beyond ±2^63 are left unchanged with C2 set.

frndint.description: Rounds ST(0) to an integral value with the rounding mode from the control word; the result stays in floating-point format.

frstor.description: Loads the x87 environment and all eight data registers from a memory area written by fnsave.

fs.description: Makes the memory operand of the next instruction relative to the FS base. On x86-64 Linux FS points at thread-local storage, so fs:[0x28] holds the stack canary. LLVM prints the prefix alone when it has no effect.

fscale.description: Multiplies ST(0) by 2 raised to ST(1) truncated toward zero, which adds an integer to the exponent; used with f2xm1 to build exp and pow.

fsin.description: Replaces ST(0) with its sine (radians). Arguments beyond ±2^63 are left unchanged with C2 set, and accuracy near large multiples of pi is poor, so math libraries avoid it.

fsincos.description: Computes both the sine and the cosine of ST(0): the sine replaces ST(0) and the cosine is pushed, so ST(0) = cos and ST(1) = sin.
fsincos.operation: t = cos(st0); st0 = sin(st0); push t

fsqrt.description: Replaces ST(0) with its correctly rounded square root; a negative input gives NaN and raises invalid-operation.

fst.description: Stores ST(0) to a 32- or 64-bit memory location, rounding to that format, or copies it to ST(i), without popping the stack.

fstp.description: Stores ST(0) to memory as a 32-, 64- or 80-bit value, or to ST(i), and pops the stack. 'fstp st(0)' just discards the top value.

fsub.description: Subtracts a 32- or 64-bit floating-point value in memory from ST(0); in the 'fsub st(i), st' form ST(i) = ST(i) − ST(0).
fsub.operation: st0 = st0 - src; or st(i) = st(i) - st0

fsubp.description: Computes ST(i) − ST(0), writes the difference into ST(i) and pops the stack.

fsubr.description: Subtracts ST(0) from a 32- or 64-bit floating-point value in memory and keeps the result in ST(0); in the 'fsubr st(i), st' form ST(i) = ST(0) − ST(i).
fsubr.operation: st0 = src - st0; or st(i) = st0 - st(i)

fsubrp.description: Computes ST(0) − ST(i), writes the difference into ST(i) and pops the stack.

ftst.description: Compares ST(0) with +0.0 and sets C0, C2, C3 in the status word: C3 for equal, C0 for less, all three for unordered.

fucom.description: Compares ST(0) with ST(i) and sets C0, C2, C3 in the status word. Unlike fcom, a quiet NaN operand does not raise invalid-operation.

fucomi.description: Compares ST(0) with ST(i) and writes ZF, PF and CF directly (unordered sets all three), so a jcc can follow; read the result like an unsigned compare (ja, jb). Quiet NaNs raise nothing.

fucomp.description: Like fucom: compares ST(0) with ST(i), sets C0, C2, C3 in the status word, then pops the stack.

fucompi.summary: Unordered compare into EFLAGS and pop
fucompi.description: Like fucomi, sets ZF, PF and CF from comparing ST(0) with ST(i), then pops the stack. A frequent float compare in 32-bit x87 code.

fucompp.description: Compares ST(0) with ST(1), sets C0, C2, C3 in the status word and pops both values off the stack.

fxam.description: Classifies ST(0) into C0, C2, C3 — empty, NaN, infinity, zero, denormal, normal or unsupported — and copies its sign into C1.

fxch.description: Swaps ST(0) with ST(i), ST(1) by default. Cheap on most processors; compilers use it to bring an operand to the top of the stack.

fxrstor.summary: Restore x87, MMX and SSE state
fxrstor.description: Loads the x87, MMX and XMM registers and MXCSR from a 512-byte, 16-byte-aligned area written by fxsave. In this format the x87 instruction and data pointers are 32-bit.

fxrstor64.summary: Restore x87 and SSE state (64-bit format)
fxrstor64.description: Same as fxrstor with REX.W: the saved x87 instruction and data pointers are read as full 64-bit addresses. Used by 64-bit kernels and debuggers.

fxsave.summary: Save x87, MMX and SSE state
fxsave.description: Writes the x87, MMX and XMM registers and MXCSR to a 512-byte, 16-byte-aligned area. Kernels use it or xsave on context switches; unlike fnsave it leaves the x87 state as is.

fxsave64.summary: Save x87 and SSE state (64-bit format)
fxsave64.description: Same as fxsave with REX.W: the x87 instruction and data pointers are stored as 64-bit addresses rather than selector:offset pairs.

fxtract.description: Splits ST(0) into its unbiased exponent and significand: the exponent replaces ST(0), then the significand is pushed, so ST(0) = significand and ST(1) = exponent.
fxtract.operation: t = significand(st0); st0 = exponent(st0); push t

fyl2x.description: Computes ST(1) × log2(ST(0)), stores it in ST(1) and pops. With ln(2) or log10(2) loaded as ST(1) it yields natural or decimal logarithms.

fyl2xp1.summary: Multiply by base-2 logarithm of x+1
fyl2xp1.description: Computes ST(1) × log2(ST(0) + 1) and pops. Accurate when ST(0) is near zero, which suits log1p; ST(0) must lie within about ±0.29.

getsec.description: Runs the Intel TXT (SMX) function selected by EAX, such as querying capabilities or entering a measured launch environment (SENTER). Used by trusted-boot loaders such as tboot.

gf2p8affineinvqb.description: For each byte, takes its multiplicative inverse in GF(2^8) (polynomial x^8+x^4+x^3+x+1), multiplies it by the 8×8 bit matrix in the matching source qword and XORs imm8; this can compute the AES S-box.

gf2p8affineqb.description: Multiplies each destination byte, as a bit vector, by the 8×8 bit matrix in the matching source qword and XORs imm8. A general bit-shuffling tool: bit reversal, rotations, SM4 and AES S-box steps.

gf2p8mulb.description: Multiplies bytes pairwise in GF(2^8), reducing by the AES polynomial x^8+x^4+x^3+x+1. Used for AES MixColumns, Reed–Solomon and erasure codes.

gs.description: Makes the memory operand of the next instruction relative to the GS base. macOS and Windows x64 user code keep thread-local data there; kernels use it for per-CPU data after swapgs.

haddpd.description: Adds adjacent pairs: the low result is the sum of the two doubles in the destination, the high result the sum of the two in the source. VEX vhaddpd has a separate destination.

haddps.description: Adds adjacent pairs of floats: results 0–1 come from the destination’s pairs, results 2–3 from the source’s. Often used in the last steps of a horizontal sum.

hlt.description: Stops the processor until the next interrupt, NMI or reset. Privileged: kernels run it in the idle loop, and in user mode it faults with #GP.

hreset.description: Clears the parts of the processor’s history selected by EAX, such as the Intel Thread Director history; the immediate is ignored. Run by the OS on context switches.

hsubpd.description: Subtracts within adjacent pairs: the low result is destination[0] − destination[1], the high result source[0] − source[1].

hsubps.description: Subtracts within adjacent float pairs: results 0–1 are differences of the destination’s pairs, results 2–3 of the source’s, the lower element minus the upper.

idiv.description: Divides DX:AX, EDX:EAX or RDX:RAX (AX for bytes) by a signed source: quotient in the low half, remainder in the high half. Compilers put cdq/cqo before it; zero or INT_MIN / -1 raises #DE.
idiv.operation: rax = rdx:rax / src; rdx = rdx:rax % src

imul.description: One-operand form multiplies the accumulator by the source into DX:AX, EDX:EAX or RDX:RAX; two- and three-operand forms keep the low half: dst = dst × src or dst = src × imm. CF and OF report overflow.

imulzu.summary: Signed multiply by immediate, zero upper (APX)
imulzu.description: APX form of three-operand imul: dst = src × imm, and the destination is zero-extended to 64 bits even for 16-bit operands instead of keeping its old upper bits. CF and OF flag overflow.

in.description: Reads a byte, word or doubleword into AL, AX or EAX from the I/O port given by an immediate (0–255) or by DX. Allowed only with enough privilege (IOPL) or when the I/O permission bitmap grants it.

inc.description: Adds one to a register or memory operand. Sets OF, SF, ZF, AF, PF but leaves CF unchanged. APX adds a three-operand NDD form and an {nf} form that leaves the flags untouched.

incsspd.description: Adds 4 × the low byte of the register to the CET shadow stack pointer, dropping that many 4-byte entries. 32-bit runtimes use it in longjmp and exception unwinding.

incsspq.description: Adds 8 × the low byte of the register to the CET shadow stack pointer, discarding that many saved return addresses. Used by longjmp and C++ unwinding.

insb.description: Reads a byte from the I/O port in DX, stores it at ES:[RDI] and moves RDI by 1 forwards or backwards according to DF; with rep it repeats RCX times. Privileged like in.

insd.description: Reads a doubleword from the I/O port in DX, stores it at ES:[RDI] and moves RDI by 4 forwards or backwards according to DF; with rep it repeats RCX times. Privileged like in.

insertps.description: Copies one float — the source element chosen by imm8[7:6], or a value loaded from memory — into the destination element chosen by imm8[5:4], then zeroes the elements flagged in imm8[3:0].
insertps.operation: dst[imm[5:4]] = src[imm[7:6]]; zero lanes in imm[3:0]

insertq.description: AMD SSE4A: inserts the low bits of the source into the destination’s low qword at a given bit index and length, taken from two immediates or from the source’s upper qword. The destination’s high qword becomes undefined.

insw.description: Reads a word from the I/O port in DX, stores it at ES:[RDI] and moves RDI by 2 forwards or backwards according to DF; with rep it repeats RCX times. Privileged like in.

int.description: Invokes the interrupt or trap handler for vector imm8 through the IDT. 'int 0x80' was the classic 32-bit Linux system call; the two-byte 'int 3' differs slightly from the one-byte int3.
int.operation: push flags, cs, rip; rip = IDT[imm8]

int3.description: One-byte trap (0xCC) that raises #BP. Debuggers write it over code to set breakpoints, and compilers use it for __builtin_debugtrap and as padding between functions.

into.description: Raises the overflow exception (#OF, vector 4) if OF is set, otherwise does nothing. Exists only in 16- and 32-bit modes; the opcode is invalid in 64-bit mode.

invd.description: Discards the internal caches without writing modified lines back, so dirty data is lost. Privileged and used only by firmware or special boot code; wbinvd is the safe variant.

invept.description: VMX: invalidates cached guest-physical mappings derived from extended page tables. The register gives the type (single context or all), the 128-bit memory descriptor the EPT pointer. Hypervisors only.

invlpg.description: Removes the TLB entries for the page containing the memory operand’s address, after the kernel changes that page’s mapping. Privileged; the memory itself is not accessed.

invlpga.summary: Invalidate TLB entry in an ASID (AMD)
invlpga.description: AMD SVM: invalidates the TLB mapping for the virtual address in rAX within the address space ID in ECX. Used by hypervisors to flush guest translations.

invlpgb.description: AMD: invalidates TLB entries on every processor at once; rAX gives the address and what to flush, ECX the page count, EDX the ASID and PCID. Followed by tlbsync to wait for completion.

invpcid.description: Invalidates TLB entries for one address, one process-context ID or all contexts; the register holds the type, the 128-bit memory descriptor the PCID and address. Used by kernels with page-table isolation.

invvpid.description: VMX: invalidates mappings tagged with a virtual-processor ID; the register gives the type, the 128-bit memory descriptor the VPID and linear address. Hypervisors only.

iret.description: Returns from an interrupt or exception handler by popping IP, CS and FLAGS as 16-bit values, plus SP and SS on a privilege change. Rare outside real mode.
iret.operation: ip = pop(); cs = pop(); flags = pop()

iretd.description: Pops EIP, CS and EFLAGS, and ESP and SS when returning to a lower privilege level, to resume the interrupted code. Ends 32-bit interrupt handlers.
iretd.operation: eip = pop(); cs = pop(); eflags = pop()

iretq.description: Pops RIP, CS, RFLAGS, RSP and SS as 64-bit values, always restoring the stack, to resume interrupted code. 64-bit kernels end interrupt and exception handlers with it.
iretq.operation: rip, cs, rflags, rsp, ss = pop()

jcc.description: Jumps to a relative target when the condition on EFLAGS holds: je/jne (ZF), jb/jae and ja/jbe for unsigned, jl/jge and jg/jle for signed, js, jo, jp and their opposites. Otherwise falls through.

jcxz.description: Jumps to a short relative target when CX is zero, without reading or changing flags. In 32-bit code it needs an address-size prefix; the 16-bit counterpart of jecxz.

jecxz.description: Jumps to a short relative target (±127 bytes) when ECX is zero; flags are neither read nor changed. Used to skip a loop whose count is zero.

jmp.description: Unconditional jump: relative (rel8/rel32), or indirect through a register or memory as in switch tables and tail calls. Far forms load CS as well.

jmpabs.description: APX: jumps to a 64-bit absolute address carried as an immediate after a REX2 prefix, so no register or memory load is needed.

jrcxz.description: Jumps to a short relative target when RCX is zero, ignoring flags. Rare in compiler output but handy before a loop or a rep string instruction.

kaddb.description: Adds the low 8 bits of two opmask registers as integers, wrapping around, and writes the sum to the destination mask. Upper bits of the destination are zeroed.

kaddd.description: Adds the low 32 bits of two opmask registers as integers, wrapping around, and writes the sum to the destination mask. Upper bits of the destination are zeroed.

kaddq.description: Adds the low 64 bits of two opmask registers as integers, wrapping around, and writes the sum to the destination mask.

kaddw.description: Adds the low 16 bits of two opmask registers as integers, wrapping around, and writes the sum to the destination mask. Upper bits of the destination are zeroed.

kandb.description: ANDs the low 8 bits of two opmask registers into the destination, for example to combine two compare results for AVX-512 masking. Upper bits of the destination are zeroed.

kandd.description: ANDs the low 32 bits of two opmask registers into the destination, for example to combine two compare results for AVX-512 masking. Upper bits of the destination are zeroed.

kandnb.description: Inverts the first source mask and ANDs it with the second over the low 8 bits, clearing in the second the lanes set in the first. Upper bits of the destination are zeroed.

kandnd.description: Inverts the first source mask and ANDs it with the second over the low 32 bits, clearing in the second the lanes set in the first. Upper bits of the destination are zeroed.

kandnq.description: Inverts the first source mask and ANDs it with the second over the low 64 bits, clearing in the second the lanes set in the first.

kandnw.description: Inverts the first source mask and ANDs it with the second over the low 16 bits, clearing in the second the lanes set in the first. Upper bits of the destination are zeroed.

kandq.description: ANDs the low 64 bits of two opmask registers into the destination, for example to combine two compare results for AVX-512 masking.

kandw.description: ANDs the low 16 bits of two opmask registers into the destination, for example to combine two compare results for AVX-512 masking. Upper bits of the destination are zeroed.

kmovb.description: Copies 8 bits between opmask registers, memory and general-purpose registers; a move into a GPR zero-extends, a move from one takes the low bits. APX adds EVEX forms reaching r16–r31.

kmovd.description: Copies 32 bits between opmask registers, memory and general-purpose registers; a move into a GPR zero-extends, a move from one takes the low bits. APX adds EVEX forms reaching r16–r31.

kmovq.description: Copies 64 bits between opmask registers, memory and general-purpose registers; a move into a GPR zero-extends, a move from one takes the low bits. APX adds EVEX forms reaching r16–r31.

kmovw.description: Copies 16 bits between opmask registers, memory and general-purpose registers; a move into a GPR zero-extends, a move from one takes the low bits. APX adds EVEX forms reaching r16–r31.

knotb.description: Inverts the low 8 bits of the source mask and writes them to the destination mask. Upper bits of the destination are zeroed.

knotd.description: Inverts the low 32 bits of the source mask and writes them to the destination mask. Upper bits of the destination are zeroed.

knotq.description: Inverts the low 64 bits of the source mask and writes them to the destination mask.

knotw.description: Inverts the low 16 bits of the source mask and writes them to the destination mask. Upper bits of the destination are zeroed.

korb.description: ORs the low 8 bits of two opmask registers into the destination, merging the lanes selected by either mask. Upper bits of the destination are zeroed.

kord.description: ORs the low 32 bits of two opmask registers into the destination, merging the lanes selected by either mask. Upper bits of the destination are zeroed.

korq.description: ORs the low 64 bits of two opmask registers into the destination, merging the lanes selected by either mask.

kortestb.description: ORs two 8-bit masks without storing the result: ZF is set if it is all zeros, CF if it is all ones, other flags cleared. Used to branch when no lane, or every lane, matched a compare.

kortestd.description: ORs two 32-bit masks without storing the result: ZF is set if it is all zeros, CF if it is all ones, other flags cleared. Used to branch when no lane, or every lane, matched a compare.

kortestq.description: ORs two 64-bit masks without storing the result: ZF is set if it is all zeros, CF if it is all ones, other flags cleared. Used to branch when no lane, or every lane, matched a compare.

kortestw.description: ORs two 16-bit masks without storing the result: ZF is set if it is all zeros, CF if it is all ones, other flags cleared. Used to branch when no lane, or every lane, matched a compare.

korw.description: ORs the low 16 bits of two opmask registers into the destination, merging the lanes selected by either mask. Upper bits of the destination are zeroed.

kshiftlb.description: Shifts the low 8 bits of the source mask left by imm8, filling with zeros; a count of 8 or more gives zero. Upper bits of the destination are zeroed.

kshiftld.description: Shifts the low 32 bits of the source mask left by imm8, filling with zeros; a count of 32 or more gives zero. Upper bits of the destination are zeroed.

kshiftlq.description: Shifts the low 64 bits of the source mask left by imm8, filling with zeros; a count of 64 or more gives zero.

kshiftlw.description: Shifts the low 16 bits of the source mask left by imm8, filling with zeros; a count of 16 or more gives zero. Upper bits of the destination are zeroed.

kshiftrb.description: Shifts the low 8 bits of the source mask right by imm8, filling with zeros; a count of 8 or more gives zero. Upper bits of the destination are zeroed.

kshiftrd.description: Shifts the low 32 bits of the source mask right by imm8, filling with zeros; a count of 32 or more gives zero. Upper bits of the destination are zeroed.

kshiftrq.description: Shifts the low 64 bits of the source mask right by imm8, filling with zeros; a count of 64 or more gives zero.

kshiftrw.description: Shifts the low 16 bits of the source mask right by imm8, filling with zeros; a count of 16 or more gives zero. Upper bits of the destination are zeroed.

ktestb.description: Sets ZF if the AND of the two 8-bit masks is zero and CF if the AND of the inverted first mask with the second is zero; other flags are cleared and nothing else is written.

ktestd.description: Sets ZF if the AND of the two 32-bit masks is zero and CF if the AND of the inverted first mask with the second is zero; other flags are cleared and nothing else is written.

ktestq.description: Sets ZF if the AND of the two 64-bit masks is zero and CF if the AND of the inverted first mask with the second is zero; other flags are cleared and nothing else is written.

ktestw.description: Sets ZF if the AND of the two 16-bit masks is zero and CF if the AND of the inverted first mask with the second is zero; other flags are cleared and nothing else is written.

kunpckbw.description: Concatenates the low 8 bits of two masks into a 16-bit mask: the first source goes into bits 15:8, the second into bits 7:0.

kunpckdq.description: Concatenates the low 32 bits of two masks into a 64-bit mask: the first source goes into bits 63:32, the second into bits 31:0.

kunpckwd.description: Concatenates the low 16 bits of two masks into a 32-bit mask: the first source goes into bits 31:16, the second into bits 15:0.

kxnorb.description: XNORs the low 8 bits of two masks. With the same register for both sources it sets the mask to all ones, the usual setup before a gather or scatter. Upper bits of the destination are zeroed.

kxnord.description: XNORs the low 32 bits of two masks. With the same register for both sources it sets the mask to all ones, the usual setup before a gather or scatter. Upper bits of the destination are zeroed.

kxnorq.description: XNORs the low 64 bits of two masks. With the same register for both sources it sets the mask to all ones, the usual setup before a gather or scatter.

kxnorw.description: XNORs the low 16 bits of two masks. With the same register for both sources it sets the mask to all ones, the usual setup before a gather or scatter. Upper bits of the destination are zeroed.

kxorb.description: XORs the low 8 bits of two masks; XOR of a register with itself clears it. Upper bits of the destination are zeroed.

kxord.description: XORs the low 32 bits of two masks; XOR of a register with itself clears it. Upper bits of the destination are zeroed.

kxorq.description: XORs the low 64 bits of two masks; XOR of a register with itself clears it.

kxorw.description: XORs the low 16 bits of two masks; XOR of a register with itself clears it. Upper bits of the destination are zeroed.

lahf.description: Copies SF, ZF, AF, PF and CF, the low byte of FLAGS, into AH. In 64-bit mode it needs the LAHF-SAHF CPU feature, present on nearly every 64-bit processor.

lar.description: Reads the access-rights fields of the segment descriptor named by a selector into the destination and sets ZF if the selector is valid and visible at the current privilege level; otherwise clears ZF.
lar.operation: if (valid(sel)) { dst = rights(sel); ZF = 1 } else ZF = 0

lcall.description: Calls a procedure in another code segment: pushes CS and the return address, then loads CS and IP from an immediate pointer (not in 64-bit mode) or from a far pointer in memory.
lcall.operation: push cs; push rip; cs:rip = target

lddqu.description: Loads 128 bits from any address; some processors fetch two aligned blocks to speed up loads that cross a cache line. Otherwise like movdqu; avoid on uncacheable memory. VEX vlddqu adds 256 bits.

ldmxcsr.description: Loads the SSE control and status register from memory: rounding mode, exception masks and flags, flush-to-zero and denormals-are-zero. Setting a reserved bit raises #GP.

lds.description: Loads a far pointer from memory: the offset into the register and the following 16-bit selector into DS. Invalid in 64-bit mode, where C5 starts a VEX prefix.

ldtilecfg.description: Reads a 64-byte tile configuration from memory — palette, rows and bytes per row of each tmm0–tmm7 — and zeroes every tile. Must run before any other AMX tile instruction.

lea.description: Computes the address of the memory operand (base + index × scale + displacement) into the register without touching memory or flags. Compilers use it for cheap arithmetic like x*5+3 and RIP-relative addresses.

leave.description: Undoes the frame set up by 'push rbp; mov rbp, rsp': copies RBP into RSP and pops the saved RBP. Common in function epilogues.

les.description: Loads a far pointer from memory: the offset into the register and the following 16-bit selector into ES. Invalid in 64-bit mode, where C4 starts a VEX prefix.

lfence.description: Waits until all earlier instructions have completed locally before later ones start, ordering loads too. Widely used as a speculation barrier against Spectre and around rdtsc.

lfs.description: Loads a far pointer from memory: the offset into the register and the following 16-bit selector into FS. Still valid in 64-bit mode, unlike lds and les.

lgdt.description: Loads the 16-bit limit and the base address of the global descriptor table into GDTR from memory; in 64-bit mode the base is 64 bits. Privileged; run while an OS boots.

lgdtd.description: i386 spelling of lgdt with 32-bit operand size: loads a 16-bit limit and a 32-bit base from memory into GDTR. Privileged.

lgdtw.description: lgdt with a 16-bit operand-size prefix: loads the 16-bit limit and only 24 bits of the base into GDTR, the top byte becoming zero as on the 80286. Privileged.

lgs.description: Loads a far pointer from memory: the offset into the register and the following 16-bit selector into GS. Still valid in 64-bit mode, unlike lds and les.

lidt.description: Loads the 16-bit limit and the base address of the interrupt descriptor table into IDTR from memory; in 64-bit mode the base is 64 bits. Privileged; kernels run it at boot to install interrupt and exception handlers.

lidtd.description: i386 spelling of lidt with 32-bit operand size: loads a 16-bit limit and a 32-bit base from memory into IDTR. Privileged.

lidtw.description: lidt with a 16-bit operand-size prefix: loads the 16-bit limit and only 24 bits of the base into IDTR, the top byte becoming zero as on the 80286. Privileged.

ljmp.description: Jumps to another code segment: loads both CS and the instruction pointer, either from an immediate selector:offset pair (not available in 64-bit mode) or from a far pointer in memory. Used in boot code and mode switches.

lkgs.summary: Load kernel GS base from selector
lkgs.description: Loads a 16-bit selector into GS, but puts the base address from its descriptor into the IA32_KERNEL_GS_BASE MSR instead of the GS base. Part of FRED; lets a ring-0 kernel switch user GS without swapgs.

lldt.description: Loads LDTR with a selector that names an LDT descriptor in the GDT; a null selector disables the LDT. Privileged, used by operating systems.

llwpcb.description: Enables AMD Lightweight Profiling for the thread by pointing the hardware at the LWP control block whose address is in the register; an address of 0 turns profiling off.

lmsw.description: Writes the low four bits of CR0 (PE, MP, EM, TS) from the 16-bit source. It can set PE but never clear it. A leftover from the 286; privileged.

loadiwkey.summary: Load Key Locker internal wrapping key
loadiwkey.description: Loads the Key Locker internal wrapping key from the two xmm operands and xmm0, with options in eax (for example a randomised key). Ring 0 only; ZF reports failure. Later encodekey and aesenc*kl use this key.

lock.description: Makes the following read-modify-write instruction on memory atomic (add, sub, and, or, xor, inc, dec, neg, not, bts, btr, btc, xadd, cmpxchg…). Compilers emit it for atomic operations; xchg with memory is locked without it.

lodsb.description: Loads the byte at [rsi] into al and moves rsi by 1, forward or backward depending on DF. Rarely used with rep, since each step overwrites al.

lodsd.description: Loads the 32-bit value at [rsi] into eax and moves rsi by 4 in the direction given by DF.

lodsq.description: Loads the 64-bit value at [rsi] into rax and moves rsi by 8 in the direction given by DF.

lodsw.description: Loads the 16-bit value at [rsi] into ax and moves rsi by 2 in the direction given by DF.

loop.summary: Decrement count and jump if not zero
loop.description: Decrements rcx (ecx with a 67 prefix) without touching flags and jumps to a short target if the count is not zero. Slow on many CPUs, so compilers prefer dec plus jnz.

loope.description: Decrements rcx without touching flags and jumps to a short target if the count is not zero and ZF is set. Also written loopz.

loopne.description: Decrements rcx without touching flags and jumps to a short target if the count is not zero and ZF is clear. Also written loopnz.

lsl.description: Reads the limit of the segment named by a selector into the destination, if the descriptor is valid and visible at the current privilege; sets ZF on success and leaves the destination unchanged otherwise. Linux uses it in getcpu to read a per-CPU GDT entry.
lsl.operation: if (valid(src)) { dst = limit(src); ZF = 1 } else ZF = 0

lss.description: Loads a far pointer from memory: the offset goes into the destination register and the selector into SS. Changes the stack segment and pointer together; found in old real-mode and boot code.

ltr.description: Loads the task register with a selector naming a TSS descriptor and marks that TSS busy. Kernels run it once per CPU at startup; privileged.

lwpins.description: Inserts a programmer-defined event record into the AMD Lightweight Profiling ring buffer, carrying the register, memory and immediate values. CF reports whether the buffer was full.

lwpval.description: Decrements the AMD Lightweight Profiling programmed-value counter and, when it runs out, stores an event record with the register, memory and immediate values. Used to sample values at a chosen rate.

lzcnt.description: Counts zero bits above the highest set bit; a zero source gives the operand size (16, 32 or 64) and sets CF, and ZF is set when the result is 0. On CPUs without LZCNT the same bytes run as bsr and give a different answer.

maskmovdqu.description: Stores the bytes of the first xmm operand to [rdi] wherever the matching byte of the second operand has its top bit set; other bytes in memory are left alone. The store is non-temporal.
maskmovdqu.operation: for i in 0..15: if (mask[i] & 0x80) [rdi + i] = src[i]

maskmovq.description: Stores the bytes of the first MMX register to [rdi] wherever the matching byte of the second register has its top bit set, using a non-temporal hint.
maskmovq.operation: for i in 0..7: if (mask[i] & 0x80) [rdi + i] = src[i]

maxpd.description: Takes the larger of each pair of doubles. If either value is NaN, or both are zeros, the second operand is returned, so the result matches C's a > b ? a : b rather than fmax.

maxps.description: Takes the larger of each of the four pairs of floats. A NaN in either value, or two zeros, yields the second operand, which is why the order of operands matters.

maxsd.description: Writes the larger of the low doubles into the low lane of the destination, keeping its upper lane. NaN or two zeros give the second operand; compilers use it for a > b ? a : b.
