maxss.description: Writes the larger of the low floats into the low lane of the destination, keeping the other three lanes. NaN or two zeros give the second operand.

mfence.description: Waits until all earlier loads and stores are globally visible before any later ones run. Compilers emit it (or a locked instruction) for sequentially consistent stores; needed around non-temporal stores and to order a store before a load.
mfence.operation: order(all earlier loads and stores, all later ones)

minpd.description: Takes the smaller of each pair of doubles. If either value is NaN, or both are zeros, the second operand is returned, so it behaves like a < b ? a : b rather than fmin.

minps.description: Takes the smaller of each of the four pairs of floats. A NaN in either value, or two zeros, yields the second operand.

minsd.description: Writes the smaller of the low doubles into the low lane of the destination, keeping its upper lane. NaN or two zeros give the second operand.

minss.description: Writes the smaller of the low floats into the low lane of the destination, keeping the other three lanes. NaN or two zeros give the second operand.

monitor.description: Arms the hardware to watch the cache line at [rax], with extensions in ecx and hints in edx; a following mwait sleeps until that line is written. Used by kernel idle loops; usually unavailable outside ring 0.

monitorx.description: AMD's user-mode variant of monitor: arms the watch on the cache line at [rax] for a following mwaitx. Usable from ring 3 for efficient spin-waits.

montmul.description: Runs the VIA PadLock Montgomery multiplier, which speeds up modular arithmetic for RSA; operands are described by a structure that esi/rsi points to, with the size in ecx. Normally written with rep.

mov.description: Copies the source into the destination: register, memory or immediate, without changing flags. Writing a 32-bit register zeroes the upper half of the 64-bit register; forms with segment, control and debug registers also exist.

movabs.description: LLVM's name for the mov forms that carry a full 64-bit value: a 64-bit immediate into a register, or the accumulator loaded from or stored to a 64-bit absolute address. The only way to encode a 64-bit constant in one instruction.

movapd.description: Copies 128 bits between xmm registers or memory; a memory operand must be 16-byte aligned or the instruction faults. Equivalent to movaps in effect.

movaps.description: Copies 128 bits between xmm registers or memory; a memory operand must be 16-byte aligned or it faults. Compilers use it for any register copy because its encoding is the shortest.

movbe.description: Loads from or stores to memory while reversing the byte order of the 16-, 32- or 64-bit value, for big-endian data such as network headers. APX adds a register-to-register form.

movd.summary: Move doubleword to or from vector
movd.description: Moves 32 bits between a general register or memory and the low element of an mm or xmm register. Writing an xmm or mm register zeroes the bits above the 32 copied.

movddup.description: Copies the low double of the source into both lanes of the destination. Handy for broadcasting a scalar double or loading a complex number's part twice.

movdir64b.description: Reads 64 bytes from the memory operand and writes them as one atomic 64-byte direct store to the address held in the register (relative to ES). Used to submit work descriptors to accelerator devices; the read is not atomic.

movdiri.summary: Move doubleword or quadword as direct store
movdiri.description: Stores a 32- or 64-bit register to memory as a direct store that bypasses the cache with write-combining, done as a single atomic write. Used to ring device doorbells.

movdq2q.summary: Move low quadword from xmm to mm
movdq2q.description: Copies the low 64 bits of an xmm register into an MMX register and switches the x87 unit into MMX state.

movdqa.description: Copies 128 bits between xmm registers or memory; memory must be 16-byte aligned or it faults. The integer-domain counterpart of movaps.

movdqu.description: Copies 128 bits between xmm registers or memory with no alignment requirement. On modern CPUs it is as fast as movdqa when the address happens to be aligned.

movhlps.summary: Move high half to low half
movhlps.description: Copies the high 64 bits of the source xmm into the low 64 bits of the destination, leaving the destination's high half unchanged. Common in horizontal reductions.

movhpd.description: Loads a double from memory into the high lane of an xmm register, keeping the low lane, or stores the high lane to memory.

movhps.description: Loads 64 bits (two floats) from memory into the high half of an xmm register, keeping the low half, or stores the high half to memory.

movlhps.summary: Move low half to high half
movlhps.description: Copies the low 64 bits of the source xmm into the high 64 bits of the destination, leaving the destination's low half unchanged.

movlpd.description: Loads a double from memory into the low lane of an xmm register, keeping the high lane, or stores the low lane to memory.

movlps.description: Loads 64 bits (two floats) from memory into the low half of an xmm register, keeping the high half, or stores the low half to memory.

movmskpd.description: Gathers the sign bits of the two doubles into bits 0–1 of a general register and zeroes the rest. Used to branch on the result of a vector compare.

movmskps.description: Gathers the sign bits of the four floats into bits 0–3 of a general register and zeroes the rest. Used to test vector compare results with ordinary branches.

movntdq.description: Stores an xmm register to 16-byte-aligned memory with a hint to bypass the caches, useful for large copies and fills. Such stores are weakly ordered, so an sfence is needed before handing the data to another thread.

movntdqa.description: Loads 128 bits from 16-byte-aligned memory with a streaming hint. The hint only matters on write-combining memory such as video buffers; on ordinary memory it acts as movdqa.

movnti.description: Stores a 32- or 64-bit general register to memory with a hint to bypass the caches. Weakly ordered; follow with sfence before publishing the data.

movntpd.description: Stores an xmm register of doubles to 16-byte-aligned memory, bypassing the caches. Weakly ordered, so pair it with sfence.

movntps.description: Stores an xmm register of floats to 16-byte-aligned memory, bypassing the caches. Weakly ordered, so pair it with sfence.

movntq.description: Stores a 64-bit MMX register to memory, bypassing the caches. Weakly ordered, so pair it with sfence.

movntsd.description: AMD SSE4A: stores the low double of an xmm register to memory, bypassing the caches.

movntss.description: AMD SSE4A: stores the low float of an xmm register to memory, bypassing the caches.

movq.description: Moves 64 bits between mm or xmm registers, general registers and memory. Writing an xmm register zeroes its upper 64 bits, so movq xmm, xmm is a common way to clear the high half.

movq2dq.summary: Move quadword from mm to xmm
movq2dq.description: Copies an MMX register into the low 64 bits of an xmm register, zeroing the upper 64 bits, and switches the x87 unit into MMX state.

movrs.description: Loads an 8-, 16-, 32- or 64-bit value like mov, with a hint that the cache line is read by many cores and rarely written, so the hardware can keep it shared.

movsb.description: Copies the byte at [rsi] to [rdi] and moves both pointers by 1 in the direction given by DF. With rep it copies rcx bytes; memcpy implementations use rep movsb on CPUs with fast string support.

movsd.summary: Move scalar double, or move string doubleword
movsd.description: Two instructions share the name. The SSE2 one moves the low double: loading from memory zeroes the upper lane, a register copy keeps it. The string one (A5) copies 4 bytes from [rsi] to [rdi] and advances both pointers, often with rep.

movshdup.description: Copies each odd-indexed float into itself and the even lane below it, giving {s1, s1, s3, s3}. Used in complex multiplication and horizontal sums.

movsldup.description: Copies each even-indexed float into itself and the odd lane above it, giving {s0, s0, s2, s2}.

movsq.description: Copies 8 bytes from [rsi] to [rdi] and moves both pointers by 8 in the direction given by DF. With rep it copies rcx quadwords.

movss.description: Moves the low float between xmm registers or memory. A load from memory zeroes the upper three lanes; a register-to-register copy replaces only the low lane.

movsw.description: Copies 2 bytes from [rsi] to [rdi] and moves both pointers by 2 in the direction given by DF. With rep it copies rcx words.

movsx.description: Copies an 8- or 16-bit source into a wider register, filling the upper bits with copies of the sign bit. Compilers use it for signed char and short.

movsxd.description: Sign-extends a 32-bit source into a 64-bit register, typically to turn an int index into a pointer offset. Without REX.W it is just a 32-bit move.

movupd.description: Copies 128 bits of doubles between xmm registers or memory with no alignment requirement.

movups.description: Copies 128 bits between xmm registers or memory with no alignment requirement. Compilers use it for generic 16-byte loads and stores, including struct copies.

movzx.description: Copies an 8- or 16-bit source into a wider register, filling the upper bits with zeros. Used for unsigned char and short, and to avoid partial-register stalls.

mpsadbw.summary: Multiple sums of absolute byte differences
mpsadbw.description: Compares a 4-byte block of the source, picked by the immediate, with eight overlapping 4-byte windows of the destination and writes the eight sums of absolute differences as words. Built for video motion estimation.
mpsadbw.operation: dst.w[i] = Σj |a[off + i + j] - b[blk + j]|, i = 0..7

mul.description: Multiplies the accumulator (al, ax, eax or rax) by the unsigned source and writes the double-width product to ax, dx:ax, edx:eax or rdx:rax. CF and OF are set when the high half is non-zero.

mulpd.description: Multiplies the two pairs of doubles lane by lane, writing the products into the destination.

mulps.description: Multiplies the four pairs of floats lane by lane, writing the products into the destination.

mulsd.description: Multiplies the low doubles and writes the product into the low lane of the destination, keeping its upper lane. Compilers use it for ordinary double multiplication.

mulss.description: Multiplies the low floats and writes the product into the low lane of the destination, keeping the other three lanes.

mulx.description: BMI2: multiplies edx or rdx by the unsigned source; the first operand receives the high half and the second the low half, and flags are untouched. Used in big-number arithmetic together with adcx and adox.
mulx.operation: hi:lo = rdx * src  // dst1 = hi, dst2 = lo

mwait.description: Puts the core into an optimised wait or a deeper sleep state, chosen by the hint in eax, until the line armed by monitor is written or an interrupt arrives. Used in kernel idle loops; usually ring 0 only.

mwaitx.summary: Wait for monitored write with timeout
mwaitx.description: AMD's user-mode variant of mwait: waits until the line armed by monitorx is written, an interrupt arrives, or, if enabled in ecx, a timeout in ebx (in TSC ticks) expires.
mwaitx.operation: wait until write(monitor_line) or interrupt or timeout(ebx)

neg.description: Replaces the operand with its two's-complement negation. CF is set unless the operand was zero; the other flags follow the subtraction 0 - x. APX adds a form that writes a separate destination.

nop.description: Does nothing. The 0F 1F forms take a memory operand that is never accessed, letting assemblers pad code to an alignment boundary with a single long instruction.

not.description: Inverts every bit of the operand and leaves the flags unchanged. APX adds a form that writes a separate destination.

or.description: ORs the source into the destination. CF and OF are cleared and SF, ZF, PF follow the result; or reg, reg is sometimes used just to test a value. APX adds three-operand and no-flags forms.

orpd.description: ORs 128 bits of the source into the destination. Compilers use it with sign-bit masks, for example to implement copysign or -fabs.

orps.description: ORs 128 bits of the source into the destination. Used with sign masks and to merge vector compare results.

out.description: Writes al, ax or eax to the I/O port given by an 8-bit immediate or by dx. Allowed only when IOPL or the TSS I/O bitmap permits, so normally kernels and drivers.

outsb.description: Writes the byte at [rsi] to the I/O port in dx and moves rsi by 1 in the direction given by DF; with rep it sends rcx bytes. Subject to I/O permission checks.

outsd.description: Writes the 32-bit value at [rsi] to the I/O port in dx and moves rsi by 4 in the direction given by DF; with rep it sends rcx doublewords.

outsw.description: Writes the 16-bit value at [rsi] to the I/O port in dx and moves rsi by 2 in the direction given by DF; with rep it sends rcx words, as in ATA PIO transfers.

pabsb.description: Replaces each signed byte of the source with its absolute value in the destination. The result is unsigned, so -128 becomes 0x80 (128).

pabsd.description: Replaces each signed 32-bit element of the source with its absolute value in the destination; the most negative value stays 0x80000000.

pabsw.description: Replaces each signed 16-bit element of the source with its absolute value in the destination; -32768 stays 0x8000.

packssdw.summary: Pack doublewords to words with signed saturation
packssdw.description: Narrows the signed doublewords of the destination (low half of the result) and the source (high half) to signed words, clamping to -32768…32767.

packsswb.summary: Pack words to bytes with signed saturation
packsswb.description: Narrows the signed words of the destination (low half of the result) and the source (high half) to signed bytes, clamping to -128…127.

packusdw.summary: Pack doublewords to words with unsigned saturation
packusdw.description: Narrows the signed doublewords of the destination and the source to unsigned words, clamping negatives to 0 and large values to 65535; the destination's elements fill the low half.

packuswb.summary: Pack words to bytes with unsigned saturation
packuswb.description: Narrows the signed words of the destination and the source to unsigned bytes, clamping to 0…255; the destination's elements fill the low half. Common when converting pixels back to 8 bits.

paddb.description: Adds the bytes of the source to those of the destination lane by lane, wrapping on overflow.

paddd.description: Adds the 32-bit elements of the source to those of the destination lane by lane, wrapping on overflow.

paddq.description: Adds the 64-bit elements of the source to those of the destination lane by lane, wrapping on overflow.

paddsb.summary: Packed add bytes with signed saturation
paddsb.description: Adds signed bytes lane by lane, clamping each sum to -128…127 instead of wrapping.

paddsw.summary: Packed add words with signed saturation
paddsw.description: Adds signed words lane by lane, clamping each sum to -32768…32767. Common in audio mixing.

paddusb.summary: Packed add bytes with unsigned saturation
paddusb.description: Adds unsigned bytes lane by lane, clamping each sum at 255. Common in pixel arithmetic.

paddusw.summary: Packed add words with unsigned saturation
paddusw.description: Adds unsigned words lane by lane, clamping each sum at 65535.

paddw.description: Adds the 16-bit elements of the source to those of the destination lane by lane, wrapping on overflow.

palignr.description: Joins the destination (high part) and the source (low part) into one double-width value, shifts it right by the immediate number of bytes and keeps the low 16 (or 8 for mm) bytes. Used to read unaligned windows from two loads.

pand.description: ANDs the source into the destination across the whole register.

pandn.description: Inverts the destination and ANDs it with the source. The inverted operand is the first one, the opposite of what the name may suggest.

pause.description: Tells the CPU it is inside a spin-wait loop, saving power, freeing resources for the sibling hyper-thread and avoiding a pipeline flush on exit. On recent Intel cores it can stall for over 100 cycles. Encoded as rep nop.

pavgb.description: Averages unsigned bytes lane by lane, rounding up halves.

pavgusb.description: AMD 3DNow!: averages the eight unsigned bytes of two MMX operands lane by lane, rounding up halves. Same result as pavgb on mm.

pavgw.description: Averages unsigned 16-bit elements lane by lane, rounding up halves.

pblendvb.description: Picks each byte from the source where the top bit of the matching byte in xmm0 is set, and keeps the destination byte otherwise. The mask register xmm0 is implicit.

pblendw.description: Picks word i from the source when bit i of the immediate is set and keeps the destination word otherwise.

pbndkb.summary: Platform bind key to binary large object
pbndkb.description: Part of Intel Total Storage Encryption: binds an encryption key to the platform and writes the wrapped key out, using structures addressed by rbx and rcx. Ring 0 only; status comes back in ZF and eax.

pclmulqdq.description: Multiplies one 64-bit half of each operand as polynomials over GF(2) and writes the 128-bit product. Immediate bit 0 picks the destination's half, bit 4 the source's. Used for CRC32, AES-GCM and other checksums.

pcmpeqb.description: Sets each byte of the destination to all ones where the bytes are equal and to zero otherwise. pcmpeqb x, x is a common way to fill a register with ones.

pcmpeqd.description: Sets each 32-bit element of the destination to all ones where the elements are equal and to zero otherwise.

pcmpeqq.description: Sets each 64-bit element of the destination to all ones where the elements are equal and to zero otherwise.

pcmpeqw.description: Sets each 16-bit element of the destination to all ones where the elements are equal and to zero otherwise.

pcmpestri.description: Compares two strings of bytes or words whose lengths are in eax and edx, using the mode in the immediate (any match, ranges, equal each, substring), and puts the index of the first or last hit in ecx. CF, ZF, SF and OF describe the result.
pcmpestri.operation: ecx = index(match(dst, eax, src, edx, imm))

pcmpestrm.description: Compares two strings whose lengths are in eax and edx, using the mode in the immediate, and writes the result as a bit mask or element mask into xmm0. Flags describe the result as for pcmpestri.
pcmpestrm.operation: xmm0 = mask(match(dst, eax, src, edx, imm))

pcmpgtb.summary: Packed compare signed bytes for greater than
pcmpgtb.description: Sets each byte of the destination to all ones where the destination's signed byte is greater than the source's, and to zero otherwise. For unsigned compares the sign bits have to be flipped first.

pcmpgtd.summary: Packed compare signed doublewords for greater than
pcmpgtd.description: Sets each 32-bit element of the destination to all ones where the destination's signed value is greater than the source's, and to zero otherwise.

pcmpgtq.summary: Packed compare signed quadwords for greater than
pcmpgtq.description: Sets each 64-bit element of the destination to all ones where the destination's signed value is greater than the source's, and to zero otherwise.

pcmpgtw.summary: Packed compare signed words for greater than
pcmpgtw.description: Sets each 16-bit element of the destination to all ones where the destination's signed value is greater than the source's, and to zero otherwise.

pcmpistri.description: Compares two strings of bytes or words that end at the first zero element, using the mode in the immediate, and puts the index of the first or last hit in ecx. ZF and SF tell whether each operand contained the terminator; used in fast strlen and strchr.

pcmpistrm.description: Compares two zero-terminated strings of bytes or words using the mode in the immediate and writes the result as a bit mask or element mask into xmm0. Flags describe the result as for pcmpistri.

pconfig.description: Configures platform features selected by eax, such as programming memory encryption keys for Intel MKTME, with parameters in rbx, rcx and rdx. Ring 0 only; ZF and eax report the status.
pconfig.operation: leaf(eax)(rbx, rcx, rdx); ZF, eax = status

pdep.description: BMI2: takes the low bits of the second operand and places them, in order, at the positions of the set bits in the mask (the third operand); other bits become zero. Slow on AMD before Zen 3.

pext.description: BMI2: gathers the bits of the second operand that sit at the set-bit positions of the mask (the third operand) and packs them into the low bits of the destination, zeroing the rest. Slow on AMD before Zen 3.

pextrb.description: Copies the byte chosen by the low 4 bits of the immediate from an xmm register to memory or to a general register, zero-extending it in the register case.

pextrd.description: Copies the 32-bit element chosen by the low 2 bits of the immediate from an xmm register to memory or a general register.

pextrq.description: Copies the 64-bit element chosen by bit 0 of the immediate from an xmm register to memory or a 64-bit general register.

pextrw.description: Copies the 16-bit element chosen by the immediate from an mm or xmm register to a general register (zero-extended) or, in the SSE4.1 form, to memory.

pf2id.description: AMD 3DNow!: converts the two floats of the source to signed 32-bit integers, truncating toward zero and clamping out-of-range values.

pf2iw.description: Extended 3DNow!: converts the two floats of the source to signed 16-bit integers with truncation and saturation, sign-extended into each 32-bit lane.

pfacc.description: AMD 3DNow!: adds the two floats within each operand; the destination's sum goes to the low lane and the source's to the high lane.

pfadd.description: AMD 3DNow!: adds the two pairs of floats lane by lane.

pfcmpeq.description: AMD 3DNow!: sets each 32-bit lane to all ones where the floats are equal and to zero otherwise.

pfcmpge.summary: 3DNow! packed float compare greater or equal
pfcmpge.description: AMD 3DNow!: sets each 32-bit lane to all ones where the destination float is greater than or equal to the source float, and to zero otherwise.

pfcmpgt.description: AMD 3DNow!: sets each 32-bit lane to all ones where the destination float is greater than the source float, and to zero otherwise.

pfmax.description: AMD 3DNow!: takes the larger float of each pair lane by lane.

pfmin.description: AMD 3DNow!: takes the smaller float of each pair lane by lane.

pfmul.description: AMD 3DNow!: multiplies the two pairs of floats lane by lane.

pfnacc.description: Extended 3DNow!: subtracts the high float from the low one within each operand; the destination's difference goes to the low lane and the source's to the high lane.

pfpnacc.description: Extended 3DNow!: the low lane gets the destination's low float minus its high float, the high lane gets the sum of the source's two floats. Useful in complex arithmetic.

pfrcp.description: AMD 3DNow!: computes an approximate reciprocal (about 14 bits) of the source's low float and writes it into both lanes. Refined with pfrcpit1 and pfrcpit2.

pfrcpit1.description: AMD 3DNow!: first Newton–Raphson step toward a full-precision reciprocal, combining the original value with the estimate from pfrcp; pfrcpit2 finishes it.

pfrcpit2.summary: 3DNow! reciprocal or square root, final step
pfrcpit2.description: AMD 3DNow!: final Newton–Raphson step that turns the intermediate from pfrcpit1 (or pfrsqit1) and the first estimate into a full-precision result.

pfrsqit1.description: AMD 3DNow!: first Newton–Raphson step toward a full-precision reciprocal square root, using the estimate from pfrsqrt; pfrcpit2 completes it.

pfrsqrt.description: AMD 3DNow!: computes an approximate 1/sqrt (about 15 bits) of the source's low float and writes it into both lanes.

pfsub.description: AMD 3DNow!: subtracts the source floats from the destination floats lane by lane.

pfsubr.description: AMD 3DNow!: subtracts the destination floats from the source floats lane by lane, the reverse of pfsub.

phaddd.description: Adds adjacent pairs of 32-bit elements; sums from the destination fill the low half of the result and sums from the source the high half. Wraps on overflow.

phaddsw.summary: Horizontal add words with signed saturation
phaddsw.description: Adds adjacent pairs of signed words, clamping each sum to -32768…32767; sums from the destination fill the low half and sums from the source the high half.

phaddw.description: Adds adjacent pairs of 16-bit elements; sums from the destination fill the low half and sums from the source the high half. Wraps on overflow.

phminposuw.summary: Horizontal minimum and position of unsigned words
phminposuw.description: Finds the smallest of the eight unsigned words in the source; the destination gets that value in word 0, its index in bits 16–18, and zeros elsewhere.

phsubd.description: Subtracts the upper element of each adjacent pair of 32-bit elements from the lower; differences from the destination fill the low half and from the source the high half.

phsubsw.summary: Horizontal subtract words with signed saturation
phsubsw.description: Subtracts the upper word of each adjacent pair from the lower with signed saturation; differences from the destination fill the low half and from the source the high half.

phsubw.description: Subtracts the upper word of each adjacent pair from the lower, wrapping on overflow; differences from the destination fill the low half and from the source the high half.

pi2fd.description: AMD 3DNow!: converts the two signed 32-bit integers of the source to floats.

pi2fw.description: Extended 3DNow!: converts the signed 16-bit integer in the low half of each 32-bit lane of the source to a float.

pinsrb.description: Writes a byte from memory or the low byte of a general register into the xmm byte chosen by the low 4 bits of the immediate, keeping the other bytes.

pinsrd.description: Writes a 32-bit value from memory or a general register into the xmm element chosen by the low 2 bits of the immediate, keeping the others.

pinsrq.description: Writes a 64-bit value from memory or a general register into the xmm half chosen by bit 0 of the immediate, keeping the other half.

pinsrw.description: Writes a 16-bit value from memory or the low word of a general register into the mm or xmm word chosen by the immediate, keeping the others.

pmaddubsw.summary: Multiply unsigned by signed bytes and add pairs
pmaddubsw.description: Multiplies each unsigned byte of the destination by the matching signed byte of the source, adds adjacent products and stores the sums as signed words with saturation. Note which operand is unsigned; used in image filters and int8 dot products.

pmaddwd.description: Multiplies signed words lane by lane and adds each adjacent pair of 32-bit products into a doubleword. The only overflow case, all four inputs -32768, wraps to 0x80000000. A building block for dot products.

pmaxsb.description: Keeps the larger signed byte of each pair lane by lane.

pmaxsd.description: Keeps the larger signed 32-bit element of each pair lane by lane.

pmaxsw.description: Keeps the larger signed 16-bit element of each pair lane by lane.

pmaxub.description: Keeps the larger unsigned byte of each pair lane by lane. Also used with pcmpeqb to build unsigned compares.

pmaxud.description: Keeps the larger unsigned 32-bit element of each pair lane by lane.

pmaxuw.description: Keeps the larger unsigned 16-bit element of each pair lane by lane.

pminsb.description: Compares the signed bytes of both operands lane by lane and keeps the smaller one in the destination. Compilers use it for vectorized min() and clamping of int8 data.

pminsd.description: Keeps the smaller of each pair of signed 32-bit lanes in the destination. Typical in vectorized min() over int arrays.

pminsw.description: Keeps the smaller of each pair of signed 16-bit lanes in the destination. Exists for both MMX (mm) and SSE2 (xmm) registers.

pminub.description: Keeps the smaller of each pair of unsigned bytes in the destination. Often used in string and image code, e.g. combined with pcmpeqb to find a zero byte in two vectors at once.

pminud.description: Keeps the smaller of each pair of unsigned 32-bit lanes in the destination. Used for vectorized min() over uint32 data.

pminuw.description: Keeps the smaller of each pair of unsigned 16-bit lanes in the destination. Also usable as an unsigned word compare when followed by pcmpeqw.

pmovmskb.description: Gathers the top bit of every byte of a vector register into the low bits of a general-purpose register and clears the rest. Paired with pcmpeqb it is the classic way to locate a matching byte in memchr and strlen.

pmovsxbd.description: Takes the four low signed bytes of the source and widens each to a signed 32-bit lane. The memory form reads only 32 bits.

pmovsxbq.description: Takes the two low signed bytes of the source and widens each to a signed 64-bit lane. The memory form reads only 16 bits.

pmovsxbw.description: Takes the eight low signed bytes of the source and widens each to a signed 16-bit lane. The memory form reads 64 bits.

pmovsxdq.description: Takes the two low signed 32-bit lanes of the source and widens each to a signed 64-bit lane. The memory form reads 64 bits.

pmovsxwd.description: Takes the four low signed 16-bit lanes of the source and widens each to a signed 32-bit lane. The memory form reads 64 bits.

pmovsxwq.description: Takes the two low signed 16-bit lanes of the source and widens each to a signed 64-bit lane. The memory form reads 32 bits.

pmovzxbd.description: Takes the four low bytes of the source and widens each to a 32-bit lane with zeros on top. The memory form reads only 32 bits.

pmovzxbq.description: Takes the two low bytes of the source and widens each to a 64-bit lane with zeros on top. The memory form reads only 16 bits.

pmovzxbw.description: Takes the eight low bytes of the source and widens each to a 16-bit lane with zeros on top. Common when unpacking 8-bit pixels before arithmetic.

pmovzxdq.description: Takes the two low 32-bit lanes of the source and widens each to a 64-bit lane with zeros on top. The memory form reads 64 bits.

pmovzxwd.description: Takes the four low 16-bit lanes of the source and widens each to a 32-bit lane with zeros on top. The memory form reads 64 bits.

pmovzxwq.description: Takes the two low 16-bit lanes of the source and widens each to a 64-bit lane with zeros on top. The memory form reads 32 bits.

pmuldq.description: Multiplies the signed 32-bit values in the even lanes (0 and 2) of both operands and stores the two full 64-bit products. The odd lanes are ignored.

pmulhrsw.summary: Multiply high with round and scale
pmulhrsw.description: Multiplies signed 16-bit lanes, then keeps bits 30:15 of each 32-bit product with rounding. This is a rounded Q15 fixed-point multiply, common in audio and video codecs.

pmulhrw.description: AMD 3DNow! form on mm registers: multiplies signed 16-bit lanes, adds 0x8000 for rounding and keeps the high 16 bits of each product. Not supported on current processors.

pmulhuw.summary: Multiply unsigned words, keep high half
pmulhuw.description: Multiplies unsigned 16-bit lanes and stores the upper 16 bits of each 32-bit product. Compilers use it to divide by a constant via a magic multiplier.

pmulhw.summary: Multiply signed words, keep high half
pmulhw.description: Multiplies signed 16-bit lanes and stores the upper 16 bits of each 32-bit product. Together with pmullw it yields full 32-bit products.

pmulld.description: Multiplies 32-bit lanes and keeps the low 32 bits of each product, which is the same for signed and unsigned values. The usual vector int multiply, though slower than most SIMD integer ops.

pmullw.description: Multiplies 16-bit lanes and keeps the low 16 bits of each product, valid for both signed and unsigned values. Exists for MMX and SSE2 registers.

pmuludq.description: Multiplies the unsigned 32-bit values in the even lanes of both operands and stores full 64-bit products. The MMX form multiplies just the low doublewords; widely used in big-number and hash code.

pop.description: Loads a value from the top of the stack into a register or memory and moves the stack pointer past it. In 64-bit mode the size is 8 bytes, or 2 with the 66 prefix; 32-bit pops do not exist there.

pop2.description: APX instruction that pops two 64-bit registers at once: the first operand from the top of the stack, the second from the next slot. The stack pointer must be 16-byte aligned, and both registers must differ.

pop2p.summary: Pop two registers with balance hint
pop2p.description: Same as pop2, plus a push-pop acceleration hint telling the processor this pop matches an earlier push2p, so it can forward the saved values faster. Used in function epilogues.

popal.description: Restores edi, esi, ebp, ebx, edx, ecx and eax from the stack in the reverse order of pushal; the saved esp value is skipped. Exists only outside 64-bit mode.

popaw.description: 16-bit variant of popal: restores di, si, bp, bx, dx, cx and ax from the stack, skipping the saved sp. Exists only outside 64-bit mode.

popcnt.description: Counts the set bits of the source and writes the count to the destination. ZF is set when the source is zero and the other flags are cleared; some Intel cores have a false dependency on the destination register.
popcnt.operation: dst = number of 1 bits in src

popf.description: Pops a 16-bit value into the low half of FLAGS. Bits such as IF and IOPL change only when the current privilege allows it; others are silently kept.

popfd.description: Pops a 32-bit value into EFLAGS, outside 64-bit mode. Privileged bits are changed only when allowed; old code toggles the ID bit with pushfd/popfd to detect cpuid.

popfq.description: Pops a 64-bit value into RFLAGS in 64-bit mode. Privileged bits such as IF and IOPL change only when the current privilege level allows it.

popp.description: A 64-bit pop with the APX push-pop acceleration hint, marking it as the match of an earlier pushp so the processor can forward the saved value. Behaves exactly like pop otherwise.

por.description: ORs the whole destination vector with the source, bit by bit. Exists for MMX and SSE2 registers; the result is the same for any element size.

prefetch.description: AMD 3DNow! hint that brings the cache line holding the address into the L1 data cache. It never faults and has no effect on program results.
prefetch.operation: hint: load line of [addr] into L1

prefetchit0.summary: Prefetch code into all cache levels
prefetchit0.description: Hints that the code at a RIP-relative address will run soon, so its line is fetched into all instruction cache levels. With a non-RIP-relative address it acts as a no-op.

prefetchit1.summary: Prefetch code into outer cache levels
prefetchit1.description: Like prefetchit0, but hints that the code is needed a little later, so it goes to level 2 and higher. Only RIP-relative addresses have an effect.

prefetchnta.description: Hints that data at the address will be used once, so it is fetched close to the core while disturbing the caches as little as possible. Typical in streaming copies of large buffers.

prefetchrst2.description: MOVRS hint that fetches a line into the outer cache levels and marks it as data that many cores will read, so it is kept in a shared state. Has no effect on program results.

prefetcht0.description: Hints that data at the address will be needed soon, so its line is fetched into every cache level including L1. Never faults, even on an invalid address.

prefetcht1.description: Hints that data at the address will be needed somewhat later, so its line is fetched into L2 and outer caches but not necessarily L1. Never faults.

prefetcht2.description: Hints that data at the address will be needed later still, so its line goes to the outermost cache levels. On many cores it behaves the same as prefetcht1.

prefetchw.description: Fetches the line holding the address and requests it in an exclusive state, so a following store does not need another coherence round trip. Common before atomic updates of a shared variable.
prefetchw.operation: hint: fetch line of [addr] for writing

prefetchwt1.description: Combines prefetchw and the T1 hint: the line is requested in an exclusive state and placed in L2 and outer caches. Supported only on a few Xeon Phi processors.
prefetchwt1.operation: hint: fetch line of [addr] for writing (T1)

psadbw.description: Computes the absolute difference of each pair of unsigned bytes and sums the eight results of every 64-bit half into its low 16 bits, zeroing the rest. Used in motion estimation and, against zero, to sum bytes fast.

pshufb.description: Builds each destination byte from the byte of the old destination chosen by the matching source byte; a source byte with its top bit set gives zero. A general table lookup used for byte reordering, nibble lookups and endianness swaps.

pshufd.description: Fills each of the four 32-bit destination lanes with a source lane chosen by a 2-bit field of the immediate. Also used to broadcast one lane or copy a register with reordering.

pshufhw.description: Reorders the four upper 16-bit lanes of the source using 2-bit fields of the immediate and copies the lower 64 bits unchanged.

pshuflw.description: Reorders the four lower 16-bit lanes of the source using 2-bit fields of the immediate and copies the upper 64 bits unchanged.

pshufw.description: Fills each of the four 16-bit lanes of an mm register with a source lane chosen by a 2-bit field of the immediate.

psignb.description: Negates, keeps or zeroes each signed byte of the destination depending on whether the matching source byte is negative, positive or zero.

psignd.description: Negates, keeps or zeroes each signed 32-bit lane of the destination depending on whether the matching source lane is negative, positive or zero.

psignw.description: Negates, keeps or zeroes each signed 16-bit lane of the destination depending on whether the matching source lane is negative, positive or zero.

pslld.description: Shifts every 32-bit lane left by the same count, from an immediate or the low 64 bits of a register or memory operand. A count above 31 clears the lanes.

pslldq.description: Shifts the whole 128-bit register left by an immediate number of bytes, filling with zero bytes. A count above 15 clears the register.

psllq.description: Shifts every 64-bit lane left by the same count, from an immediate or the low 64 bits of a register or memory operand. A count above 63 clears the lanes.

psllw.description: Shifts every 16-bit lane left by the same count, from an immediate or the low 64 bits of a register or memory operand. A count above 15 clears the lanes.

psmash.summary: Split a large RMP page entry
psmash.description: AMD SEV-SNP hypervisor instruction that splits the reverse-map entry of a 2 MB page into 512 entries for 4 KB pages, keeping their state. The page address is in rax and a status code is returned in eax.
psmash.operation: rmp[2MB page at rax] -> 512 x 4KB entries; eax = status

psrad.description: Shifts every signed 32-bit lane right by the same count, copying the sign bit into the vacated bits. A count above 31 fills each lane with its sign.

psraw.description: Shifts every signed 16-bit lane right by the same count, copying the sign bit into the vacated bits. A count above 15 fills each lane with its sign.

psrld.description: Shifts every 32-bit lane right by the same count, filling with zeros. The count comes from an immediate or the low 64 bits of the source; above 31 it clears the lanes.

psrldq.description: Shifts the whole 128-bit register right by an immediate number of bytes, filling with zero bytes. Often used to bring the upper half down for horizontal sums.

psrlq.description: Shifts every 64-bit lane right by the same count, filling with zeros. The count comes from an immediate or the low 64 bits of the source; above 63 it clears the lanes.

psrlw.description: Shifts every 16-bit lane right by the same count, filling with zeros. The count comes from an immediate or the low 64 bits of the source; above 15 it clears the lanes.

psubb.description: Subtracts the source bytes from the destination bytes lane by lane, wrapping around on overflow. Works the same for signed and unsigned data.

psubd.description: Subtracts the source 32-bit lanes from the destination lanes, wrapping around on overflow.

psubq.description: Subtracts the source 64-bit lanes from the destination lanes, wrapping around on overflow. The MMX form subtracts a single quadword.

psubsb.summary: Packed signed byte subtract with saturation
psubsb.description: Subtracts signed bytes lane by lane and clamps each result to the range -128..127 instead of wrapping.

psubsw.summary: Packed signed word subtract with saturation
psubsw.description: Subtracts signed 16-bit lanes and clamps each result to the range -32768..32767 instead of wrapping. Common in audio sample processing.

psubusb.summary: Packed unsigned byte subtract with saturation
psubusb.description: Subtracts unsigned bytes lane by lane, giving 0 where the result would be negative. Also used to compute unsigned a > b tests and absolute differences.

psubusw.summary: Packed unsigned word subtract with saturation
psubusw.description: Subtracts unsigned 16-bit lanes, giving 0 where the result would be negative instead of wrapping.

psubw.description: Subtracts the source 16-bit lanes from the destination lanes, wrapping around on overflow. Works the same for signed and unsigned data.

pswapd.description: AMD 3DNow! extension: writes the two 32-bit halves of the source into the mm destination in swapped order. Not supported on current processors.

ptest.description: Sets ZF when the AND of both operands is all zeros and CF when the second operand has no bits outside the first; neither register changes. Used to branch on whether a vector is zero or a mask is covered.

ptwrite.summary: Write value to the processor trace
ptwrite.description: Inserts the 32- or 64-bit operand into the Intel Processor Trace stream as a packet, if tracing with PTWRITE is enabled. Lets programs annotate traces with their own values; otherwise it does nothing.

punpckhbw.description: Interleaves the bytes of the upper halves of the destination and source: destination byte, then source byte. With a zeroed source it zero-extends bytes to words.

punpckhdq.description: Interleaves the 32-bit lanes of the upper halves of the destination and source, destination lane first.

punpckhqdq.description: Puts the upper 64 bits of the destination in the low half and the upper 64 bits of the source in the high half.

punpckhwd.description: Interleaves the 16-bit lanes of the upper halves of the destination and source, destination lane first. With a zeroed or sign mask source it widens words to doublewords.

punpcklbw.description: Interleaves the bytes of the lower halves of the destination and source: destination byte, then source byte. With a zeroed source it is the classic way to zero-extend bytes to words.

punpckldq.description: Interleaves the 32-bit lanes of the lower halves of the destination and source, destination lane first.

punpcklqdq.description: Keeps the low 64 bits of the destination and puts the low 64 bits of the source above them. Often used to combine two 64-bit values into one register.

punpcklwd.description: Interleaves the 16-bit lanes of the lower halves of the destination and source, destination lane first.

push.description: Moves the stack pointer down and stores a register, memory value or sign-extended immediate at the new top. In 64-bit mode it pushes 8 bytes, or 2 with the 66 prefix.

push2.description: APX instruction that pushes two 64-bit registers at once, the first operand first, as two pushes would. The stack pointer must be 16-byte aligned; pop2 with the registers listed in reverse order undoes it.

push2p.summary: Push two registers with balance hint
push2p.description: Same as push2, plus a push-pop acceleration hint that a matching pop2p will restore these values. Used in function prologues.

pushal.description: Pushes eax, ecx, edx, ebx, the original esp, ebp, esi and edi in that order. Exists only outside 64-bit mode.
pushal.operation: push eax, ecx, edx, ebx, esp0, ebp, esi, edi

pushaw.description: 16-bit variant of pushal: pushes ax, cx, dx, bx, the original sp, bp, si and di. Exists only outside 64-bit mode.
pushaw.operation: push ax, cx, dx, bx, sp0, bp, si, di

pushf.description: Pushes the low 16 bits of the flags register onto the stack. Mostly seen in 16-bit code.

pushfd.description: Pushes EFLAGS onto the stack outside 64-bit mode, with the VM and RF bits cleared in the stored copy. Often paired with popfd to save or inspect flags.

pushfq.description: Pushes RFLAGS onto the stack in 64-bit mode, with the VM and RF bits cleared in the stored copy. Used to save flags around code that must restore them.

pushp.description: A 64-bit push with the APX push-pop acceleration hint, saying a matching popp will restore the value. Behaves exactly like push otherwise.

pvalidate.description: Run inside an AMD SEV-SNP guest to mark a private page as validated or not: rax holds the guest virtual address, ecx the page size and edx the new state. CF is set when the state did not change and eax gets a status code.

pxor.description: XORs the whole destination vector with the source, bit by bit. pxor of a register with itself is the standard way to zero it.

rcl.description: Rotates the operand and CF together left, as one value one bit wider than the operand. The count comes from 1, cl or an immediate; used for multi-word shifts.

rcpps.description: Computes a fast approximation of 1/x for each single-precision lane, with a relative error up to about 1.5 * 2^-12. Usually refined with a Newton-Raphson step.

rcpss.description: Computes a fast approximation of 1/x for the low single-precision value; the upper three lanes of the destination stay unchanged.

rcr.description: Rotates the operand and CF together right, as one value one bit wider than the operand. Paired with shr or sar to shift multi-word numbers right.

rdfsbase.description: Copies the base address of the FS segment into a 32- or 64-bit register. Works in user mode only if the OS has enabled FSGSBASE; FS usually points at thread-local storage.

rdgsbase.description: Copies the base address of the GS segment into a 32- or 64-bit register. Works in user mode only if the OS has enabled FSGSBASE; on Windows GS points at the thread block.

rdmsr.description: Reads the MSR numbered by ecx into edx:eax; the newer form takes the MSR number as an immediate and writes a 64-bit register. Kernel only: it faults at user privilege.

rdmsrlist.description: Reads several MSRs in one go: rsi points to a table of MSR numbers, rdi to the output table and rcx is a bitmask of entries to read, cleared bit by bit as it goes. Kernel only, and interruptible.
rdmsrlist.operation: for each set bit i of rcx: [rdi+8i] = msr[[rsi+8i]]; clear bit i

rdpid.description: Copies the IA32_TSC_AUX value, which operating systems set to the current CPU number, into a register. A cheaper alternative to rdtscp for finding which core the thread runs on.

rdpkru.description: Copies the PKRU register, which holds access and write disable bits for each memory protection key, into eax and clears edx. ecx must be zero.

rdpmc.description: Reads the performance-monitoring counter selected by ecx into edx:eax. User code may run it only when the OS allows it via CR4.PCE.

rdpru.description: AMD instruction that reads a register chosen by ecx, such as MPERF (0) or APERF (1), into edx:eax, even from user mode when the OS permits it.

rdrand.description: Writes a random value from the on-chip generator into the register and sets CF on success. When no value is ready CF is cleared and the register is zeroed, so callers loop until CF is 1.
rdrand.operation: if (ready) { dst = random; CF = 1 } else { dst = 0; CF = 0 }

rdseed.description: Like rdrand, but returns bits closer to the hardware entropy source, meant for seeding other generators. It fails (CF = 0) more often and needs a retry loop.
rdseed.operation: if (ready) { dst = seed; CF = 1 } else { dst = 0; CF = 0 }

rdsspd.description: Copies the low 32 bits of the CET shadow stack pointer into a register. When shadow stacks are off it does nothing, so code zeroes the register first to detect that.

rdsspq.description: Copies the CET shadow stack pointer into a 64-bit register. When shadow stacks are off it does nothing, so a zeroed register staying zero means they are disabled.

rdtsc.description: Loads the 64-bit time-stamp counter into edx:eax. It does not wait for earlier instructions, so timing code puts lfence or cpuid around it.

rdtscp.summary: Read time-stamp counter and processor ID
rdtscp.description: Loads the time-stamp counter into edx:eax and IA32_TSC_AUX (usually the CPU number) into ecx, after all earlier instructions have executed. Later instructions may still start before it.

rep.description: Repeats the following string instruction rcx times, decrementing rcx each step; with cmps or scas it also stops when ZF becomes 0 (repe). LLVM shows it alone when it does not belong to a string instruction, as in the old rep ret idiom.

repne.description: Repeats a following cmps or scas while rcx is non-zero and ZF stays 0, such as repne scasb to find a byte. LLVM shows it alone when the next instruction is not a string operation.

ret.description: Pops the return address and jumps to it. The imm16 form also releases that many extra bytes of arguments from the stack, as in the stdcall convention.

retf.description: Pops both the return address and the code segment selector, returning to a different segment or privilege level. The imm16 form also releases argument bytes.
retf.operation: rip = pop; cs = pop; rsp += imm16

retfq.description: Far return that pops a 64-bit return address and a 64-bit slot holding the code segment selector. Used, for example, to switch between 64-bit and 32-bit code segments.
retfq.operation: rip = pop64; cs = pop64; rsp += imm16

rex64.description: A REX prefix with the W bit that LLVM prints on its own line because it does not change the instruction after it. Compilers emit such prefixes as padding.

rmpadjust.description: Run inside an AMD SEV-SNP guest to set the access rights of a page for a less privileged VMPL, or to turn a page into a VM save area. Status comes back in eax.

rmpquery.description: Lets an AMD SEV-SNP guest read the permissions a VMPL has on a page, as recorded in the reverse map table. Results come back in registers.

rmpupdate.description: AMD SEV-SNP hypervisor instruction that writes the reverse-map entry of a system physical page, assigning it to a guest or back to the host. rax holds the page address, rcx points to the new entry.

rol.description: Rotates the bits of the operand left; bits leaving the top re-enter at the bottom and the last one is copied into CF. Compilers emit it for rotate idioms in hashes and ciphers.

ror.description: Rotates the bits of the operand right; bits leaving the bottom re-enter at the top and the last one is copied into CF. ror by 8 on a 16-bit value swaps its bytes.

rorx.description: BMI2 rotate: writes the source rotated right by an immediate into a separate destination and leaves all flags alone. Handy in hash loops where flags must survive.

roundpd.description: Rounds each double-precision lane to an integral value, still in floating point. The immediate picks the mode (nearest, down, up, toward zero, or the MXCSR mode) and can suppress the inexact exception.

roundps.description: Rounds each single-precision lane to an integral value, still in floating point; the immediate picks the rounding mode. Compilers use it for floorf, ceilf and truncf on vectors.

roundsd.description: Rounds the low double of the source to an integral value with the mode from the immediate; the upper half of the destination is kept. Compilers emit it for floor, ceil and trunc.
roundsd.operation: dst[0] = round(src[0], imm mode); dst[1] unchanged

roundss.description: Rounds the low single of the source to an integral value with the mode from the immediate; the upper three lanes of the destination are kept.
roundss.operation: dst[0] = round(src[0], imm mode); dst[1..3] unchanged

rsm.description: Leaves System Management Mode by restoring the processor state saved on entry and returning to the interrupted program. Valid only inside SMM firmware.
rsm.operation: restore state from SMRAM; leave SMM

rsqrtps.description: Computes a fast approximation of 1/sqrt(x) for each single-precision lane, with about 12 bits of precision. Typical in graphics code, usually followed by a Newton-Raphson step.

rsqrtss.description: Computes a fast approximation of 1/sqrt(x) for the low single-precision value; the upper three lanes of the destination stay unchanged.

rstorssp.description: Switches to another CET shadow stack by checking the restore token at the memory address and loading the shadow stack pointer from it. Used by context-switching code such as user-level threads.
rstorssp.operation: check token at [m]; ssp = m; mark token used

sahf.description: Copies bits of AH into SF, ZF, AF, PF and CF. Old code pairs it with fnstsw ax to branch on x87 comparison results.

salc.description: Undocumented one-byte instruction that sets AL to 0xFF when CF is 1 and to 0 otherwise, without changing flags. Not available in 64-bit mode.

sar.description: Shifts the operand right, copying the sign bit into the vacated top bits; the last bit shifted out goes to CF. Signed division by a power of two rounds toward minus infinity with it, so compilers add a correction.
sar.operation: dst = dst >> count  (signed); CF = last bit out

sarx.description: BMI2 shift: writes the first source shifted right arithmetically by the count in the last operand (masked to 5 or 6 bits) into a separate destination, leaving flags unchanged.

saveprevssp.description: After rstorssp switched shadow stacks, writes a restore token for the previous shadow stack onto it, so a later rstorssp can switch back.
saveprevssp.operation: push restore token to previous shadow stack

sbb.description: Subtracts the source and the carry flag from the destination. Used for multi-word subtraction, and sbb reg, reg turns CF into 0 or all ones.

scasb.description: Compares al with the byte at [rdi], sets flags as cmp does, then moves rdi forward or back by one according to DF. With repne it searches for a byte, as in old strlen code.

scasd.description: Compares eax with the doubleword at [rdi], sets flags as cmp does, then moves rdi by 4 according to DF. Usually combined with repe or repne.

scasq.description: Compares rax with the quadword at [rdi], sets flags as cmp does, then moves rdi by 8 according to DF. 64-bit mode only.

scasw.description: Compares ax with the word at [rdi], sets flags as cmp does, then moves rdi by 2 according to DF. Usually combined with repe or repne.

seamcall.description: Intel TDX instruction a hypervisor uses to enter the SEAM module (the TDX module) and request a service such as creating or running a trust domain. rax selects the function.
seamcall.operation: enter SEAM mode; call TDX module function rax

seamops.description: Intel TDX instruction available only inside the TDX module, giving it special services such as reading SEAM capabilities or producing attestation reports. rax selects the leaf.

seamret.description: Intel TDX instruction the TDX module executes to leave SEAM mode and return to the hypervisor that called it with seamcall.
seamret.operation: leave SEAM mode; return to VMM

senduipi.description: Sends a user interrupt to another thread directly from user mode, using the register as an index into the user-interrupt target table set up by the OS.

serialize.description: Waits until all earlier instructions have completed and stores have drained before fetching the next one. A cheaper alternative to cpuid for that purpose, with no register side effects.
serialize.operation: wait for all prior work; refetch

setcc.description: Writes 1 to a byte register or memory byte when the condition on the flags holds and 0 otherwise, e.g. sete, setl, setb. Compilers use it to turn comparisons into bool values, usually followed by movzx.

setssbsy.description: Kernel instruction for CET supervisor shadow stacks: marks the token at the address in IA32_PL0_SSP busy and loads it as the shadow stack pointer.
setssbsy.operation: check token at PL0_SSP; set busy; ssp = PL0_SSP

setzucc.summary: Set register if condition, zero upper
setzucc.description: APX form of setcc that writes 1 or 0 by the condition and zeroes the rest of the full register, so no extra movzx is needed.

sfence.description: Makes all earlier stores visible before any later store. Needed after non-temporal stores such as movntdq, which are otherwise weakly ordered.
sfence.operation: order all prior stores before later stores

sgdt.description: Writes the limit and base address of the global descriptor table register to memory. Faults in user mode when the OS enables UMIP.

sgdtd.description: 32-bit operand form of sgdt: stores the 16-bit limit and 32-bit base of the global descriptor table register.

sgdtw.description: 16-bit operand form of sgdt: stores the limit and base of the global descriptor table register; old processors filled the top base byte differently.

sha1msg1.description: Does the first, XOR-based part of computing the next four SHA-1 message words from the previous ones. Its result is finished by sha1msg2.

sha1msg2.description: Completes the next four SHA-1 message words, including the rotate by one, from the output of sha1msg1 and earlier words.

sha1nexte.description: Derives the SHA-1 state variable E for the next four rounds by rotating the top doubleword of the destination left by 30 and adding it to the source's top doubleword.

sha1rnds4.description: Performs four SHA-1 rounds on the A..D state in the destination using message words plus E from the source. The immediate (0–3) selects the round function and constant.

sha256msg1.description: Computes the sigma0 part of the next four SHA-256 message words from the previous ones; sha256msg2 finishes them.

sha256msg2.description: Completes the next four SHA-256 message words by adding the sigma1 terms to the intermediate result of sha256msg1.

sha256rnds2.description: Performs two SHA-256 rounds on half of the state in the destination using the other half from the source and two pre-added message-plus-constant words from the implicit xmm0.

shl.description: Shifts the operand left, filling with zeros; the last bit shifted out goes to CF. The count is masked to 5 bits (6 for 64-bit), and compilers use it to multiply by powers of two.
shl.operation: dst = dst << (count & mask); CF = last bit out

shld.description: Shifts the destination left and fills the vacated low bits with the top bits of the second operand, which itself is unchanged. Used for multi-word shifts; APX adds a form with a new destination.

shlx.description: BMI2 shift: writes the first source shifted left by the count in the last operand (masked to 5 or 6 bits) into a separate destination, leaving flags unchanged.

shr.description: Shifts the operand right, filling with zeros; the last bit shifted out goes to CF. Compilers use it for unsigned division by powers of two.
shr.operation: dst = dst >> (count & mask)  (unsigned); CF = last bit out

shrd.description: Shifts the destination right and fills the vacated high bits with the low bits of the second operand, which itself is unchanged. Used for multi-word shifts; APX adds a form with a new destination.

shrx.description: BMI2 shift: writes the first source shifted right with zero fill by the count in the last operand (masked to 5 or 6 bits) into a separate destination, leaving flags unchanged.

shufpd.description: Builds the low double from the destination and the high double from the source, each chosen by one immediate bit.

shufps.description: Builds the two low lanes from the destination and the two high lanes from the source, each chosen by a 2-bit field of the immediate. With the same register twice it acts as a general four-lane shuffle.
shufps.operation: dst[0,1] = a[sel0], a[sel1]; dst[2,3] = b[sel2], b[sel3]

sidt.description: Writes the limit and base address of the interrupt descriptor table register to memory. Faults in user mode when the OS enables UMIP; once used to detect virtual machines.

sidtd.description: 32-bit operand form of sidt: stores the 16-bit limit and 32-bit base of the interrupt descriptor table register.

sidtw.description: 16-bit operand form of sidt: stores the limit and base of the interrupt descriptor table register, mainly found in real-mode and 16-bit code.

skinit.description: AMD SVM instruction that reinitializes the processor into a known state, measures the secure loader block whose physical address is in eax into the TPM and jumps into it. Kernel only.
skinit.operation: reset to secure state; measure SLB at eax; jump to it

sldt.description: Stores the segment selector of the local descriptor table register into a register or 16-bit memory. Faults in user mode when the OS enables UMIP.

slwpcb.description: AMD Lightweight Profiling instruction that writes the address of the current LWP control block into a register, or 0 when profiling is off. Not supported on current AMD processors.

smsw.description: Stores the low 16 bits of CR0 to memory; the register forms write more of CR0. A leftover from the 286, it faults in user mode when the OS enables UMIP.

sqrtpd.description: Computes the correctly rounded square root of each double-precision lane of the source. Negative inputs give NaN.

sqrtps.description: Takes the square root of each of the four float lanes of the source and writes the results to the destination xmm register. Rounding follows MXCSR; a negative input gives the default NaN.

sqrtsd.description: Writes the square root of the low double of the source into the low lane of the destination; the upper 64 bits of the destination are kept. Compilers emit it for sqrt() on double.

sqrtss.description: Writes the square root of the low float of the source into the low lane of the destination, leaving the other three lanes unchanged. Used for sqrtf().

ss.description: Makes the memory operand of the next instruction use the SS segment. In 64-bit mode the override has no effect on addressing; LLVM prints it on its own when it cannot attach it to an operand.

stac.description: Sets EFLAGS.AC, which with SMAP enabled lets the kernel touch user-mode pages temporarily. Kernels pair it with clac around copies to and from user memory; allowed only at ring 0.

stc.description: Sets CF to 1 and leaves the other flags alone. Often used to return an error indication in CF or before adc/sbb chains.

std.description: Sets DF so that string instructions (movs, stos, cmps…) step addresses downward. The ABI requires DF to be clear at calls and returns, so code that uses std follows it with cld.

stgi.description: AMD SVM instruction that sets the global interrupt flag, allowing interrupts and other events to be delivered again after clgi. Used by hypervisors around VM entry; privileged.

sti.description: Sets IF so maskable hardware interrupts are accepted; interrupts are held off until after the next instruction, which lets sti; hlt or sti; ret run atomically. Needs sufficient privilege (IOPL).

stmxcsr.description: Writes the 32-bit MXCSR control and status register (SSE rounding mode, exception masks and sticky flags) to memory. Used to save or inspect the floating-point environment.

stosb.description: Writes AL to [rdi] and moves rdi by 1 (up, or down when DF is set). With the rep prefix it fills rcx bytes, which is how memset is often inlined.

stosd.description: Writes EAX to [rdi] and moves rdi by 4 in the direction given by DF. With rep it fills rcx doublewords.

stosq.description: Writes RAX to [rdi] and moves rdi by 8 in the direction given by DF. rep stosq is a common way to zero large blocks, for example stack frames.

stosw.description: Writes AX to [rdi] and moves rdi by 2 in the direction given by DF. With rep it fills rcx 16-bit words.

str.description: Copies the segment selector held in the task register (TR) to a register or memory. Used by operating systems; with UMIP enabled it faults outside ring 0.

sttilecfg.description: Writes the current AMX tile configuration (palette, rows and bytes per row of each tile) as a 64-byte block to memory. If no configuration is active the block is zeroed.

stui.description: Sets the user interrupt flag (UIF) so pending user interrupts can be delivered to the current thread. Part of Intel user interrupts (UINTR); clui clears the flag.

sub.description: Subtracts the source from the destination and stores the difference in the destination, setting CF on unsigned borrow and OF on signed overflow. An immediate is sign-extended to the operand size.

subpd.description: Subtracts each of the two doubles of the source from the matching lane of the destination xmm register and keeps the results in the destination.

subps.description: Subtracts each of the four floats of the source from the matching lane of the destination xmm register and keeps the results in the destination.

subsd.description: Subtracts the low double of the source from the low double of the destination; the upper half of the destination is kept. The usual code for a - b on doubles.

subss.description: Subtracts the low float of the source from the low float of the destination, leaving the other three lanes unchanged. The usual code for a - b on floats.

swapgs.description: Exchanges the current GS base with the value in the IA32_KERNEL_GS_BASE MSR. Kernels run it on entry from and exit to user mode to reach per-CPU data; ring 0 only.

syscall.description: Enters the kernel at the address in the LSTAR MSR, saving the return address in rcx and RFLAGS in r11. The standard way 64-bit Linux and macOS programs make system calls.
syscall.operation: rcx = rip; r11 = rflags; rip = LSTAR; CPL = 0

sysenter.description: Switches to ring 0 at the entry point and stack given by the SYSENTER MSRs, without saving a return address; the caller arranges that. Mostly used by 32-bit code on Intel processors.

sysexit.description: Returns from a sysenter handler to ring 3, taking the return address from edx and the user stack from ecx. Privileged; the 32-bit operand form.

sysexitq.summary: Return from fast system call to 64-bit code
sysexitq.description: The REX.W form of sysexit: returns to 64-bit user mode with rip taken from rdx and rsp from rcx. Ring 0 only.

sysret.description: Returns from a syscall handler to user mode, restoring the instruction pointer from ecx and RFLAGS from r11. Without REX.W it returns to 32-bit compatibility mode; privileged.

sysretq.summary: Return from system call to 64-bit code
sysretq.description: The REX.W form of sysret that 64-bit kernels use: rip = rcx, RFLAGS = r11, back to ring 3. A non-canonical rcx is a known pitfall, so kernels check it first.

t1mskc.description: AMD TBM: produces a value whose bits are set everywhere except at the lowest clear bit of the source, i.e. the inverted mask of the trailing ones plus one. Sets flags from the result; CF when the source is all ones.

t2rpntlvwz0.summary: Load tile pair with VNNI word transpose (z0)
t2rpntlvwz0.description: AMX-TRANSPOSE: reads a block of 16-bit elements from memory (base plus stride) and writes it into a pair of tiles rearranged into the VNNI word layout used by the dot-product instructions. The z0 and z1 forms differ in how rows are paired.

t2rpntlvwz0rs.summary: Load tile pair, VNNI transpose, read-shared (z0)
t2rpntlvwz0rs.description: Like t2rpntlvwz0, but with the AMX-MOVRS read-shared hint: the data is expected to be read by several cores, so the cache line is fetched without taking ownership.

t2rpntlvwz0rst1.summary: Load tile pair, VNNI, read-shared, low reuse (z0)
t2rpntlvwz0rst1.description: t2rpntlvwz0 with both the read-shared hint and the T1 hint that the data will not be reused much, so it should not displace other cache contents.

t2rpntlvwz0t1.summary: Load tile pair, VNNI transpose, low reuse (z0)
t2rpntlvwz0t1.description: t2rpntlvwz0 with the T1 hint that the loaded data will not be reused much, so the processor may avoid keeping it in the caches.

t2rpntlvwz1.summary: Load tile pair with VNNI word transpose (z1)
t2rpntlvwz1.description: AMX-TRANSPOSE: the z1 variant of the paired transposing tile load; it fills two tiles with 16-bit data from memory in VNNI word layout, pairing the rows differently from z0.

t2rpntlvwz1rs.summary: Load tile pair, VNNI transpose, read-shared (z1)
t2rpntlvwz1rs.description: Like t2rpntlvwz1, but with the AMX-MOVRS read-shared hint, telling the processor the data is likely read by other cores as well.

t2rpntlvwz1rst1.summary: Load tile pair, VNNI, read-shared, low reuse (z1)
t2rpntlvwz1rst1.description: t2rpntlvwz1 with both the read-shared hint and the T1 hint that the data will see little reuse.

t2rpntlvwz1t1.summary: Load tile pair, VNNI transpose, low reuse (z1)
t2rpntlvwz1t1.description: t2rpntlvwz1 with the T1 hint that the loaded data will not be reused much, so it need not stay in the caches.

tcmmimfp16ps.description: AMX-COMPLEX: treats the two source tiles as matrices of FP16 complex numbers (real, imaginary pairs), multiplies them and adds the imaginary part of each product to the FP32 accumulator tile.

tcmmrlfp16ps.description: AMX-COMPLEX: multiplies two tiles of FP16 complex numbers and adds the real part of each product (re·re − im·im) to the FP32 accumulator tile.

tconjtcmmimfp16ps.description: AMX-COMPLEX with AMX-TRANSPOSE: uses the conjugate transpose of the first source tile, multiplies it by the second FP16 complex tile and accumulates the imaginary parts into the FP32 destination.

tconjtfp16.description: Writes the conjugate transpose of a tile of FP16 complex numbers to the destination tile: rows become columns and every imaginary part changes sign.

tcvtrowd2ps.summary: Convert tile row of int32 to float
tcvtrowd2ps.description: AMX-AVX512: takes one row of the source tile, chosen by a register or immediate, treats it as signed 32-bit integers and writes them converted to FP32 into a zmm register.

tcvtrowps2bf16h.summary: Convert tile row of float to BF16 (high halves)
tcvtrowps2bf16h.description: AMX-AVX512: converts one FP32 row of a tile to BF16 and places each result in the upper 16 bits of the matching 32-bit lane of the zmm destination, zeroing the lower 16 bits.

tcvtrowps2bf16l.summary: Convert tile row of float to BF16 (low halves)
tcvtrowps2bf16l.description: AMX-AVX512: converts one FP32 row of a tile to BF16 and places each result in the lower 16 bits of the matching 32-bit lane of the zmm destination, zeroing the upper 16 bits.

tcvtrowps2phh.summary: Convert tile row of float to FP16 (high halves)
tcvtrowps2phh.description: AMX-AVX512: converts one FP32 row of a tile to FP16 and puts each result in the upper 16 bits of the matching 32-bit lane of the zmm destination, with the lower 16 bits zeroed.

tcvtrowps2phl.summary: Convert tile row of float to FP16 (low halves)
tcvtrowps2phl.description: AMX-AVX512: converts one FP32 row of a tile to FP16 and puts each result in the lower 16 bits of the matching 32-bit lane of the zmm destination, with the upper 16 bits zeroed.

tdcall.description: Intel TDX: a trust-domain guest uses it to request a service from the TDX module, with the function number in rax and arguments in other registers. Found only in confidential-VM guest kernels.

tdpbf16ps.summary: Tile dot product of BF16 pairs
tdpbf16ps.description: AMX-BF16: for each output element multiplies pairs of BF16 values from the two source tiles and adds both products to the FP32 accumulator tile. The core operation of AMX matrix multiply for bfloat16.

tdpbf8ps.summary: Tile dot product of BF8 × BF8
tdpbf8ps.description: AMX-FP8: multiplies groups of four 8-bit floats in E5M2 (BF8) format from both source tiles and accumulates the sums into the FP32 destination tile.

tdpbhf8ps.summary: Tile dot product of BF8 × HF8
tdpbhf8ps.description: AMX-FP8: like tdpbf8ps, but the first source tile holds E5M2 (BF8) values and the second holds E4M3 (HF8) values; products are summed into FP32.

tdpbssd.summary: Tile dot product of signed × signed bytes
tdpbssd.description: AMX-INT8: multiplies groups of four signed bytes from the first tile by four signed bytes from the second and adds the sums to the 32-bit integer accumulator tile, wrapping on overflow.

tdpbsud.summary: Tile dot product of signed × unsigned bytes
tdpbsud.description: AMX-INT8: the first tile holds signed bytes and the second unsigned bytes; groups of four products are summed into the int32 accumulator tile without saturation.

tdpbusd.summary: Tile dot product of unsigned × signed bytes
tdpbusd.description: AMX-INT8: the first tile holds unsigned bytes and the second signed bytes; groups of four products are summed into the int32 accumulator tile without saturation. The usual form for quantized inference.

tdpbuud.summary: Tile dot product of unsigned × unsigned bytes
tdpbuud.description: AMX-INT8: multiplies groups of four unsigned bytes from both tiles and adds the sums to the 32-bit accumulator tile, wrapping on overflow.

tdpfp16ps.summary: Tile dot product of FP16 pairs
tdpfp16ps.description: AMX-FP16: multiplies pairs of half-precision values from the two source tiles and adds both products to the FP32 accumulator tile.

tdphbf8ps.summary: Tile dot product of HF8 × BF8
tdphbf8ps.description: AMX-FP8: the first source tile holds E4M3 (HF8) values and the second E5M2 (BF8) values; groups of four products are accumulated into the FP32 destination.

tdphf8ps.summary: Tile dot product of HF8 × HF8
tdphf8ps.description: AMX-FP8: multiplies groups of four E4M3 (HF8) values from both source tiles and accumulates the sums into the FP32 destination tile.

test.description: ANDs the two operands and sets SF, ZF and PF from the result, clearing CF and OF; neither operand changes. test reg, reg is the idiomatic check for zero or negative before a jcc.

testui.description: UINTR: copies the user interrupt flag (UIF) into CF and clears the other arithmetic flags, so code can learn whether user interrupts are currently enabled.

tileloadd.description: AMX: fills a tile row by row from memory; the SIB base gives the start address and the index register gives the byte stride between rows. Row count and width come from the tile configuration.

tileloaddrs.description: tileloadd with the AMX-MOVRS read-shared hint: the data is expected to be read by several cores, so it is fetched without taking exclusive ownership of the cache lines.

tileloaddrst1.description: tileloadd with both the read-shared hint and the T1 hint that the data will see little reuse and should not crowd the caches.

tileloaddt1.summary: Load tile from memory, low reuse
tileloaddt1.description: tileloadd with the T1 hint that the loaded data will not be reused much, so the processor may keep it out of the caches.

tilemovrow.summary: Move tile row to vector register
tilemovrow.description: AMX-AVX512: copies one row of a tile, selected by a register or immediate, into a zmm register without conversion.

tilerelease.description: Returns all AMX tiles and the tile configuration to their initial state, so the operating system no longer has to save them. Compilers emit it at the end of functions that used AMX.

tilestored.description: AMX: writes a tile row by row to memory, starting at the SIB base address with the index register as the byte stride between rows.

tilezero.description: Sets every byte of the given AMX tile to zero, typically to clear an accumulator before a series of dot-product instructions.

tlbsync.description: AMD: waits until every invlpgb previously issued by this processor has completed on all other processors. Used by kernels after broadcast TLB shootdowns; privileged.

tmmultf32ps.summary: Tile matrix multiply with TF32 inputs
tmmultf32ps.description: AMX-TF32: multiplies two FP32 tiles as matrices, rounding the inputs to TF32 precision for the products, and adds the result to the FP32 accumulator tile.

tpause.description: Puts the core into a light (C0.1) or deeper (C0.2) wait state, chosen by bit 0 of the register, until the TSC reaches the deadline in edx:eax. CF is set if the OS-imposed time limit ended the wait early.

ttcmmimfp16ps.summary: Tile transpose and complex multiply, imaginary
ttcmmimfp16ps.description: AMX-COMPLEX with AMX-TRANSPOSE: transposes the first FP16 complex tile (without conjugating), multiplies it by the second and accumulates the imaginary parts into the FP32 destination.

ttcmmrlfp16ps.summary: Tile transpose and complex multiply, real
ttcmmrlfp16ps.description: AMX-COMPLEX with AMX-TRANSPOSE: transposes the first FP16 complex tile, multiplies it by the second and accumulates the real parts into the FP32 destination.

ttdpbf16ps.summary: Tile transpose and BF16 dot product
ttdpbf16ps.description: AMX-TRANSPOSE: like tdpbf16ps, but the first source tile is used transposed, which saves a separate transpose step when multiplying by a transposed matrix.

ttdpfp16ps.summary: Tile transpose and FP16 dot product
ttdpfp16ps.description: AMX-TRANSPOSE: like tdpfp16ps, but the first source tile is used transposed before the FP16 pair products are accumulated into FP32.

ttmmultf32ps.summary: Tile transpose and TF32 matrix multiply
ttmmultf32ps.description: AMX-TF32 with AMX-TRANSPOSE: like tmmultf32ps, but the first source tile is used transposed.

ttransposed.description: AMX-TRANSPOSE: writes the transpose of a tile of 32-bit elements to the destination tile, turning rows into columns.

tzcnt.description: Counts the zero bits below the lowest set bit of the source; a zero source gives the operand width and sets CF. On processors without BMI the same bytes run as bsf, which leaves the result undefined for zero.

tzmsk.description: AMD TBM: sets the bits that are below the lowest set bit of the source and clears all others, giving a mask of its trailing zeros. CF is set when the source is zero.

ucomisd.description: Compares the low doubles and sets ZF, PF and CF (PF=1 means unordered, a NaN was involved); OF, SF and AF are cleared. Unlike comisd it raises invalid only for signalling NaNs. Followed by ja/jb-style unsigned jumps.

ucomiss.description: Compares the low floats and sets ZF, PF and CF, with PF=1 for unordered (NaN); OF, SF and AF are cleared. Raises invalid only for signalling NaNs; the usual compiler choice for float == and <.

ud1.description: Always raises the invalid-opcode exception (#UD). Unlike ud2 it has a ModRM byte, so the operands can carry extra data; Clang uses it for trap codes such as UBSan checks.

ud2.description: Always raises the invalid-opcode exception (#UD). Compilers place it after noreturn calls and for __builtin_trap(), so reaching it means a crash on purpose.

uiret.description: UINTR: ends a user-interrupt handler by popping the saved rip, RFLAGS and rsp from the stack and setting UIF again so further user interrupts can arrive.
