umonitor.description: WAITPKG: arms address monitoring for the cache line at the address in the register operand, so a following umwait wakes when that line is written. Usable from user mode.

umwait.description: WAITPKG: waits in a low-power state until the range armed by umonitor is written, an interrupt arrives, or the TSC passes the deadline in edx:eax. CF is set when the OS time limit ended the wait.
umwait.operation: wait until store to monitor || TSC >= edx:eax

unpckhpd.description: Puts the high double of the destination into the low lane and the high double of the source into the high lane. Often used to extract or interleave the upper halves of two vectors.

unpckhps.description: Interleaves the upper two floats of the destination and the source: the result is dst[2], src[2], dst[3], src[3] from low to high.

unpcklpd.description: Keeps the low double of the destination in the low lane and moves the low double of the source into the high lane, combining two scalars into one vector.

unpcklps.description: Interleaves the lower two floats of the destination and the source: the result is dst[0], src[0], dst[1], src[1] from low to high.

urdmsr.description: USER_MSR: reads a model-specific register, named by a register or 32-bit immediate, into a 64-bit register from user mode. Works only for MSRs the operating system has allowed in its permission bitmap.

uwrmsr.description: USER_MSR: writes a 64-bit register to a model-specific register, named by a register or 32-bit immediate, from user mode. Only MSRs the operating system has allowed can be written.

v4fmaddps.description: AVX512_4FMAPS (Xeon Phi): performs four fused multiply-adds in a row, using a block of four consecutive zmm registers starting at the second operand, each multiplied by one broadcast float from the 16-byte memory operand.

v4fmaddss.description: AVX512_4FMAPS (Xeon Phi): the scalar form of v4fmaddps; accumulates into the low float the products of the low floats of four consecutive registers with four floats from memory.

v4fnmaddps.description: AVX512_4FMAPS (Xeon Phi): like v4fmaddps, but each of the four products is subtracted from the accumulator instead of added.

v4fnmaddss.description: AVX512_4FMAPS (Xeon Phi): scalar form of v4fnmaddps; subtracts four products of register and memory floats from the low float of the destination.

vaddbf16.description: AVX10.2: adds the bfloat16 lanes of the second and third operands and writes the sums to the destination, in 128-, 256- or 512-bit widths with EVEX masking and broadcast.

vaddpd.description: Adds the double lanes of the two sources into the destination without changing either source. VEX forms clear the bits above the vector width; EVEX forms add masking, broadcast and 512-bit zmm.

vaddph.description: AVX512-FP16: adds the FP16 lanes of the two sources into the destination, with masking, broadcast and embedded rounding on the 512-bit form.

vaddps.description: Adds the float lanes of the two sources into the destination without changing either source. VEX forms zero the upper bits; EVEX forms add masking, broadcast and zmm.

vaddsd.description: Writes the sum of the low doubles of the two sources to the low lane of the destination and copies the upper double from the first source; bits above 128 are zeroed.

vaddsh.description: AVX512-FP16: adds the low FP16 values of the two sources into the low lane of the destination, copying the remaining bits of the low 128 from the first source.

vaddss.description: Writes the sum of the low floats of the two sources to the low lane of the destination and copies lanes 1–3 from the first source; bits above 128 are zeroed.

vaddsubpd.description: Subtracts in the even double lanes and adds in the odd ones, the pattern needed for complex-number multiplication. Three-operand VEX form in xmm or ymm.

vaddsubps.description: Subtracts in the even float lanes and adds in the odd ones, as used for complex multiplication. Three-operand VEX form in xmm or ymm.

vaesdec.description: Runs one inverse AES round (inverse shift rows, inverse substitution, inverse mix columns, then XOR with the round key) on each 128-bit lane. VAES extends it to ymm and zmm, one block per lane.

vaesdeclast.description: Runs the final inverse AES round, which skips inverse mix columns, on each 128-bit lane and XORs in the round key.

vaesenc.description: Runs one AES round (shift rows, substitution, mix columns, XOR with the round key) on each 128-bit lane. With VAES the ymm and zmm forms process two or four blocks at once.

vaesenclast.description: Runs the final AES round, which leaves out mix columns, on each 128-bit lane and XORs in the round key.

vaesimc.description: Applies the inverse mix-columns transform to a 128-bit round key, turning encryption round keys into the form needed by aesdec.

vaeskeygenassist.description: Helps expand an AES key: substitutes bytes of words 1 and 3 of the source through the S-box, rotates them and XORs in the round constant from the immediate.

valignd.description: AVX-512: joins the two sources with the first in the high half, shifts the pair right by imm8 doubleword positions and keeps the low vector-width part. Supports masking and dword broadcast.

valignq.description: AVX-512: joins the two sources with the first in the high half, shifts right by imm8 quadword positions and keeps the low part. Supports masking and qword broadcast.

vandnpd.summary: Bitwise AND NOT of packed doubles
vandnpd.description: Inverts the first source and ANDs it with the second, writing the result to the destination. Often used with a sign mask to clear sign bits or select bits.

vandnps.summary: Bitwise AND NOT of packed floats
vandnps.description: Inverts the first source and ANDs it with the second, writing the result to the destination; the EVEX form adds masking and broadcast.

vandpd.description: ANDs the two sources bit by bit into the destination. With a mask constant it computes fabs() by clearing sign bits.

vandps.description: ANDs the two sources bit by bit into the destination; compilers also use it on integer data in float registers.

vbcstnebf162ps.summary: Broadcast BF16 from memory as float
vbcstnebf162ps.description: AVX-NE-CONVERT: loads one bfloat16 value, converts it to FP32 and fills every float lane of the destination with it. Does not raise floating-point exceptions.

vbcstnesh2ps.summary: Broadcast FP16 from memory as float
vbcstnesh2ps.description: AVX-NE-CONVERT: loads one half-precision value, converts it to FP32 and writes it to every float lane of the destination.

vblendmpd.description: AVX-512: for each double lane takes the second source where the mask bit is set and the first source where it is clear. With {z} the clear lanes become zero instead.

vblendmps.description: AVX-512: for each float lane takes the second source where the mask bit is set and the first source otherwise; {z} zeroes the unselected lanes.

vblendpd.description: Selects each double lane from the second source when the matching imm8 bit is set, otherwise from the first source.

vblendps.description: Selects each float lane from the second source when the matching imm8 bit is set, otherwise from the first source.

vblendvpd.summary: Blend packed doubles by sign of a vector
vblendvpd.description: Picks each double lane from the second source where the sign bit of the matching lane of the fourth operand is set, otherwise from the first source. Used after a vector compare.

vblendvps.summary: Blend packed floats by sign of a vector
vblendvps.description: Picks each float lane from the second source where the sign bit of the matching lane of the fourth operand is set, otherwise from the first source.

vbroadcastf128.description: AVX: loads 128 bits from memory and writes them to both halves of a ymm register.

vbroadcastf32x2.description: AVX512DQ: repeats a pair of floats from the source across every 64-bit position of a ymm or zmm destination, with masking per float lane.

vbroadcastf32x4.description: AVX-512: loads 128 bits of floats and repeats them in every 128-bit lane of the ymm or zmm destination, with per-float masking.

vbroadcastf32x8.description: AVX512DQ: loads 256 bits of floats and writes them to both halves of a zmm register, with per-float masking.

vbroadcastf64x2.description: AVX512DQ: loads 128 bits of doubles and repeats them in every 128-bit lane of the ymm or zmm destination, with per-double masking.

vbroadcastf64x4.description: AVX-512: loads 256 bits of doubles and writes them to both halves of a zmm register, with per-double masking.

vbroadcasti128.description: AVX2: loads 128 bits from memory and writes them to both halves of a ymm register; the integer-domain twin of vbroadcastf128.

vbroadcasti32x2.description: AVX512DQ: repeats the low pair of 32-bit integers of the source in every 64-bit position of the destination, with per-dword masking.

vbroadcasti32x4.description: AVX-512: loads 128 bits of 32-bit integers and repeats them in every 128-bit lane of the destination, with per-dword masking.

vbroadcasti32x8.description: AVX512DQ: loads 256 bits of 32-bit integers and writes them to both halves of a zmm register, with per-dword masking.

vbroadcasti64x2.description: AVX512DQ: loads 128 bits of 64-bit integers and repeats them in every 128-bit lane of the ymm or zmm destination, with per-qword masking.

vbroadcasti64x4.description: AVX-512: loads 256 bits of 64-bit integers and writes them to both halves of a zmm register, with per-qword masking.

vbroadcastsd.description: Copies one double, from memory or (with AVX2) the low lane of an xmm register, into every double lane of a ymm or zmm destination.

vbroadcastss.description: Copies one float, from memory or (with AVX2) the low lane of an xmm register, into every float lane of the destination. A common way to splat a constant.

vcmpbf16.description: AVX10.2: compares bfloat16 lanes by the predicate in imm8 and sets the matching bit of the destination mask register for each true lane. LLVM folds the predicate into the mnemonic (vcmpltbf16, vcmpeqbf16…).

vcmppd.description: Compares double lanes by one of 32 predicates. The VEX form writes all ones or all zeros per lane; the EVEX form sets bits of a k mask. LLVM prints the predicate in the mnemonic (vcmpltpd, vcmpneq_uqpd…).

vcmpph.description: AVX512-FP16: compares FP16 lanes by the imm8 predicate and sets one bit of the destination mask per lane. LLVM folds the predicate into the name (vcmpleph…).

vcmpps.description: Compares float lanes by one of 32 predicates; VEX writes an all-ones or zero lane mask, EVEX sets bits in a k register. Shown as vcmpltps, vcmpunordps and so on.

vcmpsd.description: Compares the low doubles by the imm8 predicate. VEX writes all ones or zero to the low 64 bits and copies the upper double from the first source; EVEX sets bit 0 of a mask register.

vcmpsh.description: AVX512-FP16: compares the low FP16 values by the imm8 predicate and writes the result to bit 0 of the destination mask register.

vcmpss.description: Compares the low floats by the imm8 predicate. VEX writes all ones or zero to the low lane and copies the rest from the first source; EVEX writes bit 0 of a mask register.

vcomisbf16.description: AVX10.2: compares the low bfloat16 values and sets ZF, PF and CF like comiss (PF=1 for unordered), clearing OF, SF and AF. Signals invalid for any NaN.

vcomisd.description: Compares the low doubles and sets ZF, PF and CF, with PF=1 when unordered; OF, SF and AF are cleared. Signals invalid for any NaN, unlike vucomisd. The {sae} form suppresses exceptions.

vcomish.description: AVX512-FP16: compares the low FP16 values and sets ZF, PF and CF (PF=1 for unordered), clearing OF, SF and AF. Signals invalid on any NaN unless {sae} is given.

vcomiss.description: Compares the low floats and sets ZF, PF and CF, with PF=1 when unordered; OF, SF and AF are cleared. Raises invalid for quiet NaNs too, which vucomiss does not.

vcompresspd.description: AVX-512: stores only the double lanes whose mask bit is set, packed one after another starting at the memory address. Used to filter elements in vectorised loops.
vcompresspd.operation: j = 0; for i: if k[i] { mem[j++] = src[i] }

vcompressps.description: AVX-512: stores only the float lanes selected by the mask, packed contiguously at the memory address; unselected lanes are skipped rather than written.
vcompressps.operation: j = 0; for i: if k[i] { mem[j++] = src[i] }

vcomxsd.description: AVX10.2: compares the low doubles like vcomisd but sets the flags so that an unordered result does not look equal, letting a single jcc give the IEEE answer even with NaN. Signals invalid for any NaN.

vcomxsh.description: AVX10.2: the FP16 version of vcomxsd; compares the low half-precision values and sets flags so that NaN cases are not mistaken for equality.

vcomxss.description: AVX10.2: compares the low floats like vcomiss but with flag settings that keep unordered results distinct from equal, so je/jne work correctly with NaN.

vcvt2ph2bf8.summary: Convert two FP16 vectors to BF8
vcvt2ph2bf8.description: AVX10.2: converts the FP16 lanes of both sources to 8-bit E5M2 floats and packs them into one vector, the second source filling the lower half and the first the upper half.

vcvt2ph2bf8s.summary: Convert two FP16 vectors to BF8, saturating
vcvt2ph2bf8s.description: AVX10.2: like vcvt2ph2bf8, but values too large for E5M2 become the largest finite BF8 instead of infinity.

vcvt2ph2hf8.summary: Convert two FP16 vectors to HF8
vcvt2ph2hf8.description: AVX10.2: converts the FP16 lanes of both sources to 8-bit E4M3 (HF8) floats packed into one vector, the second source in the lower half and the first in the upper half.

vcvt2ph2hf8s.summary: Convert two FP16 vectors to HF8, saturating
vcvt2ph2hf8s.description: AVX10.2: like vcvt2ph2hf8, but out-of-range values are clamped to the largest finite HF8 value.

vcvt2ps2phx.summary: Convert two float vectors to FP16
vcvt2ps2phx.description: AVX10.2: converts the FP32 lanes of both sources to half precision and packs them into one vector, the second source in the lower half and the first in the upper half.

vcvtbf162ibs.summary: Convert BF16 to signed 8-bit integers, saturating
vcvtbf162ibs.description: AVX10.2: converts each bfloat16 lane to an integer, clamps it to the signed 8-bit range −128…127 and stores it in the matching 16-bit lane. NaN gives 0.

vcvtbf162iubs.summary: Convert BF16 to unsigned 8-bit integers, saturating
vcvtbf162iubs.description: AVX10.2: converts each bfloat16 lane to an integer, clamps it to the unsigned 8-bit range 0…255 and stores it in the matching 16-bit lane. NaN gives 0.

vcvtbiasph2bf8.summary: Convert FP16 to BF8 with bias
vcvtbiasph2bf8.description: AVX10.2: converts the FP16 lanes of the third operand to E5M2, adding the per-element bias bytes from the second operand before rounding, which allows stochastic rounding. The result is half as wide.

vcvtbiasph2bf8s.summary: Convert FP16 to BF8 with bias, saturating
vcvtbiasph2bf8s.description: AVX10.2: like vcvtbiasph2bf8, but values outside the E5M2 range are clamped to the largest finite BF8 instead of infinity.

vcvtbiasph2hf8.summary: Convert FP16 to HF8 with bias
vcvtbiasph2hf8.description: AVX10.2: converts the FP16 lanes of the third operand to E4M3 (HF8) after adding bias bytes from the second operand, for stochastic rounding; the result vector is half as wide.

vcvtbiasph2hf8s.summary: Convert FP16 to HF8 with bias, saturating
vcvtbiasph2hf8s.description: AVX10.2: like vcvtbiasph2hf8, but values beyond the HF8 range are clamped to the largest finite HF8.

vcvtdq2pd.description: Converts signed 32-bit integers from the low half of the source to doubles, filling a destination twice as wide; the conversion is always exact.

vcvtdq2ph.description: AVX512-FP16: converts signed 32-bit integers to FP16, producing a result half the width of the source; large values round or overflow to infinity.

vcvtdq2ps.description: Converts each signed 32-bit integer lane to a float, rounding by MXCSR when the value has more than 24 significant bits.

vcvthf82ph.description: AVX10.2: widens each 8-bit E4M3 (HF8) value from the source to FP16 in a destination twice as wide; every HF8 value is exactly representable.

vcvtne2ps2bf16.summary: Convert two float vectors to BF16
vcvtne2ps2bf16.description: AVX512_BF16: converts the floats of both sources to bfloat16 with round-to-nearest-even and packs them into one vector, the second source in the lower half and the first in the upper half.

vcvtneebf162ps.summary: Convert even BF16 elements to floats
vcvtneebf162ps.description: AVX-NE-CONVERT: reads the even-indexed bfloat16 values from memory and widens each to FP32 in the matching 32-bit lane. No floating-point exceptions are raised.

vcvtneeph2ps.summary: Convert even FP16 elements to floats
vcvtneeph2ps.description: AVX-NE-CONVERT: reads the even-indexed half-precision values from memory and widens each to FP32 in the matching 32-bit lane.

vcvtneobf162ps.summary: Convert odd BF16 elements to floats
vcvtneobf162ps.description: AVX-NE-CONVERT: reads the odd-indexed bfloat16 values from memory and widens each to FP32; paired with the even form to unpack a whole BF16 vector.

vcvtneoph2ps.summary: Convert odd FP16 elements to floats
vcvtneoph2ps.description: AVX-NE-CONVERT: reads the odd-indexed half-precision values from memory and widens each to FP32 in the matching 32-bit lane.

vcvtneps2bf16.description: Converts FP32 lanes to bfloat16 with round-to-nearest-even, producing a result half the width of the source. Available as VEX (AVX-NE-CONVERT) and EVEX (AVX512_BF16, with masking).

vcvtpd2dq.description: Converts each double to a signed 32-bit integer using the MXCSR rounding mode, giving a result half as wide. Out-of-range values and NaN become 0x80000000; the vcvttpd2dq form truncates instead.

vcvtpd2ph.description: AVX512-FP16: converts each double to FP16, placing the results in the low part of an xmm destination with the rest zeroed.

vcvtpd2ps.description: Rounds each double to single precision by MXCSR and writes the results to an xmm destination half the width of the source, zeroing the upper bits.

vcvtpd2qq.description: AVX512DQ: converts each double to a signed 64-bit integer using the current rounding mode; out-of-range values and NaN give 0x8000000000000000.

vcvtpd2udq.description: AVX-512: converts each double to an unsigned 32-bit integer using the current rounding mode, giving a result half as wide; negative, too large or NaN inputs give 0xFFFFFFFF.

vcvtpd2uqq.description: Converts each double-precision value of the source to an unsigned 64-bit integer, rounding by the MXCSR mode or an {er} override; NaN and out-of-range inputs give all ones. EVEX only, with masking and broadcast.

vcvtph2bf8.description: Converts each FP16 value of the source to a BF8 (E5M2) 8-bit float, rounding to nearest even; values too large become infinity or NaN. Results take half the source width (zmm into ymm). AVX10.2, EVEX with masking.

vcvtph2bf8s.summary: Convert packed FP16 to BF8, saturating
vcvtph2bf8s.description: Converts each FP16 value of the source to a BF8 (E5M2) 8-bit float, rounding to nearest even; values too large saturate to the largest finite number. Results take half the source width (zmm into ymm). AVX10.2, EVEX with masking.

vcvtph2dq.description: Converts each FP16 value of the source to a signed 32-bit integer, rounding by the MXCSR mode or an {er} override; NaN and out-of-range inputs give the minimum value (integer indefinite). The source is half as wide as the destination (xmm into ymm). EVEX only, with masking and broadcast.

vcvtph2pd.description: Converts each FP16 value of the source to a double-precision value exactly. The source is a quarter of the destination width (xmm into zmm). EVEX only, with masking and broadcast.

vcvtph2ps.description: Widens each FP16 value of the source to single precision exactly; the source is half as wide (xmm into ymm). The F16C (VEX) form is how compilers load _Float16 data on CPUs without AVX512-FP16; EVEX adds masking.

vcvtps2phx.description: Narrows each single-precision value to FP16, rounding by MXCSR or {er}. Unlike vcvtps2ph it has no imm8, writes only to a register and accepts a broadcast source. Results take half the source width (zmm into ymm).

vdbpsadbw.summary: Double-block packed sum of absolute differences
vdbpsadbw.description: Within each 128-bit lane, shuffles the dwords of the third operand by imm8, then sums absolute differences of unsigned bytes between 4-byte groups of the second operand and overlapping 4-byte windows of the shuffled data, giving 16-bit sums. Used in video motion search.
vdbpsadbw.operation: tmp = shuf32(b, imm8); dst.w[i] = Σ |a.u8 − tmp.u8| over 4 bytes

vdivbf16.description: Divides each element of the second operand by the matching element of the third, writing the quotients to the destination; the sources are left intact. Division is slow, so fast-math code may multiply by a reciprocal instead. AVX10.2, EVEX with masking and broadcast.

vdivpd.description: Divides each element of the second operand by the matching element of the third, writing the quotients to the destination; the sources are left intact. vdivsh.description: Divides the low FP16 element of the second operand by that of the third and writes the quotient to the low element; the rest of the low 128 bits is copied from the second operand. EVEX only, with a mask and {er}.

vdpbf16ps.summary: Dot product of BF16 pairs into single precision
vdpbf16ps.description: Multiplies adjacent pairs of BF16 values from the second and third operands and adds both products to the matching single-precision element of the destination. Used for neural network inference and training; EVEX with masking and broadcast.

vdppd.summary: Dot product of packed doubles with mask
vdppd.description: Multiplies the two double-precision pairs of the sources, sums the products whose bits 4–5 of imm8 are set, and writes the sum to the elements selected by bits 0–1, zeroing the others. VEX 128-bit only.
vdppd.operation: s = Σ imm[4+i] ? a[i]*b[i] : 0; dst[i] = imm[i] ? s : 0

vdpphps.summary: Dot product of FP16 pairs into single precision
vdpphps.description: Multiplies adjacent pairs of FP16 values from the second and third operands and adds both products to the matching single-precision element of the destination. AVX10.2, EVEX with masking and broadcast; aimed at machine-learning kernels.

vdpps.summary: Dot product of packed singles with mask
vdpps.description: In each 128-bit lane, multiplies four single-precision pairs, sums the products whose bits 4–7 of imm8 are set, and writes the sum to the elements selected by bits 0–3, zeroing the others. The ymm form works on two lanes independently.
vdpps.operation: s = Σ imm[4+i] ? a[i]*b[i] : 0; dst[i] = imm[i] ? s : 0 (per lane)

verr.description: Sets ZF if the segment named by the selector operand is readable at the current privilege level and clears it otherwise; an unusable selector does not fault. Seen only in operating-system and legacy code.

verw.description: Sets ZF if the segment named by the selector operand is writable at the current privilege level. Kernels also run verw with any valid selector for its side effect of clearing CPU buffers, the MDS mitigation.

vexp2pd.description: Computes 2 raised to each double-precision element with a relative error below 2^-23; 512-bit zmm only, with masking. Part of AVX-512ER, which only Xeon Phi (Knights Landing and Knights Mill) has.

vexp2ps.description: Computes 2 raised to each single-precision element with a relative error below 2^-23; 512-bit zmm only, with masking. Part of AVX-512ER, which only Xeon Phi (Knights Landing and Knights Mill) has.

vexpandpd.description: Takes consecutive double-precision values from the source register or memory and places them in order into the destination lanes whose mask bit is set; other lanes are kept, or zeroed with {z}. The inverse of vcompresspd.
vexpandpd.operation: j = 0; for i: if k[i] dst[i] = src[j++]

vexpandps.description: Takes consecutive single-precision values from the source register or memory and places them in order into the destination lanes whose mask bit is set; other lanes are kept, or zeroed with {z}. The inverse of vcompressps.
vexpandps.operation: j = 0; for i: if k[i] dst[i] = src[j++]

vextractf128.description: Copies the 128-bit lane of a ymm register selected by imm8 bit 0 to an xmm register or memory, in the floating-point domain. Compilers use it to reach the upper half, e.g. for horizontal sums.

vextractf32x4.summary: Extract 128 bits of floating-point data (32-bit elements)
vextractf32x4.description: Copies the 128-bit lane of a ymm or zmm register selected by imm8 to an xmm register or memory, in the floating-point domain. The writemask applies per 32-bit element.

vextractf32x8.summary: Extract 256 bits of floating-point data (32-bit elements)
vextractf32x8.description: Copies the 256-bit lane of a zmm register selected by imm8 bit 0 to a ymm register or memory, in the floating-point domain. The writemask applies per 32-bit element.

vextractf64x2.summary: Extract 128 bits of floating-point data (64-bit elements)
vextractf64x2.description: Copies the 128-bit lane of a ymm or zmm register selected by imm8 to an xmm register or memory, in the floating-point domain. The writemask applies per 64-bit element.

vextractf64x4.summary: Extract 256 bits of floating-point data (64-bit elements)
vextractf64x4.description: Copies the 256-bit lane of a zmm register selected by imm8 bit 0 to a ymm register or memory, in the floating-point domain. The writemask applies per 64-bit element.

vextracti128.description: Copies the 128-bit lane of a ymm register selected by imm8 bit 0 to an xmm register or memory, in the integer domain. Compilers use it to reach the upper half, e.g. for horizontal sums.

vextracti32x4.summary: Extract 128 bits of integer data (32-bit elements)
vextracti32x4.description: Copies the 128-bit lane of a ymm or zmm register selected by imm8 to an xmm register or memory, in the integer domain. The writemask applies per 32-bit element.

vextracti32x8.summary: Extract 256 bits of integer data (32-bit elements)
vextracti32x8.description: Copies the 256-bit lane of a zmm register selected by imm8 bit 0 to a ymm register or memory, in the integer domain. The writemask applies per 32-bit element.

vextracti64x2.summary: Extract 128 bits of integer data (64-bit elements)
vextracti64x2.description: Copies the 128-bit lane of a ymm or zmm register selected by imm8 to an xmm register or memory, in the integer domain. The writemask applies per 64-bit element.

vextracti64x4.summary: Extract 256 bits of integer data (64-bit elements)
vextracti64x4.description: Copies the 256-bit lane of a zmm register selected by imm8 bit 0 to a ymm register or memory, in the integer domain. The writemask applies per 64-bit element.

vextractps.description: Copies the 32-bit element selected by imm8 bits 0–1 of an xmm register, as raw bits, to a general-purpose register or memory. A 64-bit register destination is zero-extended.

vfcmaddcph.description: Treats each adjacent pair of FP16 values as a complex number (real, imaginary) and multiplies the second operand by the complex conjugate of the third, adding the product to the destination. Masking works per complex pair. The destination must differ from the sources.

vfcmaddcsh.description: Treats the lowest pair of FP16 values as a complex number (real, imaginary) and multiplies the second operand by the complex conjugate of the third, adding the product to the destination. Bits 32–127 come from the second operand. The destination must differ from the sources.

vfcmulcph.description: Treats each adjacent pair of FP16 values as a complex number (real, imaginary) and multiplies the second operand by the complex conjugate of the third, writing the product to the destination. Masking works per complex pair. The destination must differ from the sources.

vfcmulcsh.description: Treats the lowest pair of FP16 values as a complex number (real, imaginary) and multiplies the second operand by the complex conjugate of the third, writing the product to the destination. Bits 32–127 come from the second operand. The destination must differ from the sources.

vfixupimmpd.summary: Fix up special packed double values
vfixupimmpd.description: Classifies each element of the second operand (NaN, ±0, 1, ±inf, negative, positive) and by that class picks a 4-bit action from the integer table in the third: keep the destination, take the input, or a constant such as ±0, ±inf, NaN or π/2. imm8 picks which classes signal.

vfixupimmps.summary: Fix up special packed single values
vfixupimmps.description: Classifies each element of the second operand (NaN, ±0, 1, ±inf, negative, positive) and by that class picks a 4-bit action from the integer table in the third: keep the destination, take the input, or a constant such as ±0, ±inf, NaN or π/2. imm8 picks which classes signal.

vfixupimmsd.summary: Fix up special scalar double values
vfixupimmsd.description: Classifies the low element of the second operand (NaN, ±0, 1, ±inf, negative, positive) and by that class picks a 4-bit action from the integer table in the third: keep the destination, take the input, or a constant such as ±0, ±inf, NaN or π/2. Upper bits copy the second operand.

vfixupimmss.summary: Fix up special scalar single values
vfixupimmss.description: Classifies the low element of the second operand (NaN, ±0, 1, ±inf, negative, positive) and by that class picks a 4-bit action from the integer table in the third: keep the destination, take the input, or a constant such as ±0, ±inf, NaN or π/2. Upper bits copy the second operand.

vfmadd132bf16.description: Fused multiply-add on packed BF16 values: computes destination × third operand + second operand with a single rounding and writes it to the destination. AVX10.2, EVEX with masking and broadcast.

vfmadd132pd.description: Fused multiply-add on packed double-precision values: computes destination × third operand + second operand with a single rounding and writes it to the destination. VEX and EVEX forms; EVEX adds masking, broadcast and {er}.

vfmadd132ph.description: Fused multiply-add on packed FP16 values: computes destination × third operand + second operand with a single rounding and writes it to the destination. EVEX only, with masking, broadcast and {er}.

vfmadd132ps.description: Fused multiply-add on packed single-precision values: computes destination × third operand + second operand with a single rounding and writes it to the destination. VEX and EVEX forms; EVEX adds masking, broadcast and {er}.

vfmadd132sd.description: Fused multiply-add on the low double-precision element: computes destination × third operand + second operand with a single rounding and writes it to the destination. The other elements of the destination keep their values. VEX and EVEX forms; EVEX adds a mask and {er}.

vfmadd132sh.description: Fused multiply-add on the low FP16 element: computes destination × third operand + second operand with a single rounding and writes it to the destination. The other elements of the destination keep their values. EVEX only, with a mask and {er}.

vfmadd132ss.description: Fused multiply-add on the low single-precision element: computes destination × third operand + second operand with a single rounding and writes it to the destination. The other elements of the destination keep their values. VEX and EVEX forms; EVEX adds a mask and {er}.

vfmadd213bf16.description: Fused multiply-add on packed BF16 values: computes second operand × destination + third operand with a single rounding and writes it to the destination. AVX10.2, EVEX with masking and broadcast.

vfmadd213pd.description: Fused multiply-add on packed double-precision values: computes second operand × destination + third operand with a single rounding and writes it to the destination. VEX and EVEX forms; EVEX adds masking, broadcast and {er}.

vfmadd213ss.description: Fused multiply-add on the low single-precision element: computes second operand × destination + third operand with a single rounding and writes it to the destination. The other elements of the destination keep their values. VEX and EVEX forms; EVEX adds a mask and {er}.

vfmadd231bf16.description: Fused multiply-add on packed BF16 values: computes second × third operand + destination with a single rounding and writes it to the destination. AVX10.2, EVEX with masking and broadcast.

vfmadd231pd.description: Fused multiply-add on packed double-precision values: computes second × third operand + destination with a single rounding and writes it to the destination. VEX and EVEX forms; EVEX adds masking, broadcast and {er}.

vfmadd231ph.description: Fused multiply-add on packed FP16 values: computes second × third operand + destination with a single rounding and writes it to the destination. EVEX only, with masking, broadcast and {er}.

vfmadd231sh.description: Fused multiply-add on the low FP16 element: computes second × third operand + destination with a single rounding and writes it to the destination. The other elements of the destination keep their values. EVEX only, with a mask and {er}.

vfmaddcph.description: Treats each adjacent pair of FP16 values as a complex number (real, imaginary) and multiplies the second operand by the third, adding the product to the destination. Masking works per complex pair. The destination must differ from the sources.

vfmaddcsh.description: Treats the lowest pair of FP16 values as a complex number (real, imaginary) and multiplies the second operand by the third, adding the product to the destination. Bits 32–127 come from the second operand. The destination must differ from the sources.

vfmaddpd.description: AMD FMA4 four-operand form on packed double-precision values: the destination receives second × third + fourth operand with a single rounding, so no source is overwritten. VEX.W picks whether the third or fourth operand may be memory. Only on AMD Bulldozer-family CPUs.

vfmaddps.description: AMD FMA4 four-operand form on packed single-precision values: the destination receives second × third + fourth operand with a single rounding, so no source is overwritten. VEX.W picks whether the third or fourth operand may be memory. Only on AMD Bulldozer-family CPUs.

vfmaddsd.description: AMD FMA4 four-operand form on the low double-precision element: the destination receives second × third + fourth operand with a single rounding, so no source is overwritten. VEX.W picks whether the third or fourth operand may be memory. Only on AMD Bulldozer-family CPUs.
vfmaddsd.operation: dst[0] = a[0] * b[0] + c[0]; upper bits zeroed

vfmaddss.description: AMD FMA4 four-operand form on the low single-precision element: the destination receives second × third + fourth operand with a single rounding, so no source is overwritten. VEX.W picks whether the third or fourth operand may be memory. Only on AMD Bulldozer-family CPUs.
vfmaddss.operation: dst[0] = a[0] * b[0] + c[0]; upper bits zeroed

vfmaddsub132pd.description: Fused multiply on packed double-precision values computing destination × third operand, then subtracting the second operand in even lanes and adding it in odd lanes, with one rounding. Handy for complex multiplication. VEX and EVEX forms; EVEX adds masking, broadcast and {er}.
vfmaddsub132pd.operation: a[i] = a[i] * c[i] ∓ b[i]  (− for even i, + for odd i)

vfmaddsub132ph.description: Fused multiply on packed FP16 values computing destination × third operand, then subtracting the second operand in even lanes and adding it in odd lanes, with one rounding. Handy for complex multiplication. EVEX only, with masking, broadcast and {er}.
vfmaddsub132ph.operation: a[i] = a[i] * c[i] ∓ b[i]  (− for even i, + for odd i)

vfmaddsub132ps.description: Fused multiply on packed single-precision values computing destination × third operand, then subtracting the second operand in even lanes and adding it in odd lanes, with one rounding. vfmaddsub132ps.operation: a[i] = a[i] * c[i] ∓ b[i]  (− for even i, + for odd i)

vfmaddsub213pd.description: Fused multiply on packed double-precision values computing second operand × destination, then subtracting the third operand in even lanes and adding it in odd lanes, with one rounding. Handy for complex multiplication. VEX and EVEX forms; EVEX adds masking, broadcast and {er}.
vfmaddsub213pd.operation: a[i] = b[i] * a[i] ∓ c[i]  (− for even i, + for odd i)

vfmaddsub213ph.description: Fused multiply on packed FP16 values computing second operand × destination, then subtracting the third operand in even lanes and adding it in odd lanes, with one rounding. Handy for complex multiplication. EVEX only, with masking, broadcast and {er}.
vfmaddsub213ph.operation: a[i] = b[i] * a[i] ∓ c[i]  (− for even i, + for odd i)

vfmaddsub213ps.operation: a[i] = b[i] * a[i] ∓ c[i]  (− for even i, + for odd i)

vfmaddsub231pd.description: Fused multiply on packed double-precision values computing second × third operand, then subtracting the destination in even lanes and adding it in odd lanes, with one rounding. Handy for complex multiplication. VEX and EVEX forms; EVEX adds masking, broadcast and {er}.
vfmaddsub231pd.operation: a[i] = b[i] * c[i] ∓ a[i]  (− for even i, + for odd i)

vfmaddsub231ph.description: Fused multiply on packed FP16 values computing second × third operand, then subtracting the destination in even lanes and adding it in odd lanes, with one rounding. Handy for complex multiplication. EVEX only, with masking, broadcast and {er}.
vfmaddsub231ph.operation: a[i] = b[i] * c[i] ∓ a[i]  (− for even i, + for odd i)

vfmaddsub231ps.description: Fused multiply on packed single-precision values computing second × third operand, then subtracting the destination in even lanes and adding it in odd lanes, with one rounding. Handy for complex multiplication. VEX and EVEX forms; EVEX adds masking, broadcast and {er}.
vfmaddsub231ps.operation: a[i] = b[i] * c[i] ∓ a[i]  (− for even i, + for odd i)

vfmaddsubpd.description: AMD FMA4 four-operand form on packed double-precision values: second × third operand, then the fourth is subtracted in even lanes and added in odd lanes, with one rounding; no source is overwritten. Only on AMD Bulldozer-family CPUs.
vfmaddsubpd.operation: dst[i] = a[i] * b[i] ∓ c[i]  (− for even i, + for odd i)

vfmaddsubps.description: AMD FMA4 four-operand form on packed single-precision values: second × third operand, then the fourth is subtracted in even lanes and added in odd lanes, with one rounding; no source is overwritten. Only on AMD Bulldozer-family CPUs.
vfmaddsubps.operation: dst[i] = a[i] * b[i] ∓ c[i]  (− for even i, + for odd i)

vfmsub132bf16.description: Fused multiply-subtract on packed BF16 values: computes destination × third operand − second operand with a single rounding and writes it to the destination. AVX10.2, EVEX with masking and broadcast.

vfmsub132pd.description: Fused multiply-subtract on packed double-precision values: computes destination × third operand − second operand with a single rounding and writes it to the destination. VEX and EVEX forms; EVEX adds masking, broadcast and {er}.

vfmsub231bf16.description: Computes (op2 × op3) − op1 on each BF16 element, rounding once, and writes it to op1. AVX10.2, EVEX only, with masking and broadcast.

vfmsub231pd.description: Computes (op2 × op3) − op1 on each double-precision element, rounding once, and writes it to op1. VEX forms are FMA; EVEX forms add masking, broadcast and zmm rounding control.

vfmsub231ph.description: Computes (op2 × op3) − op1 on each FP16 element, rounding once, and writes it to op1. AVX512-FP16, EVEX only, with masking and broadcast.

vfmsub231ps.description: Computes (op2 × op3) − op1 on each single-precision element, rounding once, and writes it to op1. VEX forms are FMA; EVEX forms add masking, broadcast and zmm rounding control.

vfmsub231sd.description: Computes (op2 × op3) − op1 on the low double-precision element, rounding once, and writes it to op1. The other elements of op1 are kept. VEX (FMA) or EVEX with masking.

vfmsub231sh.description: Computes (op2 × op3) − op1 on the low FP16 element, rounding once, and writes it to op1. The other elements of op1 are kept. AVX512-FP16, EVEX only.

vfmsub231ss.description: Computes (op2 × op3) − op1 on the low single-precision element, rounding once, and writes it to op1. The other elements of op1 are kept. VEX (FMA) or EVEX with masking.

vfmsubadd132pd.description: Multiplies op1 by op3, then adds op2 in even-indexed elements and subtracts it in odd ones, on each double-precision element, rounding once, and writes it to op1. VEX forms are FMA; EVEX forms add masking, broadcast and zmm rounding control.
vfmsubadd132pd.operation: dst[i] = dst[i]*src3[i] + src2[i] (even i), dst[i]*src3[i] - src2[i] (odd i)

vfmsubadd132ph.description: Multiplies op1 by op3, then adds op2 in even-indexed elements and subtracts it in odd ones, on each FP16 element, rounding once, and writes it to op1. AVX512-FP16, EVEX only, with masking and broadcast.
vfmsubadd132ph.operation: dst[i] = dst[i]*src3[i] + src2[i] (even i), dst[i]*src3[i] - src2[i] (odd i)

vfmsubadd132ps.description: Multiplies op1 by op3, then adds op2 in even-indexed elements and subtracts it in odd ones, on each single-precision element, rounding once, and writes it to op1. VEX forms are FMA; EVEX forms add masking, broadcast and zmm rounding control.
vfmsubadd132ps.operation: dst[i] = dst[i]*src3[i] + src2[i] (even i), dst[i]*src3[i] - src2[i] (odd i)

vfmsubadd213pd.description: Multiplies op2 by op1, then adds op3 in even-indexed elements and subtracts it in odd ones, on each double-precision element, rounding once, and writes it to op1. VEX forms are FMA; EVEX forms add masking, broadcast and zmm rounding control.
vfmsubadd213pd.operation: dst[i] = src2[i]*dst[i] + src3[i] (even i), src2[i]*dst[i] - src3[i] (odd i)

vfmsubadd213ph.description: Multiplies op2 by op1, then adds op3 in even-indexed elements and subtracts it in odd ones, on each FP16 element, rounding once, and writes it to op1. AVX512-FP16, EVEX only, with masking and broadcast.
vfmsubadd213ph.operation: dst[i] = src2[i]*dst[i] + src3[i] (even i), src2[i]*dst[i] - src3[i] (odd i)

vfmsubadd213ps.description: Multiplies op2 by op1, then adds op3 in even-indexed elements and subtracts it in odd ones, on each single-precision element, rounding once, and writes it to op1. VEX forms are FMA; EVEX forms add masking, broadcast and zmm rounding control.
vfmsubadd213ps.operation: dst[i] = src2[i]*dst[i] + src3[i] (even i), src2[i]*dst[i] - src3[i] (odd i)

vfmsubadd231pd.description: Multiplies op2 by op3, then adds op1 in even-indexed elements and subtracts it in odd ones, on each double-precision element, rounding once, and writes it to op1. VEX forms are FMA; EVEX forms add masking, broadcast and zmm rounding control.
vfmsubadd231pd.operation: dst[i] = src2[i]*src3[i] + dst[i] (even i), src2[i]*src3[i] - dst[i] (odd i)

vfmsubadd231ph.description: Multiplies op2 by op3, then adds op1 in even-indexed elements and subtracts it in odd ones, on each FP16 element, rounding once, and writes it to op1. AVX512-FP16, EVEX only, with masking and broadcast.
vfmsubadd231ph.operation: dst[i] = src2[i]*src3[i] + dst[i] (even i), src2[i]*src3[i] - dst[i] (odd i)

vfmsubadd231ps.description: Multiplies op2 by op3, then adds op1 in even-indexed elements and subtracts it in odd ones, on each single-precision element, rounding once, and writes it to op1. VEX forms are FMA; EVEX forms add masking, broadcast and zmm rounding control.
vfmsubadd231ps.operation: dst[i] = src2[i]*src3[i] + dst[i] (even i), src2[i]*src3[i] - dst[i] (odd i)

vfmsubaddpd.description: Multiplies op2 by op3, then adds op4 in even-indexed elements and subtracts it in odd ones, on each double-precision element, rounding once, and writes it to op1 without changing the sources. AMD FMA4 only (Bulldozer family).
vfmsubaddpd.operation: dst[i] = src2[i]*src3[i] + src4[i] (even i), src2[i]*src3[i] - src4[i] (odd i)

vfmsubaddps.description: Multiplies op2 by op3, then adds op4 in even-indexed elements and subtracts it in odd ones, on each single-precision element, rounding once, and writes it to op1 without changing the sources. AMD FMA4 only (Bulldozer family).
vfmsubaddps.operation: dst[i] = src2[i]*src3[i] + src4[i] (even i), src2[i]*src3[i] - src4[i] (odd i)

vfmsubpd.description: Computes (op2 × op3) − op4 on each double-precision element, rounding once, and writes it to op1 without changing the sources. AMD FMA4 only (Bulldozer family).

vfmsubps.description: Computes (op2 × op3) − op4 on each single-precision element, rounding once, and writes it to op1 without changing the sources. AMD FMA4 only (Bulldozer family).

vfmsubsd.description: Computes (op2 × op3) − op4 on the low double-precision element (the rest of op1 is cleared), rounding once, and writes it to op1 without changing the sources. AMD FMA4 only (Bulldozer family).

vfmsubss.description: Computes (op2 × op3) − op4 on the low single-precision element (the rest of op1 is cleared), rounding once, and writes it to op1 without changing the sources. AMD FMA4 only (Bulldozer family).

vfmulcph.description: Treats each pair of FP16 values (real part even, imaginary part odd) as a complex number and multiplies the second and third operands pair by pair. AVX512-FP16, masked per complex pair; the destination must differ from both sources.

vfmulcsh.description: Multiplies the low complex number (two FP16 values: real, imaginary) of the second and third operands; the other elements come from the second operand. AVX512-FP16; the destination must differ from both sources.

vfnmadd132bf16.description: Computes op2 − (op1 × op3) on each BF16 element, rounding once, and writes it to op1. AVX10.2, EVEX only, with masking and broadcast.

vfnmadd132pd.description: Computes op2 − (op1 × op3) on each double-precision element, rounding once, and writes it to op1. VEX forms are FMA; EVEX forms add masking, broadcast and zmm rounding control.

vfnmadd132ph.description: Computes op2 − (op1 × op3) on each FP16 element, rounding once, and writes it to op1. AVX512-FP16, EVEX only, with masking and broadcast.

vfnmadd132ps.description: Computes op2 − (op1 × op3) on each single-precision element, rounding once, and writes it to op1. VEX forms are FMA; EVEX forms add masking, broadcast and zmm rounding control.

vfnmadd132sd.description: Computes op2 − (op1 × op3) on the low double-precision element, rounding once, and writes it to op1. The other elements of op1 are kept. VEX (FMA) or EVEX with masking.

vfnmadd132sh.description: Computes op2 − (op1 × op3) on the low FP16 element, rounding once, and writes it to op1. The other elements of op1 are kept. AVX512-FP16, EVEX only.

vfnmadd132ss.description: Computes op2 − (op1 × op3) on the low single-precision element, rounding once, and writes it to op1. The other elements of op1 are kept. VEX (FMA) or EVEX with masking.

vfnmadd213bf16.description: Computes op3 − (op2 × op1) on each BF16 element, rounding once, and writes it to op1. AVX10.2, EVEX only, with masking and broadcast.

vfnmadd213pd.description: Computes op3 − (op2 × op1) on each double-precision element, rounding once, and writes it to op1. VEX forms are FMA; EVEX forms add masking, broadcast and zmm rounding control.

vfnmaddps.description: Computes op4 − (op2 × op3) on each single-precision element, rounding once, and writes it to op1 without changing the sources. AMD FMA4 only (Bulldozer family).

vfnmaddsd.description: Computes op4 − (op2 × op3) on the low double-precision element (the rest of op1 is cleared), rounding once, and writes it to op1 without changing the sources. AMD FMA4 only (Bulldozer family).

vfnmaddss.description: Computes op4 − (op2 × op3) on the low single-precision element (the rest of op1 is cleared), rounding once, and writes it to op1 without changing the sources. AMD FMA4 only (Bulldozer family).

vfnmsub132bf16.description: Computes −(op1 × op3) − op2 on each BF16 element, rounding once, and writes it to op1. AVX10.2, EVEX only, with masking and broadcast.

vfnmsub132pd.description: Computes −(op1 × op3) − op2 on each double-precision element, rounding once, and writes it to op1. VEX forms are FMA; EVEX forms add masking, broadcast and zmm rounding control.

vfnmsub213bf16.description: Computes −(op2 × op1) − op3 on each BF16 element, rounding once, and writes it to op1. AVX10.2, EVEX only, with masking and broadcast.

vfnmsub213pd.description: Computes −(op2 × op1) − op3 on each double-precision element, rounding once, and writes it to op1. VEX forms are FMA; EVEX forms add masking, broadcast and zmm rounding control.

vfnmsub231pd.description: Computes −(op2 × op3) − op1 on each double-precision element, rounding once, and writes it to op1. VEX forms are FMA; EVEX forms add masking, broadcast and zmm rounding control.

vfnmsubps.description: Computes −(op2 × op3) − op4 on each single-precision element, rounding once, and writes it to op1 without changing the sources. AMD FMA4 only (Bulldozer family).

vfnmsubsd.description: Computes −(op2 × op3) − op4 on the low double-precision element (the rest of op1 is cleared), rounding once, and writes it to op1 without changing the sources. AMD FMA4 only (Bulldozer family).

vfpclassbf16.description: Sets a mask bit for each BF16 element that falls in any class chosen by imm8: quiet NaN, ±0, ±infinity, denormal, negative finite or signalling NaN. AVX10.2, with write mask and broadcast; handy for fast NaN and infinity checks.

vfpclasspd.description: Sets a mask bit for each double element that falls in any class chosen by imm8: quiet NaN, ±0, ±infinity, denormal, negative finite or signalling NaN. AVX512DQ, with write mask and broadcast; handy for fast NaN and infinity checks.

vfpclassph.description: Sets a mask bit for each FP16 element that falls in any class chosen by imm8: quiet NaN, ±0, ±infinity, denormal, negative finite or signalling NaN. AVX512-FP16, with write mask and broadcast; handy for fast NaN and infinity checks.

vfpclassps.description: Sets a mask bit for each single element that falls in any class chosen by imm8: quiet NaN, ±0, ±infinity, denormal, negative finite or signalling NaN. AVX512DQ, with write mask and broadcast; handy for fast NaN and infinity checks.

vfpclasssd.description: Checks whether the low double element falls in any class chosen by imm8 (quiet or signalling NaN, ±0, ±infinity, denormal, negative finite) and writes the answer to bit 0 of a mask register, clearing the others. AVX512DQ.

vfpclasssh.description: Checks whether the low FP16 element falls in any class chosen by imm8 (quiet or signalling NaN, ±0, ±infinity, denormal, negative finite) and writes the answer to bit 0 of a mask register, clearing the others. AVX512-FP16.

vfpclassss.description: Checks whether the low single element falls in any class chosen by imm8 (quiet or signalling NaN, ±0, ±infinity, denormal, negative finite) and writes the answer to bit 0 of a mask register, clearing the others. AVX512DQ.

vfrczpd.description: Writes the fractional part of each double-precision element, x − trunc(x), which keeps the sign of x. AMD XOP only (Bulldozer family), xmm or ymm.

vfrczps.description: Writes the fractional part of each single-precision element, x − trunc(x), which keeps the sign of x. AMD XOP only (Bulldozer family), xmm or ymm.

vfrczsd.description: Writes the fractional part of the low double-precision element, x − trunc(x), keeping the sign of x. AMD XOP only (Bulldozer family).

vfrczss.description: Writes the fractional part of the low single-precision element, x − trunc(x), keeping the sign of x. AMD XOP only (Bulldozer family).

vgatherdpd.description: Loads double-precision elements from base + index × scale, with 32-bit indices taken from a vector, wherever the mask selects them. VEX takes a vector mask (sign bits), EVEX a k register; the mask is cleared as elements arrive.

vgatherdps.description: Loads single-precision elements from base + index × scale, with 32-bit indices taken from a vector, wherever the mask selects them. VEX takes a vector mask (sign bits), EVEX a k register; the mask is cleared as elements arrive.

vgatherpf0dpd.summary: Prefetch gathered doubles into L1, 32-bit indices
vgatherpf0dpd.description: Hints that the double-precision elements at base + 32-bit index × scale, for each set mask bit, be brought into the L1 cache (T0 hint). Nothing is written to registers. Only on Xeon Phi (AVX512PF).
vgatherpf0dpd.operation: for each i with k[i]: prefetcht0 [base + idx32[i]*scale]

vgatherpf0dps.summary: Prefetch gathered singles into L1, 32-bit indices
vgatherpf0dps.description: Hints that the single-precision elements at base + 32-bit index × scale, for each set mask bit, be brought into the L1 cache (T0 hint). Nothing is written to registers. Only on Xeon Phi (AVX512PF).
vgatherpf0dps.operation: for each i with k[i]: prefetcht0 [base + idx32[i]*scale]

vgatherpf0qpd.summary: Prefetch gathered doubles into L1, 64-bit indices
vgatherpf0qpd.description: Hints that the double-precision elements at base + 64-bit index × scale, for each set mask bit, be brought into the L1 cache (T0 hint). Nothing is written to registers. Only on Xeon Phi (AVX512PF).
vgatherpf0qpd.operation: for each i with k[i]: prefetcht0 [base + idx64[i]*scale]

vgatherpf0qps.summary: Prefetch gathered singles into L1, 64-bit indices
vgatherpf0qps.description: Hints that the single-precision elements at base + 64-bit index × scale, for each set mask bit, be brought into the L1 cache (T0 hint). Nothing is written to registers. Only on Xeon Phi (AVX512PF).
vgatherpf0qps.operation: for each i with k[i]: prefetcht0 [base + idx64[i]*scale]

vgatherpf1dpd.summary: Prefetch gathered doubles into L2, 32-bit indices
vgatherpf1dpd.description: Hints that the double-precision elements at base + 32-bit index × scale, for each set mask bit, be brought into the L2 cache (T1 hint). Nothing is written to registers. Only on Xeon Phi (AVX512PF).
vgatherpf1dpd.operation: for each i with k[i]: prefetcht1 [base + idx32[i]*scale]

vgatherpf1dps.summary: Prefetch gathered singles into L2, 32-bit indices
vgatherpf1dps.description: Hints that the single-precision elements at base + 32-bit index × scale, for each set mask bit, be brought into the L2 cache (T1 hint). Nothing is written to registers. Only on Xeon Phi (AVX512PF).
vgatherpf1dps.operation: for each i with k[i]: prefetcht1 [base + idx32[i]*scale]

vgatherpf1qpd.summary: Prefetch gathered doubles into L2, 64-bit indices
vgatherpf1qpd.description: Hints that the double-precision elements at base + 64-bit index × scale, for each set mask bit, be brought into the L2 cache (T1 hint). Nothing is written to registers. Only on Xeon Phi (AVX512PF).
vgatherpf1qpd.operation: for each i with k[i]: prefetcht1 [base + idx64[i]*scale]

vgatherpf1qps.summary: Prefetch gathered singles into L2, 64-bit indices
vgatherpf1qps.description: Hints that the single-precision elements at base + 64-bit index × scale, for each set mask bit, be brought into the L2 cache (T1 hint). Nothing is written to registers. Only on Xeon Phi (AVX512PF).
vgatherpf1qps.operation: for each i with k[i]: prefetcht1 [base + idx64[i]*scale]

vgatherqpd.description: Loads double-precision elements from base + index × scale, with 64-bit indices taken from a vector, wherever the mask selects them. VEX takes a vector mask (sign bits), EVEX a k register; the mask is cleared as elements arrive.

vgatherqps.description: Loads single-precision elements from base + index × scale, with 64-bit indices taken from a vector, wherever the mask selects them. VEX takes a vector mask (sign bits), EVEX a k register; the mask is cleared as elements arrive. The result is half as wide as the index vector.

vgetexpbf16.description: Writes floor(log2(|x|)) of each BF16 element as a floating-point value, i.e. its unbiased exponent; denormals are normalized first and zero gives −infinity. AVX10.2, with masking and broadcast.

vgetexppd.description: Writes floor(log2(|x|)) of each double element as a floating-point value, i.e. its unbiased exponent; denormals are normalized first and zero gives −infinity. AVX512F, with masking and broadcast.

vgetexpph.description: Writes floor(log2(|x|)) of each FP16 element as a floating-point value, i.e. its unbiased exponent; denormals are normalized first and zero gives −infinity. AVX512-FP16, with masking and broadcast.

vgetexpps.description: Writes floor(log2(|x|)) of each single element as a floating-point value, i.e. its unbiased exponent; denormals are normalized first and zero gives −infinity. AVX512F, with masking and broadcast.

vgetexpsd.description: Writes floor(log2(|x|)) of the third operand's low double element as a floating-point value; the other elements come from the second operand. Zero gives −infinity. AVX512F, with masking and SAE.

vgetexpsh.description: Writes floor(log2(|x|)) of the third operand's low FP16 element as a floating-point value; the other elements come from the second operand. Zero gives −infinity. AVX512-FP16, with masking and SAE.

vgetexpss.description: Writes floor(log2(|x|)) of the third operand's low single element as a floating-point value; the other elements come from the second operand. Zero gives −infinity. AVX512F, with masking and SAE.

vgetmantbf16.description: Returns each BF16 element's mantissa scaled into the interval chosen by imm8[1:0] ([1,2), [1/2,2), [1/2,1) or [3/4,3/2)), with imm8[3:2] setting the sign. Used with vgetexp to split values in math libraries. AVX10.2.
vgetmantbf16.operation: dst[i] = mantissa(src[i], interval = imm8[1:0], sign = imm8[3:2])

vgetmantpd.description: Returns each double element's mantissa scaled into the interval chosen by imm8[1:0] ([1,2), [1/2,2), [1/2,1) or [3/4,3/2)), with imm8[3:2] setting the sign. Used with vgetexp to split values in math libraries. AVX512F.
vgetmantpd.operation: dst[i] = mantissa(src[i], interval = imm8[1:0], sign = imm8[3:2])

vgetmantph.description: Returns each FP16 element's mantissa scaled into the interval chosen by imm8[1:0] ([1,2), [1/2,2), [1/2,1) or [3/4,3/2)), with imm8[3:2] setting the sign. Used with vgetexp to split values in math libraries. AVX512-FP16.
vgetmantph.operation: dst[i] = mantissa(src[i], interval = imm8[1:0], sign = imm8[3:2])

vgetmantps.description: Returns each single element's mantissa scaled into the interval chosen by imm8[1:0] ([1,2), [1/2,2), [1/2,1) or [3/4,3/2)), with imm8[3:2] setting the sign. Used with vgetexp to split values in math libraries. AVX512F.
vgetmantps.operation: dst[i] = mantissa(src[i], interval = imm8[1:0], sign = imm8[3:2])

vgetmantsd.description: Returns the third operand's low double mantissa scaled into the interval chosen by imm8[1:0], with imm8[3:2] setting the sign; the other elements come from the second operand. AVX512F.
vgetmantsd.operation: dst[0] = mantissa(src3[0], imm8); upper from src2

vgetmantsh.description: Returns the third operand's low FP16 mantissa scaled into the interval chosen by imm8[1:0], with imm8[3:2] setting the sign; the other elements come from the second operand. AVX512-FP16.
vgetmantsh.operation: dst[0] = mantissa(src3[0], imm8); upper from src2

vgetmantss.description: Returns the third operand's low single mantissa scaled into the interval chosen by imm8[1:0], with imm8[3:2] setting the sign; the other elements come from the second operand. AVX512F.
vgetmantss.operation: dst[0] = mantissa(src3[0], imm8); upper from src2

vgf2p8affineinvqb.description: Inverts each byte of the second operand in GF(2^8) (the AES polynomial), then applies A·x ⊕ imm8, with A the 8×8 bit matrix in the matching qword of the third operand. With the right matrix this is the AES S-box. VEX and EVEX forms.

vgf2p8affineqb.description: Applies A·x ⊕ imm8 over GF(2) to each byte of the second operand, with A the 8×8 bit matrix in the matching qword of the third operand. Often used for arbitrary bit permutations, byte shifts and rotates. VEX and EVEX forms.

vgf2p8mulb.description: Multiplies the bytes of the second and third operands pairwise in GF(2^8), reducing by the AES polynomial x^8 + x^4 + x^3 + x + 1. VEX and EVEX forms, the latter with byte masking.

vhaddpd.description: Adds adjacent pairs of doubles: in each 128-bit lane the low result is the sum of the second operand's two elements and the high result the sum of the third's. Slower than a shuffle plus add on many CPUs.
vhaddpd.operation: per lane: dst[0] = a[0] + a[1]; dst[1] = b[0] + b[1]

vhaddps.description: Adds adjacent pairs of floats within each 128-bit lane: the two low results come from the second operand, the two high ones from the third. Common in dot products and reductions.
vhaddps.operation: per lane: dst = {a0+a1, a2+a3, b0+b1, b2+b3}

vhsubpd.description: Subtracts within adjacent pairs of doubles: in each 128-bit lane the low result is the second operand's low element minus its high one, the high result the same for the third operand.
vhsubpd.operation: per lane: dst[0] = a[0] - a[1]; dst[1] = b[0] - b[1]

vhsubps.description: Subtracts the odd float from the even one in each adjacent pair, per 128-bit lane: the two low results come from the second operand, the two high ones from the third.
vhsubps.operation: per lane: dst = {a0-a1, a2-a3, b0-b1, b2-b3}

vinsertf128.description: Copies the second operand into the destination and replaces one part of it with the 128-bit value from the third operand (register or memory). AVX; imm8[0] picks the half of the ymm register.

vinsertf32x4.description: Copies the second operand into the destination and replaces one part of it with the 128-bit value from the third operand (register or memory). AVX-512; imm8 picks the 128-bit lane, masking per 32-bit element.

vinsertf32x8.description: Copies the second operand into the destination and replaces one part of it with the 256-bit value from the third operand (register or memory). AVX512DQ; imm8[0] picks the half of the zmm register, masking per 32-bit element.

vinsertf64x2.description: Copies the second operand into the destination and replaces one part of it with the 128-bit value from the third operand (register or memory). AVX512DQ; imm8 picks the 128-bit lane, masking per 64-bit element.

vinsertf64x4.description: Copies the second operand into the destination and replaces one part of it with the 256-bit value from the third operand (register or memory). AVX-512; imm8[0] picks the half of the zmm register, masking per 64-bit element.

vinserti128.description: Copies the second operand into the destination and replaces one part of it with the 128-bit value from the third operand (register or memory). AVX2; imm8[0] picks the half of the ymm register.

vinserti32x4.description: Copies the second operand into the destination and replaces one part of it with the 128-bit value from the third operand (register or memory). AVX-512; imm8 picks the 128-bit lane, masking per dword.

vinserti32x8.description: Copies the second operand into the destination and replaces one part of it with the 256-bit value from the third operand (register or memory). AVX512DQ; imm8[0] picks the half of the zmm register, masking per dword.

vinserti64x2.description: Copies the second operand into the destination and replaces one part of it with the 128-bit value from the third operand (register or memory). AVX512DQ; imm8 picks the 128-bit lane, masking per qword.

vinserti64x4.description: Copies the second operand into the destination and replaces one part of it with the 256-bit value from the third operand (register or memory). AVX-512; imm8[0] picks the half of the zmm register, masking per qword.

vinsertps.description: Copies the second operand, puts one float from the third into the element chosen by imm8[5:4] and zeroes the elements set in imm8[3:0]. From a register imm8[7:6] picks the source element; from memory one float is loaded.
vinsertps.operation: dst = src2; dst[imm8[5:4]] = src3[imm8[7:6]]; zero where imm8[3:0]

vlddqu.description: Loads 128 or 256 bits from memory with no alignment requirement. On some older CPUs it handled loads that straddle cache lines faster than vmovdqu; on modern ones the two behave the same.

vldmxcsr.description: Loads the 32-bit MXCSR register from memory, setting SSE/AVX rounding mode, exception masks, flush-to-zero and denormals-are-zero. Setting reserved bits raises #GP.

vmaskmovdqu.description: Stores the bytes of the first operand to the address in rdi (edi) wherever the matching byte of the second operand has its top bit set. Carries a non-temporal hint and is slow on many CPUs.
vmaskmovdqu.operation: for i in 0..15: if (src2.b[i] & 0x80) [rdi + i] = src1.b[i]

vmaskmovpd.summary: Masked load or store, packed double
vmaskmovpd.description: Loads or stores only the double elements whose mask element (the middle operand) has its sign bit set; masked-off loads read zero and masked-off elements never fault. AVX, xmm or ymm.
vmaskmovpd.operation: load: dst[i] = mask[i] < 0 ? [mem + i] : 0; store: if (mask[i] < 0) [mem + i] = src[i]

vmaskmovps.summary: Masked load or store, packed single
vmaskmovps.description: Loads or stores only the single elements whose mask element (the middle operand) has its sign bit set; masked-off loads read zero and masked-off elements never fault. AVX, xmm or ymm.
vmaskmovps.operation: load: dst[i] = mask[i] < 0 ? [mem + i] : 0; store: if (mask[i] < 0) [mem + i] = src[i]

vmaxbf16.description: Writes the larger of each pair of BF16 elements from the second and third operands. If either is NaN, or both are zero, the third operand is returned, so the operation is not commutative. AVX10.2, EVEX only, with masking and broadcast.

vmaxpd.description: Writes the larger of each pair of double elements from the second and third operands. If either is NaN, or both are zero, the third operand is returned, so the operation is not commutative. VEX and EVEX forms, the latter with masking and broadcast.

vmaxph.description: Writes the larger of each pair of FP16 elements from the second and third operands. If either is NaN, or both are zero, the third operand is returned, so the operation is not commutative. AVX512-FP16, with masking and broadcast.

vmaxps.description: Writes the larger of each pair of single elements from the second and third operands. If either is NaN, or both are zero, the third operand is returned, so the operation is not commutative. VEX and EVEX forms, the latter with masking and broadcast.

vmaxsd.description: Writes the larger of the low double elements of the second and third operands; the other elements come from the second. A NaN or two zeros return the third operand, so the order matters. VEX or EVEX with masking.
vmaxsd.operation: dst[0] = src2[0] > src3[0] ? src2[0] : src3[0]; upper from src2

vmaxsh.description: Writes the larger of the low FP16 elements of the second and third operands; the other elements come from the second. A NaN or two zeros return the third operand, so the order matters. AVX512-FP16.
vmaxsh.operation: dst[0] = src2[0] > src3[0] ? src2[0] : src3[0]; upper from src2

vmaxss.description: Writes the larger of the low single elements of the second and third operands; the other elements come from the second. A NaN or two zeros return the third operand, so the order matters. VEX or EVEX with masking.
vmaxss.operation: dst[0] = src2[0] > src3[0] ? src2[0] : src3[0]; upper from src2

vmcall.description: Lets a guest running under Intel VMX call into the virtual machine monitor, causing a VM exit; the VMM reads the request from registers. Outside VMX non-root operation it fails or invokes the SMM monitor.

vmclear.description: Takes the physical address of a VMCS from the 64-bit memory operand, writes any cached state for it back to memory and marks it clear and inactive, so it can be launched again or moved to another CPU. VMX root only.

vmfunc.description: Lets a VMX guest run a function chosen by eax without a VM exit; function 0 switches the EPT pointer to the entry selected by ecx from a list the hypervisor prepared.

vminbf16.description: Writes the smaller of each pair of BF16 elements from the second and third operands. If either is NaN, or both are zero, the third operand is returned, so the operation is not commutative. AVX10.2, EVEX only, with masking and broadcast.

vminmaxbf16.summary: IEEE minimum or maximum, packed BF16
vminmaxbf16.description: Computes an IEEE 754-2019 minimum or maximum of each pair of BF16 elements; imm8 chooses min or max, by value or by magnitude, how NaNs propagate and the result's sign. AVX10.2, with masking and broadcast.

vminmaxpd.summary: IEEE minimum or maximum, packed double
vminmaxpd.description: Computes an IEEE 754-2019 minimum or maximum of each pair of double elements; imm8 chooses min or max, by value or by magnitude, how NaNs propagate and the result's sign. AVX10.2, with masking and broadcast.

vminmaxph.summary: IEEE minimum or maximum, packed FP16
vminmaxph.description: Computes an IEEE 754-2019 minimum or maximum of each pair of FP16 elements; imm8 chooses min or max, by value or by magnitude, how NaNs propagate and the result's sign. AVX10.2, with masking and broadcast.

vminmaxps.summary: IEEE minimum or maximum, packed single
vminmaxps.description: Computes an IEEE 754-2019 minimum or maximum of each pair of single elements; imm8 chooses min or max, by value or by magnitude, how NaNs propagate and the result's sign. AVX10.2, with masking and broadcast.

vminmaxsd.summary: IEEE minimum or maximum, scalar double
vminmaxsd.description: Computes an IEEE 754-2019 minimum or maximum of the low double elements; imm8 chooses min or max, by value or by magnitude, NaN handling and sign. The other elements come from the second operand. AVX10.2.
vminmaxsd.operation: dst[0] = minmax(src2[0], src3[0], imm8); upper from src2

vminmaxsh.summary: IEEE minimum or maximum, scalar FP16
vminmaxsh.description: Computes an IEEE 754-2019 minimum or maximum of the low FP16 elements; imm8 chooses min or max, by value or by magnitude, NaN handling and sign. The other elements come from the second operand. AVX10.2.
vminmaxsh.operation: dst[0] = minmax(src2[0], src3[0], imm8); upper from src2

vminmaxss.summary: IEEE minimum or maximum, scalar single
vminmaxss.description: Computes an IEEE 754-2019 minimum or maximum of the low single elements; imm8 chooses min or max, by value or by magnitude, NaN handling and sign. The other elements come from the second operand. AVX10.2.
vminmaxss.operation: dst[0] = minmax(src2[0], src3[0], imm8); upper from src2

vminpd.description: Writes the smaller of each pair of double elements from the second and third operands. If either is NaN, or both are zero, the third operand is returned, so the operation is not commutative. VEX and EVEX forms, the latter with masking and broadcast.

vminph.description: Writes the smaller of each pair of FP16 elements from the second and third operands. If either is NaN, or both are zero, the third operand is returned, so the operation is not commutative. AVX512-FP16, with masking and broadcast.

vminps.description: Writes the smaller of each pair of single elements from the second and third operands. If either is NaN, or both are zero, the third operand is returned, so the operation is not commutative. VEX and EVEX forms, the latter with masking and broadcast.

vminsd.description: Writes the smaller of the low double elements of the second and third operands; the other elements come from the second. A NaN or two zeros return the third operand, so the order matters. VEX or EVEX with masking.
vminsd.operation: dst[0] = src2[0] < src3[0] ? src2[0] : src3[0]; upper from src2

vminsh.description: Writes the smaller of the low FP16 elements of the second and third operands; the other elements come from the second. A NaN or two zeros return the third operand, so the order matters. AVX512-FP16.
vminsh.operation: dst[0] = src2[0] < src3[0] ? src2[0] : src3[0]; upper from src2

vminss.description: Writes the smaller of the low single elements of the second and third operands; the other elements come from the second. A NaN or two zeros return the third operand, so the order matters. VEX or EVEX with masking.
vminss.operation: dst[0] = src2[0] < src3[0] ? src2[0] : src3[0]; upper from src2

vmlaunch.description: Enters the guest described by the current VMCS for the first time after vmclear, loading guest state from it. On failure execution continues with the error reported in RFLAGS. VMX root only; later entries use vmresume.

vmload.description: AMD SVM: loads the processor state that vmrun does not switch (FS, GS, TR and LDTR with hidden parts, KernelGSBase, the syscall and sysenter MSRs) from the VMCB whose physical address is in rax. Privileged.
vmload.operation: load FS, GS, TR, LDTR, syscall/sysenter MSRs from VMCB[rax]

vmmcall.description: AMD SVM counterpart of vmcall: a guest uses it to request a service from the hypervisor, which intercepts it as a VM exit. Without a hypervisor intercepting it, it raises #UD.

vmovapd.description: Copies a whole xmm, ymm or zmm vector of doubles between registers or to/from memory, which must be aligned to the vector size or #GP is raised. EVEX forms mask per 64-bit element, merging or zeroing.

vmovaps.description: Copies a whole xmm, ymm or zmm vector between registers or to/from memory aligned to the vector size (otherwise #GP). Compilers use it for any aligned vector copy; EVEX forms mask per 32-bit element.

vmovd.summary: Move doubleword to or from vector
vmovd.description: Moves 32 bits between a general register or memory and the low element of an xmm register; writing the xmm zeroes all its other bits. AVX10.2 adds an xmm-to-xmm form that keeps only the low dword.

vmovddup.description: Copies each even-indexed double into itself and the next element: the low double of every 128-bit lane fills the whole lane. The xmm form loads only 64 bits from memory, making it a cheap broadcast.

vmovdqa.description: Copies 128 or 256 bits of integer data between registers or to/from memory aligned to 16 or 32 bytes; a misaligned address raises #GP. VEX only; AVX-512 uses vmovdqa32 or vmovdqa64.

vmovdqa32.description: Copies an xmm, ymm or zmm vector of 32-bit integers between registers or to/from memory aligned to the vector size, applying a write mask per 32-bit element that merges or zeroes. AVX512F.

vmovdqa64.description: Copies an xmm, ymm or zmm vector of 64-bit integers between registers or to/from memory aligned to the vector size, applying a write mask per 64-bit element that merges or zeroes. AVX512F.

vmovdqu.description: Copies 128 or 256 bits of integer data between registers or to/from memory at any alignment. The usual way compilers load and store integer vectors; VEX only, AVX-512 uses vmovdqu8/16/32/64.

vmovdqu16.description: Copies an xmm, ymm or zmm vector between registers or to/from memory at any alignment, with a write mask per 16-bit element that merges or zeroes. Masked-off memory elements do not fault, so it suits loop tails. AVX512BW.

vmovdqu32.description: Copies an xmm, ymm or zmm vector between registers or to/from memory at any alignment, with a write mask per 32-bit element that merges or zeroes. Masked-off memory elements do not fault, so it suits loop tails. AVX512F.

vmovdqu64.description: Copies an xmm, ymm or zmm vector between registers or to/from memory at any alignment, with a write mask per 64-bit element that merges or zeroes. Masked-off memory elements do not fault, so it suits loop tails. AVX512F.

vmovdqu8.description: Copies an xmm, ymm or zmm vector between registers or to/from memory at any alignment, with a write mask per byte that merges or zeroes. Masked-off memory elements do not fault, so it suits loop tails. AVX512BW.

vmovhlps.summary: Move high to low packed single
vmovhlps.description: Builds the result from two registers: the low 64 bits are the high 64 bits of the third operand, the high 64 bits come from the high half of the second operand. Often used to fold a vector in half during a reduction.

vmovhpd.description: Load form: the high 64 bits (double) come from memory and the low 64 bits from the second operand. Store form: writes the high 64 bits of the register to memory.

vmovhps.description: Load form: the high 64 bits (two singles) come from memory and the low 64 bits from the second operand. Store form: writes the high 64 bits of the register to memory.

vmovlhps.summary: Move low to high packed single
vmovlhps.description: Builds the result from two registers: the low 64 bits come from the second operand's low half and the high 64 bits are the low 64 bits of the third operand.

vmovlpd.description: Load form: the low 64 bits (double) come from memory and the high 64 bits from the second operand. Store form: writes the low 64 bits of the register to memory.

vmovlps.description: Load form: the low 64 bits (two singles) come from memory and the high 64 bits from the second operand. Store form: writes the low 64 bits of the register to memory.

vmovmskpd.description: Collects the sign bits of the 2 or 4 doubles of an xmm or ymm register into the low bits of a general register, zeroing the rest. Used to branch on the result of a vector compare.

vmovmskps.description: Collects the sign bits of the 4 or 8 floats of an xmm or ymm register into the low bits of a general register, zeroing the rest. Used to branch on, or count, the lanes of a vector compare.

vmovntdq.description: Stores an xmm, ymm or zmm register to aligned memory with a hint to bypass the caches, so large copies or fills do not evict useful data. The stores are weakly ordered; follow them with sfence before another thread reads the data.

vmovntdqa.description: Loads an aligned 128-, 256- or 512-bit vector with a streaming hint. On write-combining memory (such as video memory) it fetches a whole line into a streaming buffer; on ordinary memory it behaves much like an aligned load.

vmovntpd.description: Stores a vector of double-precision values to aligned memory while avoiding the caches. Used for large output buffers that will not be read again soon; needs sfence before the data is shared.

vmovntps.description: Stores a vector of single-precision values to aligned memory while avoiding the caches. Used for streaming writes of large arrays; needs sfence before the data is shared.

vmovq.description: Copies 64 bits between the low quadword of an xmm register and a general register, memory or another xmm register. When the destination is an xmm register, its bits above 63 are cleared up to the full vector width.

vmovrsb.description: Loads a vector of bytes like an unaligned load, with a hint that the cache line is mostly read by many cores, so the processor can avoid taking exclusive ownership of it. Supports masking of individual bytes.

vmovrsd.description: Loads a vector of 32-bit elements with a hint that the data is shared read-mostly between cores, reducing cache-line ownership traffic. Supports per-element masking with merge or zeroing.

vmovrsq.description: Loads a vector of 64-bit elements with a hint that the data is shared read-mostly between cores, reducing cache-line ownership traffic. Supports per-element masking with merge or zeroing.

vmovrsw.description: Loads a vector of 16-bit elements with a hint that the data is shared read-mostly between cores, reducing cache-line ownership traffic. Supports per-element masking with merge or zeroing.
