vmovsd.description: Moves one double. A load from memory clears the rest of the register; a store writes only 64 bits. The register-to-register form takes the low double from the third operand and the upper bits from the second.
vmovsd.operation: load: dst = zx(m64); reg: dst = {a[127:64], b[63:0]}

vmovsh.description: Moves one 16-bit floating-point value. A load clears the rest of the destination register, a store writes 16 bits, and the three-register form takes the low half from the third operand and the remaining bits from the second.
vmovsh.operation: load: dst = zx(m16); reg: dst = {a[127:16], b[15:0]}

vmovshdup.description: Copies each odd-numbered float into both itself and the even slot below it. Often used with vmovsldup for complex-number multiplication.

vmovsldup.description: Copies each even-numbered float into both itself and the odd slot above it. Often used with vmovshdup for complex-number multiplication.

vmovss.description: Moves one float. A load from memory clears the rest of the register; a store writes only 32 bits. The register-to-register form takes the low float from the third operand and the upper bits from the second.
vmovss.operation: load: dst = zx(m32); reg: dst = {a[127:32], b[31:0]}

vmovupd.description: Loads, stores or copies a vector of doubles with no alignment requirement. EVEX forms can mask elements, merging or zeroing the unselected ones; masked-off elements in memory are not touched and do not fault.

vmovups.description: Loads, stores or copies a vector of floats with no alignment requirement. Compilers also use it for generic memory copies. EVEX forms can mask elements; masked-off memory is not touched.

vmovw.summary: Move word to or from vector
vmovw.description: Copies 16 bits between the low word of an xmm register and a general register or memory. Moving into xmm clears the rest of the vector; moving into a general register zero-extends.
vmovw.operation: xmm: dst = zx(src[15:0]); gpr: dst = zx(xmm[15:0])

vmpsadbw.summary: Multiple sums of absolute byte differences
vmpsadbw.description: Computes eight 16-bit sums of absolute differences between a fixed 4-byte block of the third operand and sliding 4-byte windows of the second, with offsets chosen by imm8. Used in video motion estimation.

vmptrld.description: Makes the VMCS at the given physical address the current one for this logical processor, so later vmread, vmwrite and vmlaunch use it. Only a hypervisor in VMX root mode can run it.

vmptrst.description: Writes the physical address of the current VMCS to memory. Used by a hypervisor to save which virtual machine control structure is active.

vmread.description: Reads the field of the current VMCS whose encoding is in the second operand and writes its value to the first operand. Failure is reported through CF and ZF. Hypervisor-only.

vmresume.description: Enters the guest described by the current VMCS, which must already have been launched with vmlaunch. Execution continues in the guest until the next VM exit.

vmrun.description: Saves host state and enters the guest whose VMCB is at the physical address in rAX, running it until a #VMEXIT. Part of AMD's Secure Virtual Machine extension.
vmrun.operation: save host; load guest from VMCB[rax]; run

vmsave.description: Stores processor state that vmrun does not switch, such as FS, GS, TR, LDTR and the syscall/sysenter MSRs, into the VMCB at the physical address in rAX. Paired with vmload.
vmsave.operation: VMCB[rax] = fs, gs, tr, ldtr, syscall MSRs

vmulbf16.description: Multiplies corresponding bfloat16 elements of two vectors. An AVX10.2 instruction with masking and 16-bit broadcast; rounding is to nearest even, and denormals are treated as zero.

vmulpd.description: Multiplies corresponding doubles of the second and third operands into the first. VEX forms cover 128/256 bits; EVEX adds 512 bits, masking, 64-bit broadcast and static rounding.

vmulph.description: Multiplies corresponding FP16 elements of two vectors. AVX512-FP16 forms support 128 to 512 bits, masking, 16-bit broadcast and static rounding on the 512-bit register form.

vmulps.description: Multiplies corresponding floats of the second and third operands into the first. VEX forms cover 128/256 bits; EVEX adds 512 bits, masking, 32-bit broadcast and static rounding.

vmulsd.description: Multiplies the low doubles of the second and third operands; the upper 64 bits of the result come from the second operand and higher bits are cleared. EVEX allows masking and static rounding.

vmulsh.description: Multiplies the low FP16 values of the second and third operands; bits 16 to 127 come from the second operand and higher bits are cleared. Supports masking and static rounding.

vmulss.description: Multiplies the low floats of the second and third operands; bits 32 to 127 come from the second operand and higher bits are cleared. EVEX allows masking and static rounding.

vmwrite.description: Writes the value of the second operand into the field of the current VMCS whose encoding is in the first operand. Failure is reported through CF and ZF. Hypervisor-only.

vmxoff.description: Takes the processor out of VMX root mode, after which virtualization instructions fault until the next vmxon. Run by a hypervisor when it shuts down.

vmxon.description: Puts the processor into VMX root mode, using the 4 KB VMXON region at the physical address given in memory. Requires CR4.VMXE set and is the first step of an Intel hypervisor.

vorpd.description: ORs the bits of two vectors holding doubles into the first operand. Used for sign manipulation such as copysign; EVEX forms add masking and 64-bit broadcast.

vorps.description: ORs the bits of two vectors holding floats into the first operand. Used for setting sign bits and combining masks; EVEX forms add masking and 32-bit broadcast.

vp2intersectd.summary: Intersect doubleword vectors into mask pair
vp2intersectd.description: Compares every 32-bit element of one vector with every element of the other and writes two masks: the named k register marks elements of the first source found in the second, the next k register marks the reverse.

vp2intersectq.summary: Intersect quadword vectors into mask pair
vp2intersectq.description: Compares every 64-bit element of one vector with every element of the other and writes two masks: the named k register marks elements of the first source found in the second, the next k register marks the reverse.

vp4dpwssd.summary: Four-step signed word dot product accumulate
vp4dpwssd.description: Xeon Phi (4VNNIW) instruction that runs four word-pair dot products in a row: a block of four consecutive zmm registers is multiplied by four word pairs from memory, and the 32-bit sums are added to the destination.
vp4dpwssd.operation: for r in 0..3: dst.d[i] += src[r].w[2i]*m.w[2r] + src[r].w[2i+1]*m.w[2r+1]

vp4dpwssds.description: Like vp4dpwssd, accumulates four steps of signed word-pair dot products from four consecutive zmm registers and memory, but each addition to the 32-bit accumulator saturates instead of wrapping.
vp4dpwssds.operation: for r in 0..3: dst.d[i] = sat32(dst.d[i] + dot(src[r], m.pair[r]))

vpabsb.description: Replaces each signed byte with its absolute value. The value -128 has no positive counterpart and comes out as 0x80, which reads correctly only as unsigned 128.

vpabsd.description: Replaces each signed 32-bit element with its absolute value; INT_MIN stays 0x80000000. EVEX forms add masking and 32-bit broadcast.

vpabsq.description: Replaces each signed 64-bit element with its absolute value; the most negative value stays unchanged. Available only in AVX-512 with masking and 64-bit broadcast.

vpabsw.description: Replaces each signed 16-bit element with its absolute value; -32768 stays 0x8000. EVEX forms add masking.

vpackssdw.summary: Pack doublewords to words, signed saturation
vpackssdw.description: Narrows signed 32-bit elements of both sources to signed 16-bit values, clamping to -32768..32767. Within each 128-bit lane the low half comes from the second operand and the high half from the third.

vpacksswb.summary: Pack words to bytes, signed saturation
vpacksswb.description: Narrows signed 16-bit elements of both sources to signed bytes, clamping to -128..127. Within each 128-bit lane the low half comes from the second operand and the high half from the third.

vpackusdw.summary: Pack doublewords to words, unsigned saturation
vpackusdw.description: Narrows signed 32-bit elements of both sources to unsigned 16-bit values, clamping negatives to 0 and large values to 65535. Lanes are interleaved per 128 bits as in vpackssdw.

vpackuswb.summary: Pack words to bytes, unsigned saturation
vpackuswb.description: Narrows signed 16-bit elements of both sources to unsigned bytes, clamping to 0..255. Common in image code to turn intermediate results back into pixels; results are ordered per 128-bit lane.

vpaddb.description: Adds corresponding bytes of the second and third operands, wrapping on overflow, and writes the first. EVEX forms support 512 bits and masking.

vpaddd.description: Adds corresponding 32-bit integers, wrapping on overflow. One of the most common vectorized integer operations; EVEX adds 512 bits, masking and 32-bit broadcast.

vpaddq.description: Adds corresponding 64-bit integers, wrapping on overflow. Also used for pointer arithmetic in vectorized loops; EVEX adds masking and 64-bit broadcast.

vpaddsb.summary: Packed signed byte add with saturation
vpaddsb.description: Adds corresponding signed bytes, clamping results to -128..127 instead of wrapping. Useful in audio and image processing.

vpaddsw.summary: Packed signed word add with saturation
vpaddsw.description: Adds corresponding signed 16-bit integers, clamping results to -32768..32767 instead of wrapping. Common in fixed-point audio code.

vpaddusb.summary: Packed unsigned byte add with saturation
vpaddusb.description: Adds corresponding unsigned bytes, clamping results at 255 instead of wrapping. Typical for brightening pixels or blending.

vpaddusw.summary: Packed unsigned word add with saturation
vpaddusw.description: Adds corresponding unsigned 16-bit integers, clamping results at 65535 instead of wrapping.

vpaddw.description: Adds corresponding 16-bit integers of the second and third operands, wrapping on overflow. EVEX forms support 512 bits and masking.

vpalignr.description: In each 128-bit lane, joins the second operand (high) and third operand (low) into 32 bytes, shifts right by imm8 bytes and keeps the low 16. Used to read unaligned windows across two loaded blocks.

vpand.description: ANDs the bits of the second and third operands into the first. The VEX-only 128/256-bit form; AVX-512 uses vpandd or vpandq, which add masking.

vpandd.description: ANDs two vectors bit by bit. The EVEX form whose mask and broadcast work on 32-bit elements; without a mask it is the same as vpandq.

vpandn.description: Inverts the second operand and ANDs it with the third, writing the first. Used to clear selected bits; the VEX-only form, with vpandnd/vpandnq in AVX-512.

vpandnd.summary: Bitwise AND NOT with doubleword masking
vpandnd.description: Inverts the second operand and ANDs it with the third. The EVEX form whose masking and broadcast work on 32-bit elements.

vpandnq.summary: Bitwise AND NOT with quadword masking
vpandnq.description: Inverts the second operand and ANDs it with the third. The EVEX form whose masking and broadcast work on 64-bit elements.

vpandq.description: ANDs two vectors bit by bit. The EVEX form whose mask and broadcast work on 64-bit elements; without a mask it is the same as vpandd.

vpavgb.description: Averages corresponding unsigned bytes, rounding halves up, without overflow. Used for image scaling and motion compensation.

vpavgw.description: Averages corresponding unsigned 16-bit integers, rounding halves up, computed with an extra bit so it never overflows.

vpblendd.description: Builds each 32-bit element from the third operand where the matching imm8 bit is 1, otherwise from the second. The selection is fixed at compile time.

vpblendmb.description: Selects each byte from the third operand where the k mask bit is set, otherwise from the second operand. With {z}, unselected bytes become zero instead.

vpblendmd.description: Selects each 32-bit element from the third operand where the k mask bit is set, otherwise from the second operand. Used by vectorized code for conditional assignments.

vpblendmq.description: Selects each 64-bit element from the third operand where the k mask bit is set, otherwise from the second operand. With {z}, unselected elements become zero.

vpblendmw.description: Selects each 16-bit element from the third operand where the k mask bit is set, otherwise from the second operand. With {z}, unselected elements become zero.

vpblendvb.description: Selects each byte from the third operand when the top bit of the matching byte in the fourth operand is set, otherwise from the second. Typically follows a compare that produced the mask.

vpblendw.description: Selects each 16-bit element from the third operand where the matching imm8 bit is 1, otherwise from the second; the same 8-bit pattern is applied to each 128-bit lane.

vpbroadcastb.description: Copies one byte from memory or the low byte of an xmm register (or, with EVEX, a general register) into every byte of the destination. Used for memchr-style searches.

vpbroadcastd.description: Copies one 32-bit value from memory, an xmm register or (with EVEX) a general register into every element of the destination. EVEX forms allow masking.

vpbroadcastmb2q.description: Zero-extends the low 8 bits of a k mask register to 64 bits and writes the value to every quadword of the destination. Part of AVX-512 conflict detection.

vpbroadcastmw2d.description: Zero-extends the low 16 bits of a k mask register to 32 bits and writes the value to every doubleword of the destination. Part of AVX-512 conflict detection.

vpbroadcastq.description: Copies one 64-bit value from memory, an xmm register or (with EVEX) a general register into every element of the destination. EVEX forms allow masking.

vpbroadcastw.description: Copies one 16-bit value from memory, an xmm register or (with EVEX) a general register into every element of the destination. EVEX forms allow masking.

vpclmulqdq.description: In each 128-bit lane, multiplies one 64-bit half of each source as polynomials over GF(2), giving a 128-bit product; imm8 bits 0 and 4 pick the halves. Used for GCM and CRC; LLVM may print aliases like vpclmullqlqdq.

vpcmov.description: AMD XOP select: for every bit, takes the second operand where the selector bit is 1 and the third operand where it is 0. The selector is the fourth operand.

vpcmpb.description: Compares signed bytes of two vectors with a predicate from imm8 and sets the matching bits of a k register. LLVM prints the predicate in the name: vpcmpltb, vpcmpleb, vpcmpneqb, vpcmpnltb, vpcmpnleb.

vpcmpd.description: Compares signed 32-bit elements with a predicate from imm8 and writes the results as bits of a k register. LLVM folds the predicate into the name (vpcmpltd, vpcmpled, vpcmpneqd…); 32-bit broadcast is allowed.

vpcmpeqb.description: Compares corresponding bytes for equality. VEX forms set each byte to all ones or zero; EVEX forms write one bit per byte into a k register. Common in strlen and memchr loops.

vpcmpeqd.description: Compares corresponding 32-bit elements for equality, producing all-ones/zero elements (VEX) or mask bits in a k register (EVEX). Comparing a register with itself is the usual way to make all ones.

vpcmpeqq.description: Compares corresponding 64-bit elements for equality, producing all-ones/zero elements (VEX) or mask bits in a k register (EVEX).

vpcmpeqw.description: Compares corresponding 16-bit elements for equality, producing all-ones/zero elements (VEX) or mask bits in a k register (EVEX). Used in UTF-16 string scanning.

vpcmpestri.description: Compares two string fragments of lengths given in eax and edx using the mode in imm8 (equal any, ranges, equal each, substring) and puts the index of the first or last match in ecx. Flags report match and string ends.
vpcmpestri.operation: ecx = index(strcmp_mode(a, eax, b, edx, imm8)); set CF ZF SF OF

vpcmpestrm.description: Compares two string fragments of lengths given in eax and edx using the mode in imm8 and writes the result mask (bits or expanded bytes/words) to xmm0. Flags report match and string ends.
vpcmpestrm.operation: xmm0 = mask(strcmp_mode(a, eax, b, edx, imm8)); set CF ZF SF OF

vpcmpgtb.summary: Compare signed bytes for greater than
vpcmpgtb.description: Sets each result byte to all ones where the byte in the second operand is greater than the one in the third, as signed values. VEX forms write a vector, EVEX forms a k mask.

vpcmpgtd.summary: Compare signed doublewords for greater than
vpcmpgtd.description: Sets each 32-bit result element to all ones where the second operand's element is greater than the third's, as signed integers. For unsigned compares code flips the sign bits first.

vpcmpgtq.summary: Compare signed quadwords for greater than
vpcmpgtq.description: Sets each 64-bit result element to all ones where the second operand's element is greater than the third's, as signed integers. EVEX forms write a k mask.

vpcmpgtw.summary: Compare signed words for greater than
vpcmpgtw.description: Sets each 16-bit result element to all ones where the second operand's element is greater than the third's, as signed integers. EVEX forms write a k mask.

vpcmpistri.description: Like vpcmpestri, but each string fragment ends at its first zero element instead of an explicit length. Puts the match index in ecx; used in fast strchr, strspn and strstr.
vpcmpistri.operation: ecx = index(strcmp_mode(a, b, imm8)); set CF ZF SF OF

vpcmpistrm.description: Like vpcmpestrm, but string fragments end at their first zero element. Writes the comparison mask to xmm0 and sets flags for match and string ends.
vpcmpistrm.operation: xmm0 = mask(strcmp_mode(a, b, imm8)); set CF ZF SF OF

vpcmpq.description: Compares signed 64-bit elements with a predicate from imm8 and writes result bits to a k register. LLVM folds the predicate into the name (vpcmpltq, vpcmpleq, vpcmpneqq…); 64-bit broadcast is allowed.

vpcmpub.description: Compares unsigned bytes with a predicate from imm8 and writes result bits to a k register. LLVM folds the predicate into the name, for example vpcmpltub or vpcmpnleub.

vpcmpud.description: Compares unsigned 32-bit elements with a predicate from imm8 and writes result bits to a k register. LLVM folds the predicate into the name (vpcmpltud, vpcmpleud…); 32-bit broadcast is allowed.

vpcmpuq.description: Compares unsigned 64-bit elements with a predicate from imm8 and writes result bits to a k register. LLVM folds the predicate into the name (vpcmpltuq, vpcmpleuq…); 64-bit broadcast is allowed.

vpcmpuw.description: Compares unsigned 16-bit elements with a predicate from imm8 and writes result bits to a k register. LLVM folds the predicate into the name, for example vpcmpltuw.

vpcmpw.description: Compares signed 16-bit elements with a predicate from imm8 and writes result bits to a k register. LLVM folds the predicate into the name, for example vpcmpltw or vpcmpneqw.

vpcomb.description: AMD XOP compare of signed bytes with a predicate from imm8 (lt, le, gt, ge, eq, neq, false, true), writing all ones or zero to each byte. LLVM prints the predicate in the name, such as vpcomltb.

vpcomd.description: AMD XOP compare of signed 32-bit elements with a predicate from imm8, writing all ones or zero to each element. LLVM prints the predicate in the name, such as vpcomgtd.

vpcompressb.description: Packs the bytes whose k mask bits are set into consecutive positions at the start of the destination. A memory destination receives only the selected bytes; a register destination gets the rest merged or zeroed.
vpcompressb.operation: j = 0; for i: if k[i] { dst.b[j++] = src.b[i] }

vpcompressd.description: Packs the 32-bit elements whose k mask bits are set into consecutive positions at the start of the destination. Used to vectorize filtering loops that keep only matching items.
vpcompressd.operation: j = 0; for i: if k[i] { dst.d[j++] = src.d[i] }

vpcompressq.description: Packs the 64-bit elements whose k mask bits are set into consecutive positions at the start of the destination; a memory store writes only those elements.
vpcompressq.operation: j = 0; for i: if k[i] { dst.q[j++] = src.q[i] }

vpcompressw.description: Packs the 16-bit elements whose k mask bits are set into consecutive positions at the start of the destination; a memory store writes only those elements.
vpcompressw.operation: j = 0; for i: if k[i] { dst.w[j++] = src.w[i] }

vpcomq.description: AMD XOP compare of signed 64-bit elements with a predicate from imm8, writing all ones or zero to each element. LLVM prints the predicate in the name, such as vpcomltq.

vpcomub.description: AMD XOP compare of unsigned bytes with a predicate from imm8, writing all ones or zero to each byte. LLVM prints the predicate in the name, such as vpcomltub.

vpcomud.description: AMD XOP compare of unsigned 32-bit elements with a predicate from imm8, writing all ones or zero to each element. LLVM prints the predicate in the name, such as vpcomgeud.

vpcomuq.description: AMD XOP compare of unsigned 64-bit elements with a predicate from imm8, writing all ones or zero to each element. LLVM prints the predicate in the name, such as vpcomltuq.

vpcomuw.description: AMD XOP compare of unsigned 16-bit elements with a predicate from imm8, writing all ones or zero to each element. LLVM prints the predicate in the name, such as vpcomequw.

vpcomw.description: AMD XOP compare of signed 16-bit elements with a predicate from imm8, writing all ones or zero to each element. LLVM prints the predicate in the name, such as vpcomlew.

vpconflictd.description: For each 32-bit element, writes a bit mask of the lower-numbered elements that hold the same value. Lets vectorized scatter or histogram loops find duplicate indices.

vpconflictq.description: For each 64-bit element, writes a bit mask of the lower-numbered elements that hold the same value. Used to handle repeated indices in vectorized scatter loops.

vpdpbssd.summary: Dot product of signed bytes, accumulate
vpdpbssd.description: For each 32-bit lane, multiplies four signed bytes of the second operand by four signed bytes of the third and adds the four products to the destination, wrapping on overflow. Used in int8 neural-network inference.

vpdpbssds.summary: Dot product of signed bytes, saturating
vpdpbssds.description: Like vpdpbssd, sums four signed-by-signed byte products into each 32-bit accumulator, but the final addition saturates to the signed 32-bit range.

vpdpbsud.summary: Dot product of signed by unsigned bytes
vpdpbsud.description: For each 32-bit lane, multiplies four signed bytes of the second operand by four unsigned bytes of the third and adds the products to the destination, wrapping on overflow.

vpdpbsuds.description: Like vpdpbsud, sums four products of signed bytes (second operand) and unsigned bytes (third operand) into each accumulator, with signed 32-bit saturation.

vpdpbusd.summary: Dot product of unsigned by signed bytes
vpdpbusd.description: The original VNNI instruction: for each 32-bit lane, multiplies four unsigned bytes of the second operand by four signed bytes of the third and adds the sum to the destination. The workhorse of int8 inference.

vpdpbusds.description: Like vpdpbusd, sums four products of unsigned bytes (second operand) and signed bytes (third operand) into each accumulator, with signed 32-bit saturation.

vpdpbuud.summary: Dot product of unsigned bytes, accumulate
vpdpbuud.description: For each 32-bit lane, multiplies four unsigned bytes of the second operand by four unsigned bytes of the third and adds the sum to the destination, wrapping on overflow.

vpdpbuuds.summary: Dot product of unsigned bytes, saturating
vpdpbuuds.description: Like vpdpbuud, sums four unsigned byte products into each 32-bit accumulator, but the result saturates to the unsigned 32-bit range.

vpdpwssd.summary: Dot product of signed words, accumulate
vpdpwssd.description: For each 32-bit lane, multiplies two pairs of signed 16-bit values from the second and third operands and adds both products to the destination, wrapping on overflow. Fuses vpmaddwd and vpaddd.

vpdpwssds.summary: Dot product of signed words, saturating
vpdpwssds.description: Like vpdpwssd, adds two signed word products to each 32-bit accumulator, but the addition saturates to the signed 32-bit range.

vpdpwsud.summary: Dot product of signed by unsigned words
vpdpwsud.description: For each 32-bit lane, multiplies two signed words of the second operand by two unsigned words of the third and adds the products to the destination, wrapping on overflow.

vpdpwsuds.description: Like vpdpwsud, adds two products of signed words (second operand) and unsigned words (third operand) to each accumulator, with signed 32-bit saturation.

vpdpwusd.summary: Dot product of unsigned by signed words
vpdpwusd.description: For each 32-bit lane, multiplies two unsigned words of the second operand by two signed words of the third and adds the products to the destination, wrapping on overflow.

vpdpwusds.description: Like vpdpwusd, adds two products of unsigned words (second operand) and signed words (third operand) to each accumulator, with signed 32-bit saturation.

vpdpwuud.summary: Dot product of unsigned words, accumulate
vpdpwuud.description: For each 32-bit lane, multiplies two unsigned words of the second operand by two unsigned words of the third and adds the products to the destination, wrapping on overflow.

vpdpwuuds.summary: Dot product of unsigned words, saturating
vpdpwuuds.description: Like vpdpwuud, adds two unsigned word products to each 32-bit accumulator, but the result saturates to the unsigned 32-bit range.

vperm2f128.description: Builds each 128-bit half of the ymm result from any of the four halves of the second and third operands, as chosen by imm8 bits 1:0 and 5:4; bits 3 and 7 zero a half instead.

vperm2i128.description: AVX2 integer twin of vperm2f128: each 128-bit half of the ymm result is any half of the two sources or zero, as chosen by imm8. Used to move data across the 128-bit lane boundary.

vpermb.description: Fills each byte of the destination with the byte of the third operand selected by the index in the matching byte of the second operand. Crosses lanes over the whole vector (AVX512-VBMI).

vpermd.description: Fills each 32-bit element with the element of the third operand chosen by the index in the second operand, across the whole vector. Note the index comes first in Intel syntax.

vpermi2b.description: Treats the second and third operands as one table of bytes and replaces each index byte in the destination with the byte it selects; the top index bit chooses the table.
vpermi2b.operation: dst.b[i] = (idx[log2 n] ? b : a).b[idx & (n-1)], idx = dst.b[i]

vpermi2d.description: The destination holds indices; each is replaced by the 32-bit element it selects from the combined table of the second and third operands. Masking applies at dword granularity.
vpermi2d.operation: dst.d[i] = (idx[log2 n] ? b : a).d[idx & (n-1)], idx = dst.d[i]

vpermi2pd.description: The destination holds indices; each is replaced by the double it selects from the combined table of the second and third operands. Supports masking and 64-bit broadcast.
vpermi2pd.operation: dst.q[i] = (idx[log2 n] ? b : a).q[idx & (n-1)], idx = dst.q[i]

vpermi2ps.description: The destination holds indices; each is replaced by the float it selects from the combined table of the second and third operands. Supports masking and 32-bit broadcast.
vpermi2ps.operation: dst.d[i] = (idx[log2 n] ? b : a).d[idx & (n-1)], idx = dst.d[i]

vpermi2q.description: The destination holds indices; each is replaced by the 64-bit element it selects from the combined table of the second and third operands.
vpermi2q.operation: dst.q[i] = (idx[log2 n] ? b : a).q[idx & (n-1)], idx = dst.q[i]

vpermi2w.description: The destination holds indices; each is replaced by the 16-bit element it selects from the combined table of the second and third operands.
vpermi2w.operation: dst.w[i] = (idx[log2 n] ? b : a).w[idx & (n-1)], idx = dst.w[i]

vpermil2pd.description: AMD XOP-era permute: within each 128-bit lane, every double is picked from either source by a selector element, and imm8 bits 1:0 can zero elements depending on the selector's match bit.

forms.heading: VEX.256.66.0F3A.W0 49 /r is4
syntax: vpermil2pd ymm, ymm, m256, ymm, imm8
vpermil2pd ymm, ymm, ymm, ymm, imm8

forms.heading: VEX.256.66.0F3A.W1 49 /r is4
syntax: vpermil2pd ymm, ymm, ymm, m256, imm8
vpermil2pd ymm, ymm, ymm, ymm, imm8

forms.heading: VEX.128.66.0F3A.W0 49 /r is4
syntax: vpermil2pd xmm, xmm, m128, xmm, imm8
vpermil2pd xmm, xmm, xmm, xmm, imm8

forms.heading: VEX.128.66.0F3A.W1 49 /r is4
syntax: vpermil2pd xmm, xmm, xmm, m128, imm8
vpermil2pd xmm, xmm, xmm, xmm, imm8

vpermil2ps.description: AMD XOP-era permute: within each 128-bit lane, every float is picked from the eight floats of both sources by a selector element, and imm8 bits 1:0 can zero elements based on the selector's bit 3.

forms.heading: VEX.256.66.0F3A.W0 48 /r is4
syntax: vpermil2ps ymm, ymm, m256, ymm, imm8
vpermil2ps ymm, ymm, ymm, ymm, imm8

forms.heading: VEX.256.66.0F3A.W1 48 /r is4
syntax: vpermil2ps ymm, ymm, ymm, m256, imm8
vpermil2ps ymm, ymm, ymm, ymm, imm8

forms.heading: VEX.128.66.0F3A.W0 48 /r is4
syntax: vpermil2ps xmm, xmm, m128, xmm, imm8
vpermil2ps xmm, xmm, xmm, xmm, imm8

forms.heading: VEX.128.66.0F3A.W1 48 /r is4
syntax: vpermil2ps xmm, xmm, xmm, m128, imm8
vpermil2ps xmm, xmm, xmm, xmm, imm8

vpermilpd.description: Picks each double from the two doubles of its own 128-bit lane, using a bit of imm8 or bit 1 of the matching element in a control vector. Does not cross lanes.

vpermilps.description: Picks each float from the four floats of its own 128-bit lane, using 2-bit fields of imm8 or the low two bits of the matching element in a control vector. Does not cross lanes.

vpermpd.description: With imm8, picks each of four doubles from any position of the source (per 256 bits in zmm). The EVEX register form takes an index vector as the second operand and permutes across the whole vector.

vpermps.description: Fills each float of the destination with the float of the third operand chosen by the index in the second operand, across the whole vector. EVEX adds 512 bits and masking.

vpermq.description: With imm8, picks each of four quadwords from any position of the source (per 256 bits in zmm). The EVEX register form takes an index vector as the second operand and permutes across the whole vector.

vpermt2b.description: Uses the second operand as indices into a combined table made of the destination and the third operand; the top index bit picks the table. The destination table is overwritten with the result.
vpermt2b.operation: dst.b[i] = (idx[log2 n] ? b : dst).b[idx & (n-1)], idx = a.b[i]

vpermt2d.description: Uses the second operand as indices into a combined table of the destination and the third operand, writing the selected 32-bit elements over the first table.
vpermt2d.operation: dst.d[i] = (idx[log2 n] ? b : dst).d[idx & (n-1)], idx = a.d[i]

vpermt2pd.description: Uses the second operand as indices into a combined table of the destination and the third operand, writing the selected doubles over the first table. Supports masking and broadcast.
vpermt2pd.operation: dst.q[i] = (idx[log2 n] ? b : dst).q[idx & (n-1)], idx = a.q[i]

vpermt2ps.description: Uses the second operand as indices into a combined table of the destination and the third operand, writing the selected floats over the first table. Supports masking and broadcast.
vpermt2ps.operation: dst.d[i] = (idx[log2 n] ? b : dst).d[idx & (n-1)], idx = a.d[i]

vpermt2q.description: Uses the second operand as indices into a combined table of the destination and the third operand, writing the selected 64-bit elements over the first table.
vpermt2q.operation: dst.q[i] = (idx[log2 n] ? b : dst).q[idx & (n-1)], idx = a.q[i]

vpermt2w.description: Uses the second operand as indices into a combined table of the destination and the third operand, writing the selected 16-bit elements over the first table.
vpermt2w.operation: dst.w[i] = (idx[log2 n] ? b : dst).w[idx & (n-1)], idx = a.w[i]

vpermw.description: Fills each 16-bit element with the element of the third operand chosen by the index in the second operand, across the whole vector. Supports masking.

vpexpandb.description: Reads consecutive bytes from the start of the source (register or memory) and places them, in order, into the destination positions whose k mask bits are set; other positions are merged or zeroed.
vpexpandb.operation: j = 0; for i: if k[i] { dst.b[i] = src.b[j++] }

vpexpandd.description: Reads consecutive 32-bit elements from the start of the source and places them, in order, into destination positions whose k mask bits are set. The reverse of vpcompressd.
vpexpandd.operation: j = 0; for i: if k[i] { dst.d[i] = src.d[j++] }

vpexpandq.description: Reads consecutive 64-bit elements from the start of the source and places them, in order, into destination positions whose k mask bits are set. The reverse of vpcompressq.
vpexpandq.operation: j = 0; for i: if k[i] { dst.q[i] = src.q[j++] }

vpexpandw.description: Reads consecutive 16-bit elements from the start of the source and places them, in order, into destination positions whose k mask bits are set. The reverse of vpcompressw.
vpexpandw.operation: j = 0; for i: if k[i] { dst.w[i] = src.w[j++] }

vpextrb.description: Copies the byte of an xmm register selected by imm8 to memory or to a general register, where it is zero-extended.

vpextrd.description: Copies the 32-bit element of an xmm register selected by imm8 to memory or a general register.

vpextrq.description: Copies the low or high 64-bit half of an xmm register, chosen by imm8 bit 0, to memory or a 64-bit general register.

vpextrw.description: Copies the 16-bit element of an xmm register selected by imm8 to memory or to a general register, where it is zero-extended. Two encodings exist; only one can store to memory.

vpgatherdd.description: Loads 32-bit elements from base + index*scale for each 32-bit index in a vector. The VEX form uses a vector mask (third operand) and clears it as elements arrive; the EVEX form uses and clears a k mask.

vpgatherdq.description: Loads 64-bit elements from base + index*scale, using 32-bit indices, so the index vector is half the width of the data. The mask is cleared element by element as loads complete.

vpgatherqd.description: Loads 32-bit elements from base + index*scale, using 64-bit indices, so the result is half the width of the index vector. The mask is cleared element by element as loads complete.

vpgatherqq.description: Loads 64-bit elements from base + index*scale for each 64-bit index in a vector. Useful for following arrays of pointers or offsets; the mask is cleared as loads complete.

vphaddbd.summary: Horizontal add signed bytes to doublewords (XOP)
vphaddbd.description: AMD XOP: sums each group of four adjacent signed bytes and writes the result as a sign-extended 32-bit element.

vphaddbq.summary: Horizontal add signed bytes to quadwords (XOP)
vphaddbq.description: AMD XOP: sums each group of eight adjacent signed bytes and writes the result as a sign-extended 64-bit element.

vphaddbw.summary: Horizontal add signed bytes to words (XOP)
vphaddbw.description: AMD XOP: adds each pair of adjacent signed bytes and writes the sum as a sign-extended 16-bit element.

vphaddd.description: Adds adjacent pairs of 32-bit elements. In each 128-bit lane the low half of the result comes from the second operand's pairs and the high half from the third's; wraps on overflow.

vphadddq.summary: Horizontal add signed doublewords to quadwords (XOP)
vphadddq.description: AMD XOP: adds each pair of adjacent signed 32-bit elements and writes the sum as a sign-extended 64-bit element.

vphaddsw.summary: Horizontal add of word pairs with saturation
vphaddsw.description: Adds adjacent pairs of signed 16-bit elements with signed saturation. In each 128-bit lane the low half comes from the second operand and the high half from the third.
vphaddsw.operation: dst.lane.w = sat16(pairs of a), sat16(pairs of b)

vphaddubd.summary: Horizontal add unsigned bytes to doublewords (XOP)
vphaddubd.description: AMD XOP: sums each group of four adjacent unsigned bytes and writes the result as a zero-extended 32-bit element.

vphaddubq.summary: Horizontal add unsigned bytes to quadwords (XOP)
vphaddubq.description: AMD XOP: sums each group of eight adjacent unsigned bytes and writes the result as a zero-extended 64-bit element.

vphaddubw.summary: Horizontal add unsigned bytes to words (XOP)
vphaddubw.description: AMD XOP: adds each pair of adjacent unsigned bytes and writes the sum as a zero-extended 16-bit element.

vphaddudq.summary: Horizontal add unsigned doublewords to quadwords (XOP)
vphaddudq.description: AMD XOP: adds each pair of adjacent unsigned 32-bit elements and writes the sum as a zero-extended 64-bit element.

vphadduwd.summary: Horizontal add unsigned words to doublewords (XOP)
vphadduwd.description: AMD XOP: adds each pair of adjacent unsigned 16-bit elements and writes the sum as a zero-extended 32-bit element.

vphadduwq.summary: Horizontal add unsigned words to quadwords (XOP)
vphadduwq.description: AMD XOP: sums each group of four adjacent unsigned 16-bit elements and writes the result as a zero-extended 64-bit element.

vphaddw.description: Adds adjacent pairs of 16-bit elements, wrapping on overflow. In each 128-bit lane the low half of the result comes from the second operand and the high half from the third.
vphaddw.operation: dst.lane.w = pairs of a summed, pairs of b summed

vphaddwd.summary: Horizontal add signed words to doublewords (XOP)
vphaddwd.description: AMD XOP: adds each pair of adjacent signed 16-bit elements and writes the sum as a sign-extended 32-bit element.

vphaddwq.summary: Horizontal add signed words to quadwords (XOP)
vphaddwq.description: AMD XOP: sums each group of four adjacent signed 16-bit elements and writes the result as a sign-extended 64-bit element.

vphminposuw.summary: Minimum unsigned word and its position
vphminposuw.description: Finds the smallest of the eight unsigned words in the source, writes its value to word 0 of the destination and its index to bits 18:16, and clears every other bit. On a tie the lowest index wins.
vphminposuw.operation: dst[15:0] = min(src.w[i]); dst[18:16] = i; other bits = 0

vphsubbw.summary: Horizontal subtract signed bytes to words
vphsubbw.description: For each word of the source, subtracts its upper signed byte from its lower signed byte and writes the 16-bit difference to the matching word of the destination. An AMD XOP instruction.

vphsubd.description: Subtracts the second dword of each adjacent pair from the first. Differences from the first source fill the low half of each 128-bit lane of the destination, those from the second source the high half; results wrap around.
vphsubd.operation: per lane: dst = {a0-a1, a2-a3, b0-b1, b2-b3}

vphsubdq.summary: Horizontal subtract signed dwords to qwords
vphsubdq.description: For each qword of the source, subtracts its upper signed dword from its lower signed dword and writes the 64-bit difference to the matching qword of the destination. An AMD XOP instruction.

vphsubsw.summary: Horizontal subtract words with signed saturation
vphsubsw.description: Like vphsubw, subtracts the second signed word of each adjacent pair from the first, but clamps each difference to -32768..32767. Pairs of the first source go to the low half of each 128-bit lane, pairs of the second to the high half.
vphsubsw.operation: per lane: dst.w = sat16(a[2i] - a[2i+1]), then b pairs

vphsubw.description: Subtracts the second word of each adjacent pair from the first. Differences from the first source fill the low half of each 128-bit lane, those from the second source the high half; results wrap around.
vphsubw.operation: per lane: dst = {a0-a1, a2-a3, …, b0-b1, b2-b3, …}

vphsubwd.summary: Horizontal subtract signed words to dwords
vphsubwd.description: For each dword of the source, subtracts its upper signed word from its lower signed word and writes the 32-bit difference to the matching dword of the destination. An AMD XOP instruction.

vpinsrb.description: Copies the first source to the destination, then replaces the byte selected by the low 4 bits of imm8 with a byte from a general register or memory. Bits above 127 of the destination are cleared; the EVEX form needs AVX512BW.

vpinsrd.description: Copies the first source to the destination, then replaces the dword selected by the low 2 bits of imm8 with a dword from a general register or memory. Bits above 127 of the destination are cleared; the EVEX form needs AVX512DQ.

vpinsrq.description: Copies the first source to the destination, then replaces the qword selected by the lowest bit of imm8 with a qword from a general register or memory. Bits above 127 of the destination are cleared; the EVEX form needs AVX512DQ.

vpinsrw.description: Copies the first source to the destination, then replaces the word selected by the low 3 bits of imm8 with a word from a general register or memory. Bits above 127 of the destination are cleared; the EVEX form needs AVX512BW.

vplzcntd.summary: Count leading zeros in packed dwords
vplzcntd.description: Writes, for each 32-bit element, the number of zero bits above its highest set bit (32 for a zero element). Part of AVX-512CD; supports masking and a broadcast memory source.

vplzcntq.summary: Count leading zeros in packed qwords
vplzcntq.description: Writes, for each 64-bit element, the number of zero bits above its highest set bit (64 for a zero element). Part of AVX-512CD; supports masking and a broadcast memory source.

vpmacsdd.description: Multiplies corresponding signed dwords of the first two sources and adds the low 32 bits of each product to the matching dword of the third source, wrapping on overflow. An AMD XOP instruction; the fourth operand is the accumulator.

vpmacsdqh.summary: Multiply high dwords and add qwords
vpmacsdqh.description: Multiplies signed dwords 1 and 3 of the first two sources into 64-bit products and adds each to the matching qword of the third source, wrapping on overflow. An AMD XOP instruction; the fourth operand is the accumulator.

vpmacsdql.summary: Multiply low dwords and add qwords
vpmacsdql.description: Multiplies signed dwords 0 and 2 of the first two sources into 64-bit products and adds each to the matching qword of the third source, wrapping on overflow. An AMD XOP instruction; the fourth operand is the accumulator.

vpmacssdd.summary: Multiply and add packed dwords with saturation
vpmacssdd.description: Multiplies corresponding signed dwords of the first two sources, adds the matching dword of the third source and clamps the sum to the signed 32-bit range. An AMD XOP instruction; the fourth operand is the accumulator.

vpmacssdqh.summary: Multiply high dwords and add qwords with saturation
vpmacssdqh.description: Multiplies signed dwords 1 and 3 of the first two sources into 64-bit products and adds each to the matching qword of the third source, clamping the sum to the signed 64-bit range. An AMD XOP instruction; the fourth operand is the accumulator.

vpmacssdql.summary: Multiply low dwords and add qwords with saturation
vpmacssdql.description: Multiplies signed dwords 0 and 2 of the first two sources into 64-bit products and adds each to the matching qword of the third source, clamping the sum to the signed 64-bit range. An AMD XOP instruction; the fourth operand is the accumulator.

vpmacsswd.summary: Multiply odd words and add dwords with saturation
vpmacsswd.description: Multiplies the signed odd-numbered words (1, 3, 5, 7) of the first two sources, adds each 32-bit product to the matching dword of the third source and clamps the sum to the signed 32-bit range. An AMD XOP instruction; the fourth operand is the accumulator.

vpmacssww.summary: Multiply and add packed words with saturation
vpmacssww.description: Multiplies corresponding signed words of the first two sources, adds the matching word of the third source and clamps the result to -32768..32767. An AMD XOP instruction; the fourth operand is the accumulator.

vpmacswd.summary: Multiply odd words and add dwords
vpmacswd.description: Multiplies the signed odd-numbered words (1, 3, 5, 7) of the first two sources into 32-bit products and adds each to the matching dword of the third source, wrapping on overflow. An AMD XOP instruction; the fourth operand is the accumulator.

vpmacsww.description: Multiplies corresponding words of the first two sources and adds the low 16 bits of each product to the matching word of the third source, wrapping on overflow. An AMD XOP instruction; the fourth operand is the accumulator.

vpmadcsswd.summary: Multiply words, add pairs and accumulate, saturated
vpmadcsswd.description: Multiplies all eight pairs of signed words, adds each two adjacent products and the matching dword of the third source, and clamps the total to the signed 32-bit range. An AMD XOP instruction; the fourth operand is the accumulator.

vpmadcswd.summary: Multiply words, add pairs and accumulate
vpmadcswd.description: Multiplies all eight pairs of signed words, adds each two adjacent products together with the matching dword of the third source, wrapping on overflow. An AMD XOP instruction; the fourth operand is the accumulator.

vpmadd52huq.description: Multiplies the low 52 bits of each unsigned qword of the two sources into a 104-bit product and adds its upper 52 bits to the destination qword, which is the accumulator. Used in big-number arithmetic; VEX (AVX-IFMA) and EVEX forms.

vpmadd52luq.description: Multiplies the low 52 bits of each unsigned qword of the two sources into a 104-bit product and adds its lower 52 bits to the destination qword, which is the accumulator. Paired with vpmadd52huq in big-number code.

vpmaddubsw.summary: Multiply unsigned by signed bytes, add pairs
vpmaddubsw.description: Multiplies each unsigned byte of the first source by the matching signed byte of the second, adds adjacent pairs of the products and stores the sums as words with signed saturation. Common in 8-bit dot products and image filters.

vpmaddwd.summary: Multiply words and add adjacent pairs
vpmaddwd.description: Multiplies corresponding signed words and adds each adjacent pair of 32-bit products into a dword. The only overflow case, all four inputs equal to -32768, wraps to 0x80000000.

vpmaskmovd.summary: Masked load or store of dwords
vpmaskmovd.description: Moves only the dwords whose mask element has its top bit set. The load form (vpmaskmovd dst, mask, mem) zeroes the others; the store form (vpmaskmovd mem, mask, src) leaves other memory untouched. Masked-off elements never fault.
vpmaskmovd.operation: load: dst[i] = mask[i] < 0 ? mem[i] : 0; store: if (mask[i] < 0) mem[i] = src[i]

vpmaskmovq.summary: Masked load or store of qwords
vpmaskmovq.description: Moves only the qwords whose mask element has its top bit set. The load form (vpmaskmovq dst, mask, mem) zeroes the others; the store form (vpmaskmovq mem, mask, src) leaves other memory untouched. Masked-off elements never fault.
vpmaskmovq.operation: load: dst[i] = mask[i] < 0 ? mem[i] : 0; store: if (mask[i] < 0) mem[i] = src[i]

vpmaxsb.description: Writes the larger of each pair of signed bytes from the two sources to the destination. The EVEX form (AVX512BW) adds masking.

vpmaxsd.description: Writes the larger of each pair of signed dwords from the two sources to the destination. The EVEX form (AVX512F) adds masking and broadcast.

vpmaxsq.description: Writes the larger of each pair of signed qwords from the two sources to the destination. EVEX only (AVX512F), with masking and broadcast.

vpmaxsw.description: Writes the larger of each pair of signed words from the two sources to the destination. The EVEX form (AVX512BW) adds masking.

vpmaxub.description: Writes the larger of each pair of unsigned bytes from the two sources to the destination. The EVEX form (AVX512BW) adds masking.

vpmaxud.description: Writes the larger of each pair of unsigned dwords from the two sources to the destination. The EVEX form (AVX512F) adds masking and broadcast.

vpmaxuq.description: Writes the larger of each pair of unsigned qwords from the two sources to the destination. EVEX only (AVX512F), with masking and broadcast.

vpmaxuw.description: Writes the larger of each pair of unsigned words from the two sources to the destination. The EVEX form (AVX512BW) adds masking.

vpminsb.description: Writes the smaller of each pair of signed bytes from the two sources to the destination. The EVEX form (AVX512BW) adds masking.

vpminsd.description: Writes the smaller of each pair of signed dwords from the two sources to the destination. The EVEX form (AVX512F) adds masking and broadcast.

vpminsq.description: Writes the smaller of each pair of signed qwords from the two sources to the destination. EVEX only (AVX512F), with masking and broadcast.

vpminsw.description: Writes the smaller of each pair of signed words from the two sources to the destination. The EVEX form (AVX512BW) adds masking.

vpminub.description: Writes the smaller of each pair of unsigned bytes from the two sources to the destination. The EVEX form (AVX512BW) adds masking.

vpminud.description: Writes the smaller of each pair of unsigned dwords from the two sources to the destination. The EVEX form (AVX512F) adds masking and broadcast.

vpminuq.description: Writes the smaller of each pair of unsigned qwords from the two sources to the destination. EVEX only (AVX512F), with masking and broadcast.

vpminuw.description: Writes the smaller of each pair of unsigned words from the two sources to the destination. The EVEX form (AVX512BW) adds masking.

vpmovb2m.summary: Byte sign bits to mask register
vpmovb2m.description: Sets each bit of the mask register to the most significant bit of the matching byte of the vector and clears the mask bits beyond the element count. Needs AVX512BW.

vpmovd2m.summary: Dword sign bits to mask register
vpmovd2m.description: Sets each bit of the mask register to the most significant bit of the matching dword of the vector and clears the mask bits beyond the element count. Needs AVX512DQ.

vpmovdb.description: Narrows each dword to its low byte and packs the results into the low part of a vector register or into memory; with a memory destination and a mask only the selected elements are written. AVX512F.

vpmovdw.description: Narrows each dword to its low word and packs the results into the low part of a vector register or into memory; with a memory destination and a mask only the selected elements are written. AVX512F.

vpmovm2b.description: Sets each byte of the destination to all ones when the matching mask bit is 1 and to zero otherwise, turning a comparison mask back into lane masks. Needs AVX512BW.

vpmovm2d.description: Sets each dword of the destination to all ones when the matching mask bit is 1 and to zero otherwise, turning a comparison mask back into lane masks. Needs AVX512DQ.

vpmovm2q.description: Sets each qword of the destination to all ones when the matching mask bit is 1 and to zero otherwise, turning a comparison mask back into lane masks. Needs AVX512DQ.

vpmovm2w.description: Sets each word of the destination to all ones when the matching mask bit is 1 and to zero otherwise, turning a comparison mask back into lane masks. Needs AVX512BW.

vpmovmskb.summary: Byte sign mask to general register
vpmovmskb.description: Collects the most significant bit of every byte of the vector into a general-purpose register (16 bits for xmm, 32 for ymm) and zeroes the rest. Paired with vpcmpeqb in fast strlen, memchr and similar scans.

vpmovq2m.summary: Qword sign bits to mask register
vpmovq2m.description: Sets each bit of the mask register to the most significant bit of the matching qword of the vector and clears the mask bits beyond the element count. Needs AVX512DQ.

vpmovqb.description: Narrows each qword to its low byte and packs the results into the low part of a vector register or into memory; with a memory destination and a mask only the selected elements are written. AVX512F.

vpmovqd.description: Narrows each qword to its low dword and packs the results into the low part of a vector register or into memory; with a memory destination and a mask only the selected elements are written. AVX512F.

vpmovqw.description: Narrows each qword to its low word and packs the results into the low part of a vector register or into memory; with a memory destination and a mask only the selected elements are written. AVX512F.

vpmovsdb.summary: Narrow dwords to bytes with signed saturation
vpmovsdb.description: Converts each signed dword to a signed byte, clamping to -128..127, and packs the results into a vector register or memory. AVX512F; supports masking.

vpmovsdw.summary: Narrow dwords to words with signed saturation
vpmovsdw.description: Converts each signed dword to a signed word, clamping to -32768..32767, and packs the results into a vector register or memory. AVX512F; supports masking.

vpmovsqb.summary: Narrow qwords to bytes with signed saturation
vpmovsqb.description: Converts each signed qword to a signed byte, clamping to -128..127, and packs the results into a vector register or memory. AVX512F; supports masking.

vpmovsqd.summary: Narrow qwords to dwords with signed saturation
vpmovsqd.description: Converts each signed qword to a signed dword, clamping to the signed 32-bit range, and packs the results into a vector register or memory. AVX512F; supports masking.

vpmovsqw.summary: Narrow qwords to words with signed saturation
vpmovsqw.description: Converts each signed qword to a signed word, clamping to -32768..32767, and packs the results into a vector register or memory. AVX512F; supports masking.

vpmovswb.summary: Narrow words to bytes with signed saturation
vpmovswb.description: Converts each signed word to a signed byte, clamping to -128..127, and packs the results into a vector register or memory. AVX512BW; supports masking.

vpmovsxbd.description: Sign-extends the low 4 or 8 bytes of the source (xmm or ymm destination) to dword elements. The source may be memory of just the needed size; the EVEX form (AVX512F) adds masking and zmm.

vpmovsxbq.description: Sign-extends the low 2 or 4 bytes of the source (xmm or ymm destination) to qword elements. The source may be memory of just the needed size; the EVEX form (AVX512F) adds masking and zmm.

vpmovsxbw.description: Sign-extends the low 8 or 16 bytes of the source (xmm or ymm destination) to word elements. The source may be memory of just the needed size; the EVEX form (AVX512BW) adds masking and zmm.

vpmovsxdq.description: Sign-extends the low 2 or 4 dwords of the source (xmm or ymm destination) to qword elements. The source may be memory of just the needed size; the EVEX form (AVX512F) adds masking and zmm.

vpmovsxwd.description: Sign-extends the low 4 or 8 words of the source (xmm or ymm destination) to dword elements. The source may be memory of just the needed size; the EVEX form (AVX512F) adds masking and zmm.

vpmovsxwq.description: Sign-extends the low 2 or 4 words of the source (xmm or ymm destination) to qword elements. The source may be memory of just the needed size; the EVEX form (AVX512F) adds masking and zmm.

vpmovusdb.summary: Narrow dwords to bytes with unsigned saturation
vpmovusdb.description: Treats each dword as unsigned and converts it to a byte, clamping larger values to 255, then packs the results into a vector register or memory. AVX512F; supports masking.

vpmovusdw.summary: Narrow dwords to words with unsigned saturation
vpmovusdw.description: Treats each dword as unsigned and converts it to a word, clamping larger values to 65535, then packs the results into a vector register or memory. AVX512F; supports masking.

vpmovusqb.summary: Narrow qwords to bytes with unsigned saturation
vpmovusqb.description: Treats each qword as unsigned and converts it to a byte, clamping larger values to 255, then packs the results into a vector register or memory. AVX512F; supports masking.

vpmovusqd.summary: Narrow qwords to dwords with unsigned saturation
vpmovusqd.description: Treats each qword as unsigned and converts it to a dword, clamping larger values to 0xFFFFFFFF, then packs the results into a vector register or memory. AVX512F; supports masking.

vpmovusqw.summary: Narrow qwords to words with unsigned saturation
vpmovusqw.description: Treats each qword as unsigned and converts it to a word, clamping larger values to 65535, then packs the results into a vector register or memory. AVX512F; supports masking.

vpmovuswb.summary: Narrow words to bytes with unsigned saturation
vpmovuswb.description: Treats each word as unsigned and converts it to a byte, clamping larger values to 255, then packs the results into a vector register or memory. AVX512BW; supports masking.

vpmovw2m.summary: Word sign bits to mask register
vpmovw2m.description: Sets each bit of the mask register to the most significant bit of the matching word of the vector and clears the mask bits beyond the element count. Needs AVX512BW.

vpmovwb.description: Narrows each word to its low byte and packs the results into the low part of a vector register or into memory; with a memory destination and a mask only the selected elements are written. AVX512BW.

vpmovzxbd.description: Zero-extends the low 4 or 8 bytes of the source (xmm or ymm destination) to dword elements. The source may be memory of just the needed size; the EVEX form (AVX512F) adds masking and zmm.

vpmovzxbq.description: Zero-extends the low 2 or 4 bytes of the source (xmm or ymm destination) to qword elements. The source may be memory of just the needed size; the EVEX form (AVX512F) adds masking and zmm.

vpmovzxbw.description: Zero-extends the low 8 or 16 bytes of the source (xmm or ymm destination) to word elements. The source may be memory of just the needed size; the EVEX form (AVX512BW) adds masking and zmm.

vpmovzxdq.description: Zero-extends the low 2 or 4 dwords of the source (xmm or ymm destination) to qword elements. The source may be memory of just the needed size; the EVEX form (AVX512F) adds masking and zmm.

vpmovzxwd.description: Zero-extends the low 4 or 8 words of the source (xmm or ymm destination) to dword elements. The source may be memory of just the needed size; the EVEX form (AVX512F) adds masking and zmm.

vpmovzxwq.description: Zero-extends the low 2 or 4 words of the source (xmm or ymm destination) to qword elements. The source may be memory of just the needed size; the EVEX form (AVX512F) adds masking and zmm.

vpmuldq.summary: Multiply even signed dwords to qwords
vpmuldq.description: Multiplies the signed dwords at even positions (0, 2, …) of the two sources and writes each full 64-bit product to a qword; odd dwords are ignored. The EVEX form adds masking and broadcast.

vpmulhrsw.summary: Multiply words with rounding, keep high part
vpmulhrsw.description: Multiplies signed words, rounds the 32-bit product and keeps bits 30:15, which is a rounded Q15 fixed-point multiply. The one overflow case, -32768 times -32768, gives -32768.

vpmulhuw.summary: Multiply unsigned words, keep high half
vpmulhuw.description: Multiplies corresponding unsigned words and writes the upper 16 bits of each 32-bit product. Compilers use it for division of 16-bit values by a constant.

vpmulhw.summary: Multiply signed words, keep high half
vpmulhw.description: Multiplies corresponding signed words and writes the upper 16 bits of each 32-bit product. Together with vpmullw it yields full 32-bit products.

vpmulld.summary: Multiply packed dwords, keep low half
vpmulld.description: Multiplies corresponding dwords and keeps the low 32 bits of each product, which is the same for signed and unsigned inputs. Noticeably slower than other integer vector multiplies on many cores.

vpmullq.summary: Multiply packed qwords, keep low half
vpmullq.description: Multiplies corresponding qwords and keeps the low 64 bits of each product. Needs AVX512DQ; supports masking and broadcast.

vpmullw.summary: Multiply packed words, keep low half
vpmullw.description: Multiplies corresponding words and keeps the low 16 bits of each product, the same for signed and unsigned inputs. The EVEX form (AVX512BW) adds masking.

vpmultishiftqb.description: For each destination byte, takes the 8 bits that start at the bit offset given by the matching control byte of the first source (low 6 bits) from the corresponding qword of the second source, wrapping within the qword. AVX-512 VBMI; used for bit unpacking.

vpmuludq.summary: Multiply even unsigned dwords to qwords
vpmuludq.description: Multiplies the unsigned dwords at even positions (0, 2, …) of the two sources and writes each full 64-bit product to a qword; odd dwords are ignored. Compilers also use it to build 64-bit multiplies.

vpopcntb.summary: Count set bits in packed bytes
vpopcntb.description: Writes the number of one bits in each 8-bit element of the source to the matching element of the destination. Needs AVX-512 BITALG; supports masking.

vpopcntd.summary: Count set bits in packed dwords
vpopcntd.description: Writes the number of one bits in each 32-bit element of the source to the matching element of the destination. Needs AVX512_VPOPCNTDQ; supports masking and broadcast.

vpopcntq.summary: Count set bits in packed qwords
vpopcntq.description: Writes the number of one bits in each 64-bit element of the source to the matching element of the destination. Needs AVX512_VPOPCNTDQ; supports masking and broadcast.

vpopcntw.summary: Count set bits in packed words
vpopcntw.description: Writes the number of one bits in each 16-bit element of the source to the matching element of the destination. Needs AVX-512 BITALG; supports masking.

vpor.description: Combines the two sources with a bitwise OR into the destination, xmm or ymm. The AVX-512 counterparts with masking are vpord and vporq.

vpord.description: Combines the sources with a bitwise OR. The d suffix only sets the 32-bit element size for masking and for broadcasting a 32-bit memory operand. EVEX only (AVX512F).

vporq.description: Combines the sources with a bitwise OR. The q suffix only sets the 64-bit element size for masking and for broadcasting a 64-bit memory operand. EVEX only (AVX512F).

vpperm.description: Builds each destination byte from any of the 32 bytes of the first two sources, picked by the low 5 bits of the matching selector byte in the third source; the top 3 selector bits can also invert, bit-reverse, zero, set or sign-fill it. AMD XOP.

vprold.summary: Rotate packed dwords left by immediate
vprold.description: Rotates each 32-bit element of the source left by imm8 modulo 32. AVX512F; supports masking and a broadcast memory source.

vprolq.summary: Rotate packed qwords left by immediate
vprolq.description: Rotates each 64-bit element of the source left by imm8 modulo 64. AVX512F; supports masking and a broadcast memory source.

vprolvd.summary: Rotate packed dwords left by variable counts
vprolvd.description: Rotates each 32-bit element of the first source left by the count in the matching element of the second source, taken modulo 32. AVX512F; supports masking and broadcast.

vprolvq.summary: Rotate packed qwords left by variable counts
vprolvq.description: Rotates each 64-bit element of the first source left by the count in the matching element of the second source, taken modulo 64. AVX512F; supports masking and broadcast.

vprord.summary: Rotate packed dwords right by immediate
vprord.description: Rotates each 32-bit element of the source right by imm8 modulo 32. AVX512F; supports masking and a broadcast memory source.

vprorq.summary: Rotate packed qwords right by immediate
vprorq.description: Rotates each 64-bit element of the source right by imm8 modulo 64. AVX512F; supports masking and a broadcast memory source.

vprorvd.summary: Rotate packed dwords right by variable counts
vprorvd.description: Rotates each 32-bit element of the first source right by the count in the matching element of the second source, taken modulo 32. AVX512F; supports masking and broadcast.

vprorvq.summary: Rotate packed qwords right by variable counts
vprorvq.description: Rotates each 64-bit element of the first source right by the count in the matching element of the second source, taken modulo 64. AVX512F; supports masking and broadcast.

vprotb.description: Rotates each byte of the data operand by an immediate or by the signed count in the matching byte of a count vector: positive counts rotate left, negative ones right. An AMD XOP instruction.

vprotd.description: Rotates each dword of the data operand by an immediate or by the signed count in the matching dword of a count vector: positive counts rotate left, negative ones right. An AMD XOP instruction.

vprotq.description: Rotates each qword of the data operand by an immediate or by the signed count in the matching qword of a count vector: positive counts rotate left, negative ones right. An AMD XOP instruction.

vprotw.description: Rotates each word of the data operand by an immediate or by the signed count in the matching word of a count vector: positive counts rotate left, negative ones right. An AMD XOP instruction.

vpsadbw.description: Takes the absolute differences of unsigned bytes in each 8-byte group and sums them into the low 16 bits of the matching qword, clearing the rest. Used in motion estimation and, against zero, to sum bytes quickly.

vpscatterdd.description: Stores each dword whose mask bit is set to base + dword index × scale, clearing that mask bit; the mask is zero once all stores are done. Overlapping addresses are written from the lowest element up. AVX512F.
vpscatterdd.operation: for each i with k[i]: [base + idx.d[i]*scale] = src.d[i]; k[i] = 0

vpscatterdq.description: Stores each qword whose mask bit is set to base + dword index × scale, clearing that mask bit; the mask is zero once all stores are done. Overlapping addresses are written from the lowest element up. AVX512F.
vpscatterdq.operation: for each i with k[i]: [base + idx.d[i]*scale] = src.q[i]; k[i] = 0

vpscatterqd.description: Stores each dword whose mask bit is set to base + qword index × scale, clearing that mask bit; the mask is zero once all stores are done. Overlapping addresses are written from the lowest element up. AVX512F.
vpscatterqd.operation: for each i with k[i]: [base + idx.q[i]*scale] = src.d[i]; k[i] = 0

vpscatterqq.description: Stores each qword whose mask bit is set to base + qword index × scale, clearing that mask bit; the mask is zero once all stores are done. Overlapping addresses are written from the lowest element up. AVX512F.
vpscatterqq.operation: for each i with k[i]: [base + idx.q[i]*scale] = src.q[i]; k[i] = 0

vpshab.summary: Arithmetic shift of packed bytes by signed counts
vpshab.description: Shifts each signed byte of the data operand by the signed count in the matching byte of the count operand: positive counts shift left, negative ones shift right copying the sign bit. An AMD XOP instruction.

vpshad.summary: Arithmetic shift of packed dwords by signed counts
vpshad.description: Shifts each signed dword of the data operand by the signed count in the matching dword of the count operand: positive counts shift left, negative ones shift right copying the sign bit. An AMD XOP instruction.

vpshaq.summary: Arithmetic shift of packed qwords by signed counts
vpshaq.description: Shifts each signed qword of the data operand by the signed count in the matching qword of the count operand: positive counts shift left, negative ones shift right copying the sign bit. An AMD XOP instruction.

vpshaw.summary: Arithmetic shift of packed words by signed counts
vpshaw.description: Shifts each signed word of the data operand by the signed count in the matching word of the count operand: positive counts shift left, negative ones shift right copying the sign bit. An AMD XOP instruction.

vpshlb.summary: Logical shift of packed bytes by signed counts
vpshlb.description: Shifts each byte of the data operand by the signed count in the matching byte of the count operand: positive counts shift left, negative ones shift right filling with zeros. An AMD XOP instruction.

vpshld.summary: Logical shift of packed dwords by signed counts
vpshld.description: Shifts each dword of the data operand by the signed count in the matching dword of the count operand: positive counts shift left, negative ones shift right filling with zeros. An AMD XOP instruction, not the AVX-512 vpshldd.

vpshldd.description: For each 32-bit element, joins the first source (upper half) with the second (lower half), shifts the pair left by imm8 modulo 32 and keeps the upper half: a funnel shift. AVX-512 VBMI2; supports masking and broadcast.

vpshldq.description: For each 64-bit element, joins the first source (upper half) with the second (lower half), shifts the pair left by imm8 modulo 64 and keeps the upper half: a funnel shift. AVX-512 VBMI2; supports masking and broadcast.

vpshldvd.summary: Concatenate and shift dwords left by variable counts
vpshldvd.description: For each 32-bit element, joins the destination (upper half) with the first source (lower half), shifts left by the matching count of the second source modulo 32 and writes the upper half back to the destination. AVX-512 VBMI2.

vpshldvq.summary: Concatenate and shift qwords left by variable counts
vpshldvq.description: For each 64-bit element, joins the destination (upper half) with the first source (lower half), shifts left by the matching count of the second source modulo 64 and writes the upper half back to the destination. AVX-512 VBMI2.

vpshldvw.summary: Concatenate and shift words left by variable counts
vpshldvw.description: For each 16-bit element, joins the destination (upper half) with the first source (lower half), shifts left by the matching count of the second source modulo 16 and writes the upper half back to the destination. AVX-512 VBMI2.

vpshldw.description: For each 16-bit element, joins the first source (upper half) with the second (lower half), shifts the pair left by imm8 modulo 16 and keeps the upper half: a funnel shift. AVX-512 VBMI2; supports masking.

vpshlq.summary: Logical shift of packed qwords by signed counts
vpshlq.description: Shifts each qword of the data operand by the signed count in the matching qword of the count operand: positive counts shift left, negative ones shift right filling with zeros. An AMD XOP instruction.

vpshlw.summary: Logical shift of packed words by signed counts
vpshlw.description: Shifts each word of the data operand by the signed count in the matching word of the count operand: positive counts shift left, negative ones shift right filling with zeros. An AMD XOP instruction.

vpshrdd.description: For each 32-bit element, joins the second source (upper half) with the first (lower half), shifts the pair right by imm8 modulo 32 and keeps the lower half: a funnel shift. AVX-512 VBMI2; supports masking and broadcast.

vpshrdq.description: For each 64-bit element, joins the second source (upper half) with the first (lower half), shifts the pair right by imm8 modulo 64 and keeps the lower half: a funnel shift. AVX-512 VBMI2; supports masking and broadcast.

vpshrdvd.summary: Concatenate and shift dwords right by variable counts
vpshrdvd.description: For each 32-bit element, joins the first source (upper half) with the destination (lower half), shifts right by the matching count of the second source modulo 32 and writes the lower half back to the destination. AVX-512 VBMI2.

vpshrdvq.summary: Concatenate and shift qwords right by variable counts
vpshrdvq.description: For each 64-bit element, joins the first source (upper half) with the destination (lower half), shifts right by the matching count of the second source modulo 64 and writes the lower half back to the destination. AVX-512 VBMI2.

vpshrdvw.summary: Concatenate and shift words right by variable counts
vpshrdvw.description: For each 16-bit element, joins the first source (upper half) with the destination (lower half), shifts right by the matching count of the second source modulo 16 and writes the lower half back to the destination. AVX-512 VBMI2.

vpshrdw.description: For each 16-bit element, joins the second source (upper half) with the first (lower half), shifts the pair right by imm8 modulo 16 and keeps the lower half: a funnel shift. AVX-512 VBMI2; supports masking.

vpshufb.description: Picks each destination byte from the first source, indexed by the low 4 bits of the matching control byte of the second source within the same 128-bit lane; a control byte with bit 7 set gives zero. The workhorse of table lookups and byte reordering.

vpshufbitqmb.summary: Gather bits into a mask register
vpshufbitqmb.description: For each control byte of the second source, takes the bit at that position (modulo 64) of the matching qword of the first source and writes it to the corresponding bit of the mask register. AVX-512 BITALG.

vpshufd.description: Rearranges the four dwords inside each 128-bit lane of the source using the 2-bit selectors of imm8, without touching the source. Often used to broadcast one element or swap halves.

vpshufhw.description: Reorders the four upper words of each 128-bit lane using the 2-bit fields of imm8 and copies the four lower words unchanged. The EVEX form (AVX512BW) adds masking.

vpshuflw.description: Reorders the four lower words of each 128-bit lane using the 2-bit fields of imm8 and copies the four upper words unchanged. The EVEX form (AVX512BW) adds masking.

vpsignb.description: Negates, zeroes or keeps each signed byte of the first source when the matching byte of the second source is negative, zero or positive. Negating -128 leaves it unchanged. VEX only.

vpsignd.description: Negates, zeroes or keeps each signed dword of the first source when the matching dword of the second source is negative, zero or positive. Negating -2^31 leaves it unchanged. VEX only.

vpsignw.description: Negates, zeroes or keeps each signed word of the first source when the matching word of the second source is negative, zero or positive. Negating -32768 leaves it unchanged. VEX only.

vpslld.description: Shifts every 32-bit element left by one count, taken from imm8 or the low 64 bits of an xmm operand, filling with zeros; counts above 31 clear the elements. EVEX forms (AVX512F) add masking.

vpslldq.description: Shifts each 128-bit lane of the source left by imm8 bytes, filling with zero bytes; counts above 15 clear the lane. The count is in bytes, not bits, and nothing crosses between lanes.

vpsllq.description: Shifts every 64-bit element left by one count, taken from imm8 or the low 64 bits of an xmm operand, filling with zeros; counts above 63 clear the elements. EVEX forms (AVX512F) add masking.

vpsllvd.summary: Shift packed dwords left by variable counts
vpsllvd.description: Shifts each 32-bit element of the first source left by the unsigned count in the matching element of the second source; counts above 31 give zero. AVX2, plus EVEX forms in AVX512F.

vpsllvq.summary: Shift packed qwords left by variable counts
vpsllvq.description: Shifts each 64-bit element of the first source left by the unsigned count in the matching element of the second source; counts above 63 give zero. AVX2, plus EVEX forms in AVX512F.

vpsllvw.summary: Shift packed words left by variable counts
vpsllvw.description: Shifts each 16-bit element of the first source left by the unsigned count in the matching element of the second source; counts above 15 give zero. AVX512BW, EVEX only.

vpsllw.description: Shifts every 16-bit element left by one count, taken from imm8 or the low 64 bits of an xmm operand, filling with zeros; counts above 15 clear the elements. EVEX forms (AVX512BW) add masking.

vpsrad.description: Shifts every signed 32-bit element right by one count, taken from imm8 or the low 64 bits of an xmm operand, copying the sign bit; counts above 31 fill elements with the sign. EVEX forms (AVX512F) add masking.

vpsraq.description: Shifts every signed 64-bit element right by one count, taken from imm8 or the low 64 bits of an xmm operand, copying the sign bit; counts above 63 fill elements with the sign. AVX512F only; there is no VEX form.

vpsravd.summary: Shift packed dwords right arithmetically by variable counts
vpsravd.description: Shifts each signed 32-bit element of the first source right by the unsigned count in the matching element of the second source, copying the sign bit; counts above 31 fill with the sign. AVX2, plus EVEX forms in AVX512F.

vpsravq.summary: Shift packed qwords right arithmetically by variable counts
vpsravq.description: Shifts each signed 64-bit element of the first source right by the unsigned count in the matching element of the second source, copying the sign bit; counts above 63 fill with the sign. AVX512F, EVEX only.

vpsravw.summary: Shift packed words right arithmetically by variable counts
vpsravw.description: Shifts each signed 16-bit element of the first source right by the unsigned count in the matching element of the second source, copying the sign bit; counts above 15 fill with the sign. AVX512BW, EVEX only.

vpsraw.description: Shifts every signed 16-bit element right by one count, taken from imm8 or the low 64 bits of an xmm operand, copying the sign bit; counts above 15 fill elements with the sign. EVEX forms (AVX512BW) add masking.

vpsrld.description: Shifts every 32-bit element right by one count, taken from imm8 or the low 64 bits of an xmm operand, filling with zeros; counts above 31 clear the elements. EVEX forms (AVX512F) add masking.

vpsrldq.description: Shifts each 128-bit lane of the source right by imm8 bytes, filling with zero bytes; counts above 15 clear the lane. The count is in bytes, not bits, and nothing crosses between lanes.

vpsrlq.description: Shifts every 64-bit element right by one count, taken from imm8 or the low 64 bits of an xmm operand, filling with zeros; counts above 63 clear the elements. EVEX forms (AVX512F) add masking.

vpsrlvd.summary: Shift packed dwords right logically by variable counts
vpsrlvd.description: Shifts each 32-bit element of the first source right by the unsigned count in the matching element of the second source, filling with zeros; counts above 31 give zero. AVX2, plus EVEX forms in AVX512F.

vpsrlvq.summary: Shift packed qwords right logically by variable counts
vpsrlvq.description: Shifts each 64-bit element of the first source right by the unsigned count in the matching element of the second source, filling with zeros; counts above 63 give zero. AVX2, plus EVEX forms in AVX512F.

vpsrlvw.summary: Shift packed words right logically by variable counts
vpsrlvw.description: Shifts each 16-bit element of the first source right by the unsigned count in the matching element of the second source, filling with zeros; counts above 15 give zero. AVX512BW, EVEX only.

vpsrlw.description: Shifts every 16-bit element right by one count, taken from imm8 or the low 64 bits of an xmm operand, filling with zeros; counts above 15 clear the elements. EVEX forms (AVX512BW) add masking.
