vpsubb.description: Subtracts each byte of the second source from the matching byte of the first, wrapping on overflow; the same for signed and unsigned values. The EVEX form (AVX512BW) adds masking.

vpsubd.description: Subtracts each dword of the second source from the matching dword of the first, wrapping on overflow; the same for signed and unsigned values. The EVEX form (AVX512F) adds masking and broadcast.

vpsubq.description: Subtracts each qword of the second source from the matching qword of the first, wrapping on overflow; the same for signed and unsigned values. The EVEX form (AVX512F) adds masking and broadcast.

vpsubsb.summary: Subtract packed signed bytes with saturation
vpsubsb.description: Subtracts each signed byte of the second source from the matching one of the first and clamps the result to -128..127 instead of wrapping. The EVEX form (AVX512BW) adds masking.

vpsubsw.summary: Subtract packed signed words with saturation
vpsubsw.description: Subtracts each signed word of the second source from the matching one of the first and clamps the result to -32768..32767 instead of wrapping. The EVEX form (AVX512BW) adds masking.

vpsubusb.summary: Subtract packed unsigned bytes with saturation
vpsubusb.description: Subtracts each unsigned byte of the second source from the matching one of the first; results that would go below zero become 0. The EVEX form (AVX512BW) adds masking.

vpsubusw.summary: Subtract packed unsigned words with saturation
vpsubusw.description: Subtracts each unsigned word of the second source from the matching one of the first; results that would go below zero become 0. The EVEX form (AVX512BW) adds masking.

vpsubw.description: Subtracts each word of the second source from the matching word of the first, wrapping on overflow; the same for signed and unsigned values. The EVEX form (AVX512BW) adds masking.

vpternlogd.description: Computes any three-input bitwise function: for every bit, the bits of the destination, first and second source form a 3-bit index into the imm8 truth table. Compilers use it for bit select, three-way XOR, NOT and all-ones; d sets 32-bit masking.

vpternlogq.description: Computes any three-input bitwise function: for every bit, the bits of the destination, first and second source form a 3-bit index into the imm8 truth table. Compilers use it for bit select, three-way XOR, NOT and all-ones; q sets 64-bit masking.

vptest.summary: Vector bitwise test and set flags
vptest.description: Sets ZF when the AND of the two operands is all zeros and CF when the second operand ANDed with the inverse of the first is all zeros; AF, OF, PF and SF are cleared. Nothing else is written; a jz or jc usually follows.

vptestmb.description: Sets each mask bit when the AND of the matching bytes of the two sources is nonzero, otherwise clears it. With the same register twice it marks the nonzero bytes. Needs AVX512BW; can itself be masked.

vptestmd.description: Sets each mask bit when the AND of the matching dwords of the two sources is nonzero, otherwise clears it. With the same register twice it marks the nonzero dwords. Needs AVX512F; can itself be masked.

vptestmq.description: ANDs each 64-bit element of the two sources and sets the matching bit of the destination mask register when the result is non-zero. A write mask in {k} limits which bits can become 1; the rest are cleared.

vptestmw.description: ANDs each 16-bit element of the two sources and sets the matching mask bit when the result is non-zero. Bits outside the write mask {k} are cleared. Requires AVX512BW.

vptestnmb.summary: Test bytes for zero into a mask
vptestnmb.description: ANDs each byte of the two sources and sets the matching mask bit when the result is zero — the inverse of vptestmb. With the same register twice it finds zero bytes, as in strlen-style loops.

vptestnmd.summary: Test dwords for zero into a mask
vptestnmd.description: ANDs each 32-bit element of the two sources and sets the matching mask bit when the result is zero. Bits outside the write mask {k} are cleared.

vptestnmq.summary: Test qwords for zero into a mask
vptestnmq.description: ANDs each 64-bit element of the two sources and sets the matching mask bit when the result is zero. Bits outside the write mask {k} are cleared.

vptestnmw.summary: Test words for zero into a mask
vptestnmw.description: ANDs each 16-bit element of the two sources and sets the matching mask bit when the result is zero. Bits outside the write mask {k} are cleared. Requires AVX512BW.

vpunpckhbw.description: Within each 128-bit lane, interleaves the upper eight bytes of the first source with the upper eight bytes of the second, starting with the first source. Often used with a zero register to widen bytes to words.
vpunpckhbw.operation: dst = {a.hi[0], b.hi[0], a.hi[1], b.hi[1], …} per lane

vpunpckhdq.description: Within each 128-bit lane, interleaves the upper two 32-bit elements of the first source with those of the second. The EVEX form supports masking and dword broadcast.
vpunpckhdq.operation: dst = {a[2], b[2], a[3], b[3]} per lane

vpunpckhqdq.description: Within each 128-bit lane, takes the upper 64-bit element of the first source and then the upper 64-bit element of the second. The EVEX form supports masking and qword broadcast.

vpunpckhwd.description: Within each 128-bit lane, interleaves the upper four 16-bit elements of the first source with those of the second. With a zero register it zero-extends words to dwords.
vpunpckhwd.operation: dst = {a[4], b[4], …, a[7], b[7]} per lane

vpunpcklbw.description: Within each 128-bit lane, interleaves the lower eight bytes of the first source with the lower eight bytes of the second, starting with the first source. A common way to widen bytes against a zero register.

vpunpckldq.description: Within each 128-bit lane, interleaves the lower two 32-bit elements of the first source with those of the second. The EVEX form supports masking and dword broadcast.
vpunpckldq.operation: dst = {a[0], b[0], a[1], b[1]} per lane

vpunpcklqdq.description: Within each 128-bit lane, takes the lower 64-bit element of the first source and then the lower 64-bit element of the second. Compilers use it to combine two 64-bit values into one register.

vpunpcklwd.description: Within each 128-bit lane, interleaves the lower four 16-bit elements of the first source with those of the second. With a zero register it zero-extends words to dwords.
vpunpcklwd.operation: dst = {a[0], b[0], …, a[3], b[3]} per lane

vpxor.description: XORs the two sources bit by bit into the destination, leaving both sources unchanged. vpxor of a register with itself is the usual way to zero it.

vpxord.description: EVEX XOR of two vectors, with the write mask and broadcast working on 32-bit elements. Masked-off elements are kept, or zeroed with {z}.

vpxorq.description: EVEX XOR of two vectors, with the write mask and broadcast working on 64-bit elements. Masked-off elements are kept, or zeroed with {z}.

vrangepd.description: For each double, picks the minimum, maximum, smaller magnitude or larger magnitude of the two sources (imm8 bits 1:0), then sets the sign from the first source, from the pick, positive or negative (bits 3:2).

vrangeps.description: For each float, picks the minimum, maximum, smaller magnitude or larger magnitude of the two sources (imm8 bits 1:0), then controls the sign of the result (bits 3:2). Supports masking and broadcast.

vrangesd.description: Applies the vrangepd selection to the low doubles of the two sources; the upper double of the destination is copied from the first source.
vrangesd.operation: dst[0] = range(imm8, a[0], b[0]); dst[1] = a[1]

vrangess.description: Applies the vrangeps selection to the low floats of the two sources; elements 1–3 of the destination are copied from the first source.

vrcp14pd.description: Computes an approximate 1/x for each double with relative error below 2^-14. Code that needs full precision follows it with a Newton-Raphson step.

vrcp14ps.description: Computes an approximate 1/x for each float with relative error below 2^-14, more accurate than vrcpps. Supports masking and broadcast.

vrcp14sd.description: Approximates 1/x of the low double of the second source with relative error below 2^-14; the upper double comes from the first source.

vrcp14ss.description: Approximates 1/x of the low float of the second source with relative error below 2^-14; elements 1–3 come from the first source.

vrcp28pd.description: Approximates 1/x for each double with relative error below 2^-28. Part of AVX-512 ER, found only on Xeon Phi processors.

vrcp28ps.description: Approximates 1/x for each float with relative error below 2^-28, close to a correctly rounded result. Part of AVX-512 ER (Xeon Phi only).

vrcp28sd.description: Approximates 1/x of the low double of the second source with relative error below 2^-28; the upper double comes from the first source. AVX-512 ER (Xeon Phi only).

vrcp28ss.description: Approximates 1/x of the low float of the second source with relative error below 2^-28; elements 1–3 come from the first source. AVX-512 ER (Xeon Phi only).

vrcpbf16.description: Computes an approximate 1/x for each bfloat16 element. An AVX10.2 instruction for machine-learning code; supports masking and broadcast.

vrcpph.description: Computes an approximate 1/x for each FP16 element, accurate to nearly the full half-precision mantissa. Supports masking and broadcast.

vrcpps.description: Computes a fast approximate 1/x for each float with relative error up to 1.5·2^-12. Results can differ slightly between CPU vendors, so it is not bit-reproducible.

vrcpsh.description: Approximates 1/x of the low FP16 element of the second source; the remaining elements of the low 128 bits come from the first source.

vrcpss.description: Approximates 1/x of the low float of the second source with relative error up to 1.5·2^-12; elements 1–3 come from the first source and bits above 127 are zeroed.

vreducebf16.description: For each bfloat16, subtracts the value rounded to M fraction bits (imm8 bits 7:4, rounding from bits 3:0), leaving the small remainder. Used for argument reduction in math functions.

vreducepd.description: For each double, subtracts the value rounded to M fraction bits (imm8 bits 7:4, rounding mode in bits 3:0), leaving the remainder. Useful for range reduction in exp/log/trig code.

vreduceph.description: For each FP16 element, subtracts the value rounded to M fraction bits (imm8 bits 7:4, rounding mode in bits 3:0), leaving the remainder.

vreduceps.description: For each float, subtracts the value rounded to M fraction bits (imm8 bits 7:4, rounding mode in bits 3:0), leaving the remainder. With M = 0 it yields the fractional part.

vreducesd.description: Applies the vreducepd operation to the low double of the second source; the upper double of the destination comes from the first source.

vreducesh.description: Applies the vreduceph operation to the low FP16 element of the second source; the other elements of the low 128 bits come from the first source.

vreducess.description: Applies the vreduceps operation to the low float of the second source; elements 1–3 of the destination come from the first source.

vrndscalebf16.description: Rounds each bfloat16 to M fraction bits, where M is imm8 bits 7:4 and the rounding mode is in bits 3:0. With M = 0 it rounds to an integral value.

vrndscalepd.description: Rounds each double to M fraction bits (imm8 bits 7:4) with the rounding mode in bits 3:0. With M = 0 it acts as floor, ceil, trunc or nearbyint, like vroundpd but with masking.

vrndscaleph.description: Rounds each FP16 element to M fraction bits (imm8 bits 7:4) with the rounding mode in bits 3:0. Supports masking and broadcast.

vrndscaleps.description: Rounds each float to M fraction bits (imm8 bits 7:4) with the rounding mode in bits 3:0. With M = 0 it is the AVX-512 replacement for vroundps (floor, ceil, trunc).

vrndscalesd.description: Rounds the low double of the second source to M fraction bits as set by imm8; the upper double comes from the first source.

vrndscalesh.description: Rounds the low FP16 element of the second source to M fraction bits as set by imm8; the other elements of the low 128 bits come from the first source.

vrndscaless.description: Rounds the low float of the second source to M fraction bits as set by imm8; elements 1–3 come from the first source.

vroundpd.description: Rounds each double to an integral value using the mode in imm8: nearest, down, up, toward zero, or the MXCSR mode. Compilers emit it for floor, ceil and trunc on vectors.

vroundps.description: Rounds each float to an integral value using the mode in imm8: nearest, down, up, toward zero, or the MXCSR mode. Bit 3 of imm8 suppresses the inexact exception.

vroundsd.description: Rounds the low double of the second source to an integral value in the imm8 mode; the upper double comes from the first source. Typical output for floor() or ceil() on a double.

vroundss.description: Rounds the low float of the second source to an integral value in the imm8 mode; elements 1–3 come from the first source. Typical output for floorf() or ceilf().

vrsqrt14pd.description: Computes an approximate 1/√x for each double with relative error below 2^-14. Usually refined with a Newton-Raphson step.

vrsqrt14ps.description: Computes an approximate 1/√x for each float with relative error below 2^-14. Used in graphics and physics code to normalise vectors quickly.

vrsqrt14sd.description: Approximates 1/√x of the low double of the second source with relative error below 2^-14; the upper double comes from the first source.

vrsqrt14ss.description: Approximates 1/√x of the low float of the second source with relative error below 2^-14; elements 1–3 come from the first source.

vrsqrt28pd.description: Approximates 1/√x for each double with relative error below 2^-28. Part of AVX-512 ER, available only on Xeon Phi.

vrsqrt28ps.description: Approximates 1/√x for each float with relative error below 2^-28. Part of AVX-512 ER, available only on Xeon Phi.

vrsqrt28sd.description: Approximates 1/√x of the low double of the second source with relative error below 2^-28; the upper double comes from the first source. AVX-512 ER (Xeon Phi only).

vrsqrt28ss.description: Approximates 1/√x of the low float of the second source with relative error below 2^-28; elements 1–3 come from the first source. AVX-512 ER (Xeon Phi only).

vrsqrtbf16.description: Computes an approximate 1/√x for each bfloat16 element. An AVX10.2 instruction aimed at normalisation layers in neural networks.

vrsqrtph.description: Computes an approximate 1/√x for each FP16 element. Supports masking and broadcast.

vrsqrtps.description: Computes a fast approximate 1/√x for each float with relative error up to 1.5·2^-12. Results are not guaranteed identical across CPU vendors.

vrsqrtsh.description: Approximates 1/√x of the low FP16 element of the second source; the other elements of the low 128 bits come from the first source.

vrsqrtss.description: Approximates 1/√x of the low float of the second source with relative error up to 1.5·2^-12; elements 1–3 come from the first source.

vscalefbf16.summary: Packed bfloat16 scale by power of two
vscalefbf16.description: Multiplies each bfloat16 of the first source by 2 raised to the floor of the matching element of the second source. An AVX10.2 instruction.

vscalefpd.summary: Packed double scale by power of two
vscalefpd.description: Multiplies each double of the first source by 2^floor(b) taken from the second source, like a vector ldexp that accepts floating-point exponents. Used with vgetexp in exp and log routines.

vscalefph.summary: Packed half-precision scale by power of two
vscalefph.description: Multiplies each FP16 element of the first source by 2^floor(b) taken from the second source. Supports masking, broadcast and embedded rounding.

vscalefps.summary: Packed single scale by power of two
vscalefps.description: Multiplies each float of the first source by 2^floor(b) taken from the second source. Supports masking, broadcast and embedded rounding.

vscalefsd.summary: Scalar double scale by power of two
vscalefsd.description: Multiplies the low double of the first source by 2^floor of the low double of the second; the upper double comes from the first source.

vscalefsh.summary: Scalar half-precision scale by power of two
vscalefsh.description: Multiplies the low FP16 element of the first source by 2^floor of the low element of the second; the other elements come from the first source.

vscalefss.summary: Scalar single scale by power of two
vscalefss.description: Multiplies the low float of the first source by 2^floor of the low float of the second; elements 1–3 come from the first source.

vscatterdpd.description: Stores each double of the source register to base + index[i]·scale, where the indices are 32-bit values in a vector register. Only elements enabled in the mask are written, and their mask bits are cleared as they complete.
vscatterdpd.operation: for i where k[i]: [base + idx32[i]·scale] = src[i]; k[i] = 0

vscatterdps.description: Stores each float of the source register to base + index[i]·scale using 32-bit vector indices. Only masked-in elements are written; overlapping addresses are written in element order, so the highest wins.
vscatterdps.operation: for i where k[i]: [base + idx32[i]·scale] = src[i]; k[i] = 0

vscatterpf0dpd.summary: Scatter prefetch doubles to L1, dword index
vscatterpf0dpd.description: Prefetches, with intent to write, the cache lines that a scatter of doubles with 32-bit indices would touch, into the L1 cache. Masked-in elements only. AVX-512 PF, Xeon Phi only.
vscatterpf0dpd.operation: for i where k[i]: prefetchw L1 [base + idx32[i]·scale]

vscatterpf0dps.summary: Scatter prefetch singles to L1, dword index
vscatterpf0dps.description: Prefetches, with intent to write, the cache lines that a scatter of floats with 32-bit indices would touch, into the L1 cache. AVX-512 PF, Xeon Phi only.
vscatterpf0dps.operation: for i where k[i]: prefetchw L1 [base + idx32[i]·scale]

vscatterpf0qpd.summary: Scatter prefetch doubles to L1, qword index
vscatterpf0qpd.description: Prefetches, with intent to write, the cache lines that a scatter of doubles with 64-bit indices would touch, into the L1 cache. AVX-512 PF, Xeon Phi only.
vscatterpf0qpd.operation: for i where k[i]: prefetchw L1 [base + idx64[i]·scale]

vscatterpf0qps.summary: Scatter prefetch singles to L1, qword index
vscatterpf0qps.description: Prefetches, with intent to write, the cache lines that a scatter of floats with 64-bit indices would touch, into the L1 cache. AVX-512 PF, Xeon Phi only.
vscatterpf0qps.operation: for i where k[i]: prefetchw L1 [base + idx64[i]·scale]

vscatterpf1dpd.summary: Scatter prefetch doubles to L2, dword index
vscatterpf1dpd.description: Prefetches, with intent to write, the cache lines that a scatter of doubles with 32-bit indices would touch, into the L2 cache. AVX-512 PF, Xeon Phi only.
vscatterpf1dpd.operation: for i where k[i]: prefetchw L2 [base + idx32[i]·scale]

vscatterpf1dps.summary: Scatter prefetch singles to L2, dword index
vscatterpf1dps.description: Prefetches, with intent to write, the cache lines that a scatter of floats with 32-bit indices would touch, into the L2 cache. AVX-512 PF, Xeon Phi only.
vscatterpf1dps.operation: for i where k[i]: prefetchw L2 [base + idx32[i]·scale]

vscatterpf1qpd.summary: Scatter prefetch doubles to L2, qword index
vscatterpf1qpd.description: Prefetches, with intent to write, the cache lines that a scatter of doubles with 64-bit indices would touch, into the L2 cache. AVX-512 PF, Xeon Phi only.
vscatterpf1qpd.operation: for i where k[i]: prefetchw L2 [base + idx64[i]·scale]

vscatterpf1qps.summary: Scatter prefetch singles to L2, qword index
vscatterpf1qps.description: Prefetches, with intent to write, the cache lines that a scatter of floats with 64-bit indices would touch, into the L2 cache. AVX-512 PF, Xeon Phi only.
vscatterpf1qps.operation: for i where k[i]: prefetchw L2 [base + idx64[i]·scale]

vscatterqpd.description: Stores each double of the source register to base + index[i]·scale, where the indices are 64-bit values in a vector register. Only masked-in elements are written, and their mask bits are cleared.
vscatterqpd.operation: for i where k[i]: [base + idx64[i]·scale] = src[i]; k[i] = 0

vscatterqps.description: Stores floats to base + index[i]·scale using 64-bit vector indices. Because the indices are twice as wide, the data register is half the width of the index register (zmm indices, ymm data).
vscatterqps.operation: for i where k[i]: [base + idx64[i]·scale] = src[i]; k[i] = 0

vsha512msg1.description: Performs the first part of the SHA-512 message-schedule update on four 64-bit words, adding the σ0 term of the next words taken from the xmm source. Pairs with vsha512msg2.

vsha512msg2.description: Finishes the SHA-512 message-schedule step for four 64-bit words by adding the σ1 terms of earlier words, producing the next four message words.

vsha512rnds2.description: Performs two rounds of SHA-512 compression on the state held in the two ymm operands, using two message-plus-constant qwords from the xmm source. The destination receives the updated half of the state.

vshuff32x4.description: Builds the destination from 128-bit blocks chosen by imm8: the lower half of the blocks comes from the first source and the upper half from the second. Masking and broadcast work on 32-bit elements.
vshuff32x4.operation: dst.lane[j] = (j < n/2 ? a : b).lane[imm8 field j]

vshuff64x2.description: Builds the destination from 128-bit blocks chosen by imm8: the lower half of the blocks comes from the first source and the upper half from the second. Masking and broadcast work on 64-bit elements.
vshuff64x2.operation: dst.lane[j] = (j < n/2 ? a : b).lane[imm8 field j]

vshufi32x4.description: Integer twin of vshuff32x4: picks 128-bit blocks by imm8, lower half from the first source and upper half from the second, with dword masking. With one register twice it rotates or broadcasts lanes.
vshufi32x4.operation: dst.lane[j] = (j < n/2 ? a : b).lane[imm8 field j]

vshufi64x2.description: Integer twin of vshuff64x2: picks 128-bit blocks by imm8, lower half from the first source and upper half from the second, with qword masking and broadcast.
vshufi64x2.operation: dst.lane[j] = (j < n/2 ? a : b).lane[imm8 field j]

vshufpd.description: In each 128-bit lane, the low result double is chosen from the first source and the high one from the second, each by one imm8 bit. Three-operand form; the EVEX version adds masking and broadcast.
vshufpd.operation: dst.lane[0] = a.lane[imm8 bit]; dst.lane[1] = b.lane[imm8 bit]

vshufps.description: In each 128-bit lane, the two low result floats are picked from the first source and the two high ones from the second, each by a 2-bit field of imm8. With the same register twice it acts as a general four-element shuffle.
vshufps.operation: dst = {a[imm8[1:0]], a[imm8[3:2]], b[imm8[5:4]], b[imm8[7:6]]} per lane

vsm3msg1.description: Computes an intermediate value for the SM3 hash message expansion from three registers of message words. Pairs with vsm3msg2; SM3 is the Chinese national hash standard.

vsm3msg2.description: Finishes the SM3 message expansion started by vsm3msg1, producing the next four 32-bit message words in the destination.

vsm3rnds2.description: Performs two rounds of SM3 compression on the hash state in the first two operands, using message words from the third; imm8 gives the round number, which selects the constants and boolean functions.

vsm4key4.description: Runs four rounds of the SM4 block cipher key schedule in each 128-bit lane, producing four round keys from the previous ones and the constants in the second source.

vsm4rnds4.description: Runs four rounds of SM4 encryption or decryption on the block in each 128-bit lane of the first source, using four round keys from the second source.

vsqrtbf16.description: Computes the square root of each bfloat16 element. An AVX10.2 instruction; supports masking and broadcast.

vsqrtpd.description: Computes the correctly rounded square root of each double. The EVEX form adds masking, broadcast and embedded rounding; negative inputs give NaN.

vsqrtph.description: Computes the square root of each FP16 element. Supports masking, broadcast and embedded rounding.

vsqrtps.description: Computes the correctly rounded square root of each float. The EVEX form adds masking, broadcast and embedded rounding.

vsqrtsd.description: Takes the square root of the low double of the second source; the upper double comes from the first source. Compilers emit it for sqrt(); a stale first source can create a false dependency.

vsqrtsh.description: Takes the square root of the low FP16 element of the second source; the other elements of the low 128 bits come from the first source.

vsqrtss.description: Takes the square root of the low float of the second source; elements 1–3 come from the first source. Compilers emit it for sqrtf().

vstmxcsr.description: Writes the 32-bit MXCSR register, which holds the SSE/AVX rounding mode, exception masks and sticky exception flags, to memory. VEX version of stmxcsr.

vsubbf16.description: Subtracts each bfloat16 of the second source from the matching element of the first. An AVX10.2 instruction; supports masking and broadcast.

vsubpd.description: Subtracts each double of the second source from the matching double of the first, without overwriting either source. The EVEX form adds masking, broadcast and embedded rounding.

vsubph.description: Subtracts each FP16 element of the second source from the matching element of the first. Supports masking, broadcast and embedded rounding.

vsubps.description: Subtracts each float of the second source from the matching float of the first, without overwriting either source. The EVEX form adds masking, broadcast and embedded rounding.

vsubsd.description: Subtracts the low double of the second source from the low double of the first; the upper double comes from the first source. The usual code for a - b on doubles under AVX.

vsubsh.description: Subtracts the low FP16 element of the second source from that of the first; the other elements of the low 128 bits come from the first source.

vsubss.description: Subtracts the low float of the second source from the low float of the first; elements 1–3 come from the first source. The usual code for a - b on floats under AVX.

vtestpd.summary: Test sign bits of packed doubles
vtestpd.description: Looks only at the sign bits of the doubles: ZF is set when a AND b has no sign bit set, CF when (NOT a) AND b has none. Other arithmetic flags are cleared; no register is written.

vtestps.summary: Test sign bits of packed singles
vtestps.description: Looks only at the sign bits of the floats: ZF is set when a AND b has no sign bit set, CF when (NOT a) AND b has none. Handy after a vector compare to branch on any or all lanes.

vucomisd.description: Compares the low doubles and sets ZF, PF and CF like an unsigned compare; a NaN operand sets all three. Signals invalid only for signalling NaNs. Followed by ja/jb/jp branches.
vucomisd.operation: ZF,PF,CF = cmp(a[0], b[0]); OF = SF = AF = 0

vucomish.description: Compares the low FP16 elements and sets ZF, PF and CF like an unsigned compare; a NaN operand sets all three. Signals invalid only for signalling NaNs.
vucomish.operation: ZF,PF,CF = cmp(a[0], b[0]); OF = SF = AF = 0

vucomiss.description: Compares the low floats and sets ZF, PF and CF like an unsigned compare; a NaN operand sets all three, so equality tests also check PF. Signals invalid only for signalling NaNs.
vucomiss.operation: ZF,PF,CF = cmp(a[0], b[0]); OF = SF = AF = 0

vucomxsd.summary: Unordered compare scalar doubles, new flags
vucomxsd.description: AVX10.2 variant of vucomisd that sets EFLAGS so a NaN operand no longer looks equal, letting a single conditional jump test equality or ordering without a separate parity check.

vucomxsh.summary: Unordered compare scalar FP16, new flags
vucomxsh.description: AVX10.2 variant of vucomish that sets EFLAGS so a NaN operand no longer looks equal, letting a single conditional jump test the result without a parity check.

vucomxss.summary: Unordered compare scalar singles, new flags
vucomxss.description: AVX10.2 variant of vucomiss that sets EFLAGS so a NaN operand no longer looks equal, letting a single conditional jump test equality or ordering without a parity check.

vunpckhpd.description: Within each 128-bit lane, takes the high double of the first source and then the high double of the second.

vunpckhps.description: Within each 128-bit lane, interleaves the upper two floats of the first source with the upper two floats of the second.
vunpckhps.operation: dst = {a[2], b[2], a[3], b[3]} per lane

vunpcklpd.description: Within each 128-bit lane, takes the low double of the first source and then the low double of the second. Often used to pack two scalar doubles into one register.

vunpcklps.description: Within each 128-bit lane, interleaves the lower two floats of the first source with the lower two floats of the second.
vunpcklps.operation: dst = {a[0], b[0], a[1], b[1]} per lane

vxorpd.description: XORs the two sources bit by bit. Compilers use it to zero a register (same register twice) or to flip the sign of doubles with a sign-bit mask.

vxorps.description: XORs the two sources bit by bit. vxorps of a register with itself is the standard zeroing idiom; with a sign mask it negates floats.

vzeroall.description: Clears ymm0–ymm15 entirely (ymm0–ymm7 in 32-bit mode), including the upper parts of the matching zmm registers. zmm16–31 are left alone.

vzeroupper.summary: Zero upper halves of vector registers
vzeroupper.description: Clears bits 128 and above of ymm0–ymm15 and zmm0–zmm15. Compilers place it before calls and returns from AVX code to avoid the slow mix of AVX and legacy SSE state.

wait.description: Also written fwait. Checks for unmasked x87 floating-point exceptions and raises them before continuing. Assemblers put it in front of fstsw, fsave and friends to form their waiting variants.

wbinvd.description: Writes all modified cache lines back to memory and then invalidates every cache. Privileged and very slow; used by firmware and kernels when changing memory types or powering down.

wbnoinvd.description: Writes all modified cache lines back to memory but keeps them valid, so later reads still hit. Privileged; used for persistent memory and memory-encryption key changes.

wrfsbase.description: Loads the FS segment base from a general register; the 32-bit form zero-extends. Usable in user mode only when the OS enables FSGSBASE; thread libraries use FS for thread-local storage.

wrgsbase.description: Loads the GS segment base from a general register; the 32-bit form zero-extends. Usable in user mode only when the OS enables FSGSBASE; kernels use GS for per-CPU data.

wrmsr.description: Writes EDX:EAX into the model-specific register numbered by ECX. Privileged (ring 0); an unknown MSR number raises #GP.

wrmsrlist.description: Writes several model-specific registers in one go: RSI points to a table of MSR numbers, RDI to a table of values, and each set bit of RCX selects an entry, cleared once written. Privileged.
wrmsrlist.operation: for i where rcx[i]: msr[[rsi+8i]] = [rdi+8i]; rcx[i] = 0

wrmsrns.description: Like wrmsr but does not serialize the pipeline, so it is cheaper for frequently written MSRs. The immediate form takes the MSR number from imm32 and the value from a 64-bit register. Privileged.
wrmsrns.operation: msr[ecx or imm32] = edx:eax or r64

wrpkru.description: Copies EAX into the PKRU register, which controls read and write access for each of the 16 memory protection keys in user mode. ECX and EDX must be zero.

wrssd.description: Stores a 32-bit register to a shadow-stack page, which ordinary stores cannot modify. Part of CET; allowed only when the OS enables shadow-stack writes for that privilege level.

wrssq.description: Stores a 64-bit register to a shadow-stack page, which ordinary stores cannot modify. Part of CET; allowed only when the OS enables shadow-stack writes.

wrussd.summary: Write dword to user shadow stack
wrussd.description: Kernel-mode store of a 32-bit register into a user shadow-stack page, used by the OS when setting up signal frames under CET. Privileged.

wrussq.summary: Write qword to user shadow stack
wrussq.description: Kernel-mode store of a 64-bit register into a user shadow-stack page, used by the OS when setting up signal frames under CET. Privileged.

xabort.description: Aborts the current RTM transaction, rolling back its effects and jumping to the xbegin fallback with the imm8 code in EAX bits 31:24. Outside a transaction it does nothing.

xadd.description: Adds the source to the destination and puts the old destination value into the source register. With lock it is an atomic fetch-and-add, used for counters and reference counts.
xadd.operation: tmp = dst; dst = dst + src; src = tmp

xbegin.description: Starts an RTM transaction. If it later aborts, all its changes are discarded and execution resumes at the relative fallback address with an abort status in EAX; on start EAX is left unchanged.
xbegin.operation: start_tx(fallback = rip + rel); on abort: eax = status, rip = fallback

xchg.description: Swaps the two operands. With a memory operand it is always atomic, as if locked, which makes it a common seq_cst store and spinlock primitive. xchg eax, eax in the 90 form is nop.
xchg.operation: tmp = a; a = b; b = tmp

xcryptcbc.description: VIA PadLock: with rep, encrypts or decrypts ECX blocks from [RSI] to [RDI] in CBC mode, using the control word at [RDX], key at [RBX] and IV at [RAX].

xcryptcfb.description: VIA PadLock: with rep, encrypts or decrypts ECX blocks from [RSI] to [RDI] in CFB mode, using the control word at [RDX], key at [RBX] and IV at [RAX].

xcryptctr.description: VIA PadLock: with rep, encrypts or decrypts ECX blocks from [RSI] to [RDI] in counter mode, using the control word at [RDX], key at [RBX] and counter block at [RAX].

xcryptecb.description: VIA PadLock: with rep, encrypts or decrypts ECX independent blocks from [RSI] to [RDI] in ECB mode, using the control word at [RDX] and the key at [RBX].

xcryptofb.description: VIA PadLock: with rep, encrypts or decrypts ECX blocks from [RSI] to [RDI] in OFB mode, using the control word at [RDX], key at [RBX] and IV at [RAX].

xend.description: Commits the current RTM transaction, making all its memory changes visible at once. Outside a transaction it raises #GP.

xgetbv.description: Reads the extended control register selected by ECX into EDX:EAX. With ECX = 0 it returns XCR0, which programs check to see whether the OS saves AVX or AVX-512 state.

xlatb.description: Replaces AL with the byte at [RBX + AL], treating AL as an unsigned index into a 256-byte table. A legacy instruction rarely emitted by modern compilers.

xor.description: XORs the source into the destination; CF and OF are cleared and SF, ZF, PF follow the result. xor eax, eax is the standard way to zero a register and also clears the upper 32 bits.

xorpd.description: XORs the second operand into the first, bit by bit. Compilers use it to zero an xmm register or to negate doubles with a sign-bit mask.

xorps.description: XORs the second operand into the first, bit by bit. xorps xmm0, xmm0 is the shortest way to zero an xmm register; with a sign mask it negates floats.

xresldtrk.description: Ends a region started by xsusldtrk inside a TSX transaction, so loads are again added to the transaction's read set and checked for conflicts.

xrstor.description: Reloads the state components selected by EDX:EAX and XCR0 (x87, SSE, AVX, AVX-512 and others) from an XSAVE area in memory. Kernels use it on context switches.

xrstor64.description: Same as xrstor, but with REX.W the x87 instruction and data pointers in the area are read as 64-bit values.

xrstors.description: Privileged restore from a compacted XSAVE area, covering supervisor state components (such as CET or PT state) as well as user ones.

xrstors64.description: Same as xrstors, but with REX.W the x87 instruction and data pointers are read as 64-bit values. Privileged.

xsave.description: Stores the state components selected by EDX:EAX and XCR0 to a 64-byte-aligned XSAVE area in the standard layout. Used by kernels and by dynamic linkers that preserve vector registers.

xsave64.description: Same as xsave, but with REX.W the x87 instruction and data pointers are stored as 64-bit values.

xsavec.description: Like xsave but writes only the requested components, packed together without gaps (compacted format), which saves space and time.

xsavec64.description: Same as xsavec, but with REX.W the x87 instruction and data pointers are stored as 64-bit values.

xsaveopt.description: Like xsave but may skip components that are in their initial state or unchanged since the last xrstor from the same area, reducing context-switch cost.

xsaveopt64.description: Same as xsaveopt, but with REX.W the x87 instruction and data pointers are stored as 64-bit values.

xsaves.description: Privileged save in the compacted format that also covers supervisor state components enabled in IA32_XSS, with the modified-only optimization of xsaveopt.

xsaves64.description: Same as xsaves, but with REX.W the x87 instruction and data pointers are stored as 64-bit values. Privileged.

xsetbv.description: Writes EDX:EAX into the extended control register selected by ECX, usually XCR0 to enable AVX or AVX-512 state saving. Privileged; done by the OS at boot.

xsha1.description: VIA PadLock: with rep, hashes ECX bytes at [RSI] with SHA-1, updating the hash state stored at [RDI].

xsha256.description: VIA PadLock: with rep, hashes ECX bytes at [RSI] with SHA-256, updating the hash state stored at [RDI].

xstore.description: VIA PadLock hardware random number generator: stores random bytes at [RDI], with EDX choosing the quality setting and EAX receiving the byte count and status. With rep it fills ECX bytes.

xsusldtrk.description: Inside a TSX transaction, stops adding loads to the read set until xresldtrk, so those loads cannot cause conflict aborts. Stores are still tracked as usual.

xtest.description: Clears ZF when executing inside an RTM or HLE transaction and sets it otherwise; CF, OF, SF, PF and AF are cleared. Lock-elision libraries use it to choose a code path.
xtest.operation: ZF = !in_transaction; CF = OF = SF = PF = AF = 0
